23/// Build the complete harness router.
24pub fn build_router(state: AppState) -> Router {
25    let max_body = state.config.max_request_bytes;
26    let dashboard_enabled = state.config.dashboard_enabled;
27    let mut router = Router::new()
28        .route("/health", get(health))
29        .route("/livez", get(livez))
30        .route("/readyz", get(readyz))
31        .route("/metrics", get(metrics))
32        .route("/v1/chat/completions", post(chat_completions).options(cors_deny))
33        .route(
34            "/v1/mcp",
35            post(mcp_call).get(mcp_get).delete(mcp_delete).options(cors_deny),
36        )
37        .route(
38            "/mcp",
39            post(mcp_call).get(mcp_get).delete(mcp_delete).options(cors_deny),
40        )
41        .route(
42            "/v1/mcp/{backend}",
43            post(mcp_backend_call)
44                .get(mcp_get)
45                .delete(mcp_delete)
46                .options(cors_deny),
47        )
48        .route(
49            "/mcp/{backend}",
50            post(mcp_backend_call)
51                .get(mcp_get)
52                .delete(mcp_delete)
53                .options(cors_deny),
54        )
55        .route("/v1/sessions/{id}/close", post(close_session).options(cors_deny))
56        .route(
57            "/v1/sessions/{id}/promote",
58            post(promote_session).options(cors_deny),
59        )
60        .route("/v1/token", post(token_exchange).options(cors_deny))
61        .route("/v1/revoke", post(crate::token_routes::revoke).options(cors_deny))
62        .route("/.well-known/jwks.json", get(jwks));
63    if !state.config.introspection_tokens.is_empty() {
64        router = router.route(
65            "/v1/introspect",
66            post(crate::token_routes::introspect).options(cors_deny),
67        );
68    }
69    if !state.config.operator_tokens.is_empty() {
70        router = router.route(
71            "/admin/v1/revocations",
72            post(crate::token_routes::admin_revoke).options(cors_deny),
73        );
74        if state.judge.as_ref().is_some_and(|judge| judge.drift().is_some()) {
75            router = router
76                .route(
77                    "/admin/v1/judge/reviews",
78                    post(crate::token_routes::admin_judge_review).options(cors_deny),
79                )
80                .route(
81                    "/admin/v1/judge/drift",
82                    get(crate::token_routes::admin_judge_drift).options(cors_deny),
83                )
84                .route(
85                    "/admin/v1/judge/drift/reset",
86                    post(crate::token_routes::admin_judge_drift_reset).options(cors_deny),
87                );
88        }
89    }
90    if dashboard_enabled {
91        router = router
92            .route("/dashboard", get(crate::dashboard::index))
93            .route("/dashboard/", get(crate::dashboard::index))
94            .route("/dashboard/style.css", get(crate::dashboard::style_css))
95            .route("/dashboard/app.js", get(crate::dashboard::app_js))
96            .route("/api/v1/dashboard/stats", get(crate::dashboard::stats))
97            .route("/api/v1/dashboard/sessions", get(crate::dashboard::list_sessions))
98            .route(
99                "/api/v1/dashboard/sessions/{id}",
100                get(crate::dashboard::session_detail),
101            );
102    }
103    router
104        .layer(axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state(
105            state.clone(),
106            enforce_allowed_hosts,
107        ))
108        .layer(axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state(
109            state.clone(),
110            request_metrics,
111        ))
112        .layer(axum::middleware::from_fn(trace_request))
113        // axum's DefaultBodyLimit rejection is a bare
114        // text/plain "length limit exceeded" — it names neither the
115        // knob nor the limit, breaks the JSON error contract every
116        // other response honours, and is the first error a
117        // vision-agent user hits. Rewrite it into the OpenAI error
118        // shape naming `max_request_bytes` and its configured value.
119        // Sits OUTSIDE the limit layer so it sees the 413 response.
120        .layer(axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state(state.clone(), explain_body_limit))
121        // axum's default body limit is 2 MiB, which silently rejects large
122        // chat contexts (Claude 200k, GPT-4 128k) before the sandbox even
123        // sees the payload. `max_request_bytes` (default 4 MiB, matching
124        // the sandbox `MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES`) is the single knob operators
125        // control.
126        .layer(axum::extract::DefaultBodyLimit::max(max_body))
127        .with_state(state)
128}
129
130/// See the layer comment in [`build_router`]: turn the bare-text 413
131/// from `DefaultBodyLimit` into the OpenAI-shaped JSON error, naming
132/// the config knob and the configured limit.
133async fn explain_body_limit(
134    State(state): State<AppState>,
135    request: Request<Body>,
136    next: axum::middleware::Next,
137) -> Response {
138    let response = next.run(request).await;
139    if response.status() != StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE {
140        return response;
141    }
142    // Only rewrite the extractor's bare-text rejection; a JSON 413
143    // minted by a handler already honours the contract.
144    let is_json = response
145        .headers()
146        .get(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE)
147        .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
148        .is_some_and(|value| value.starts_with("application/json"));
149    if is_json {
150        return response;
151    }
152    let limit = state.config.max_request_bytes;
153    (
154        StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE,
155        Json(serde_json::json!({
156            "error": {
157                "message": format!(
158                    "request body exceeds max_request_bytes ({limit} bytes); \
159                     raise `max_request_bytes` in the harness config if larger \
160                     payloads are intended"
161                ),
162                "type": "invalid_request_error",
163                "param": serde_json::Value::Null,
164                // Numeric, matching `pipeline_error`'s 413 and the
165                // documented contract ("`code` is the numeric HTTP
166                // status"): the same 413 class must not have two
167                // incompatible shapes depending on whether axum's body
168                // limit or the compression floor tripped first.
169                "code": StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE.as_u16(),
170            }
171        })),
172    )
173        .into_response()
174}

176/// DNS-rebinding defense: when `allowed_hosts` is non-empty,
177/// refuse any request whose `Host` header (port stripped,
178/// case-insensitive) is not listed — BEFORE any handler runs. A
179/// hostile page's JavaScript can reach this service under an
180/// attacker-controlled hostname whose DNS was rebound to our IP;
181/// same-origin policy doesn't help because the browser believes the
182/// origin is the attacker's. An absent or unparseable Host is refused
183/// too (every HTTP/1.1 client sends one; HTTP/2 :authority maps to it).
184async fn enforce_allowed_hosts(
185    State(state): State<AppState>,
186    request: Request<Body>,
187    next: Next,
188) -> Response {
189    if state.config.allowed_hosts.is_empty() {
190        return next.run(request).await;
191    }
192    let host = request
193        .headers()
194        .get(axum::http::header::HOST)
195        .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
196        .map(|value| {
197            // Strip :port — IPv6 literals carry brackets ([::1]:8484).
198            let stripped = value
199                .rsplit_once(':')
200                .filter(|(head, port)| !head.is_empty() && port.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()))
201                .map_or(value, |(head, _)| head);
202            stripped.trim_start_matches('[').trim_end_matches(']')
203        });
204    let allowed = host.is_some_and(|host| {
205        state.config.allowed_hosts.iter().any(|entry| {
206            entry
207                .trim_start_matches('[')
208                .trim_end_matches(']')
209                .eq_ignore_ascii_case(host)
210        })
211    });
212    if !allowed {
213        state
214            .metrics
215            .counter(
216                "pv_host_header_refused_total",
217                "Requests refused by the allowed_hosts Host-header allowlist",
218            )
219            .inc();
220        return (
221            StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,
222            Json(json!({
223                "error": {
224                    "message": "Host header is not in allowed_hosts",
225                    "type": "permission_error",
226                    "param": null,
227                    "code": 403,
228                }
229            })),
230        )
231            .into_response();
232    }
233    next.run(request).await
234}

236/// data-plane request metrics. Every HTTP request —
237/// including the early-4xx returns the review flagged as unaudited —
238/// lands in `pv_requests_total{route,status_class}` and
239/// `pv_request_duration_seconds{route}`. The route label is drawn
240/// from a FIXED set (no client-controlled values) so metric
241/// cardinality is bounded; unknown paths collapse to `other`.
242///
243/// R58 hot-path: metric handles are pre-resolved into
244/// `HotMetrics.request_counters` / `request_duration_histograms`
245/// arrays indexed by `Route::index()` and `StatusClass::index()`.
246/// This eliminates the per-request `format!` (~120 B alloc) and the
247/// 4 shared-`Registry` mutex acquisitions (2 for each `.counter()`
248/// and `.histogram_with_bounds()` call) that the prior lazy path
249/// incurred — at 10k req/s that's ~40k mutex ops/s + 1.2 MB/s of
250/// allocator churn on the middleware alone. K8s liveness /
251/// readiness probes at 5-10 s intervals per replica are the
252/// dominant callers by count.
253async fn request_metrics(State(state): State<AppState>, request: Request<Body>, next: Next) -> Response {
254    let route = route(request.uri().path());
255    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
256    let response = next.run(request).await;
257    let status_class = crate::pipeline::StatusClass::from_u16(response.status().as_u16());
258    // Safe: `Route::index()` returns `0..10` (see `Route::ORDER`
259    // length) and `StatusClass::index()` returns `0..5` (see
260    // `StatusClass::ORDER` length); `HotMetrics` allocates arrays
261    // of exactly those sizes. Silence `clippy::indexing_slicing`
262    // — a debug-assertion sanity check would be more expensive than
263    // the guarded lookup on the hot path.
264    #[allow(clippy::indexing_slicing)]
265    {
266        state.hot_metrics.request_counters[route.index()][status_class.index()].inc();
267        state.hot_metrics.request_duration_histograms[route.index()].observe_us(elapsed_us(started));
268    }
269    response
270}

272/// Fixed route-label set for `pv_requests_total`. NEVER interpolate a
273/// client-controlled value here — Prometheus cardinality is bounded
274/// only because this set is closed.
275fn route(path: &str) -> crate::pipeline::Route {
276    use crate::pipeline::Route;
277    match path {
278        "/v1/chat/completions" => Route::Chat,
279        "/v1/mcp" | "/mcp" => Route::Mcp,
280        "/health" => Route::Health,
281        "/livez" => Route::Livez,
282        "/readyz" => Route::Readyz,
283        "/metrics" => Route::Metrics,
284        "/v1/token" => Route::TokenExchange,
285        "/v1/revoke" => Route::Revoke,
286        "/v1/introspect" => Route::Introspect,
287        "/admin/v1/revocations" => Route::AdminRevocation,
288        "/.well-known/jwks.json" => Route::Jwks,
289        _ if path.starts_with("/v1/mcp/") || path.starts_with("/mcp/") => Route::Mcp,
290        _ if path.starts_with("/v1/sessions/") && path.ends_with("/close") => Route::SessionClose,
291        _ if path.starts_with("/v1/sessions/") && path.ends_with("/promote") => Route::SessionPromote,
292        _ if path.starts_with("/dashboard") || path.starts_with("/api/v1/dashboard") => Route::Dashboard,
293        _ => Route::Other,
294    }
295}

297async fn trace_request(request: Request<Body>, next: Next) -> Response {
298    let method = request.method().clone();
299    let path = request.uri().path().to_owned();
300    // Sanitize the session id BEFORE binding it into the
301    // span. Previously the raw header value went in verbatim, which
302    // (1) risked unbounded label cardinality on OTLP exporters that
303    // map span attributes to metric labels — every distinct
304    // client-supplied session id (including hostile garbage) became
305    // its own series; (2) created a split-brain when a client sent
306    // two `X-PV-Session` headers — `HeaderMap::get` returned the
307    // first while `pipeline::single_header` refused the
308    // whole request, so traces named a "friendly" id for a hard-400;
309    // (3) accepted values that pass `HeaderValue::to_str` but fail
310    // `SessionId::parse` (too long, control chars in disguise). Use
311    // `single_header` + `SessionId::parse` to bind ONE consistent
312    // value or the sentinel `"invalid"`.
313    // Use a sentinel that CANNOT pass `SessionId::parse`
314    // (0x21..=0x7e visible-ASCII only), so a client cannot legitimately
315    // send `X-PV-Session: invalid` and share a trace label with a
316    // rejected request. The leading space (0x20) is outside the
317    // allowed range → collision-free.
318    let headers = request.headers();
319    let session_id = match crate::pipeline::single_header(headers, crate::pipeline::SESSION_HEADER) {
320        Ok(Some(value)) => value
321            .to_str()
322            .ok()
323            .and_then(|v| pv_core::SessionId::parse(v).ok())
324            .map(|id| id.to_string())
325            .unwrap_or_else(|| " rejected".to_owned()),
326        Ok(None) => " unbound".to_owned(),
327        Err(_) => " duplicate-header".to_owned(),
328    };
329    let span = tracing::info_span!(
330        "proofvisor.request",
331        otel.kind = "server",
332        http.request.method = %method,
333        url.path = %path,
334        session.id = %session_id,
335        http.response.status_code = tracing::field::Empty,
336    );
337    let response = next.run(request).instrument(span.clone()).await;
338    span.record("http.response.status_code", response.status().as_u16());
339    response
340}

342async fn health() -> impl IntoResponse {
343    // DO NOT expose the CARGO_PKG_VERSION on this
344    // unauthenticated endpoint. Version disclosure lets a LAN
345    // attacker correlate an proofvisor deployment to a specific
346    // known-vulnerable release without needing a chat probe. No
347    // harness endpoint surfaces build info (`/metrics` included);
348    // the version appears only in the *outbound* upstream
349    // `User-Agent` built in `pipeline.rs`.
350    Json(json!({
351        "status": "ok",
352        // Product identifier so callers (pvctl start) can tell a real
353        // ProofVisor apart from an unrelated service squatting the
354        // port. This is not a version number and reveals no
355        // vulnerability-relevant information.
356        "service": "proofvisor",
357    }))
358}
359
360/// Kubernetes-style liveness probe.
361///
362/// Constant response: liveness answers "is the process alive at all?"
363/// and must NOT couple to backend health — otherwise a transient state
364/// backend outage triggers a pod restart cascade instead of a
365/// readiness-based traffic drain. This mirrors `/health` (kept for
366/// backward compatibility) but with a name that reads as its intent.
367/// Point `livenessProbe` at `/livez`; point `readinessProbe` at
368/// `/readyz`.
369async fn livez() -> impl IntoResponse {
370    Json(json!({
371        "status": "alive",
372        "service": "proofvisor",
373    }))
374}
375
376/// Kubernetes-style readiness probe.
377///
378/// 200 when the harness can serve a request end-to-end; 503 while
379/// draining or when a required backend is unavailable. Checks:
380///   * `draining` — set by the SIGTERM handler before axum's graceful
381///     drain begins, so the LB stops sending new traffic first.
382///   * `atif_spool_dir` — attempts a metadata read so a missing / read-only
383///     spool (the shape that produces `503 audit capture unavailable`
384///     for every chat request) is reflected in readiness rather than
385///     hidden behind a hardcoded `/health` 200.
386///
387/// Returns the JSON body regardless of status so operators can diff
388/// which check failed without opening a shell.
389async fn readyz(State(state): State<AppState>) -> impl IntoResponse {
390    let draining = state.draining.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
391    // Writability probe, not just metadata: the outage this endpoint
392    // exists to surface is a FULL DISK (observed: 100% of traffic
393    // 503-ing while the pod stayed Ready) — and a full disk keeps the
394    // spool directory perfectly readable, so an `is_dir()` check
395    // passes through the whole incident. Create-write-sync-remove a
396    // probe file so ENOSPC/EROFS/EACCES all flip readiness. The name
397    // ends in `.tmp`, matching the boot sweep's orphan pattern, so a
398    // crash between create and remove self-heals on restart; UUIDv7
399    // uniqueness keeps concurrent probes from colliding.
400    //
401    // Run under `spawn_blocking` so a partial I/O outage (the exact
402    // condition this probe exists to catch) cannot stall a Tokio
403    // worker thread. Under a K8s probe interval smaller than a
404    // stall's ms-to-second latency, blocking the runtime here would
405    // escalate a filesystem hiccup into runtime-wide starvation
406    // exactly when other request paths need the workers most.
407    let spool_writable = {
408        let dir = state.config.atif_spool_dir.clone();
409        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
410            let probe = std::path::Path::new(&dir).join(format!(".readyz-{}.tmp", pv_core::new_event_uid()));
411            std::fs::write(&probe, b"readyz")
412                .and_then(|()| {
413                    // fsync would double the probe's IOPS cost for no
414                    // signal: ENOSPC surfaces at write() on every
415                    // mainstream filesystem.
416                    std::fs::remove_file(&probe)
417                })
418                .is_ok()
419        })
420        .await
421        .unwrap_or(false)
422    };
423    // Report a shared revocation outage without removing every replica from
424    // service. Authentication still refuses requests when the store is unreadable.
425    let revocation_health: Vec<_> = state
426        .identity
427        .as_ref()
428        .and_then(|validator| validator.revocation_store())
429        .and_then(|store| store.health())
430        .into_iter()
431        .chain(state.exchanged_revocations.health())
432        .collect();
433    let revocation_available = revocation_health.iter().all(|health| health.available);
434    let local_revocations: usize = revocation_health.iter().map(|health| health.local_entries).sum();
435    let ready = !draining && spool_writable;
436    let body = Json(json!({
437        "status": if ready { "ready" } else { "not_ready" },
438        "service": "proofvisor",
439        "checks": {
440            "draining": draining,
441            "spool_dir_writable": spool_writable,
442            "revocation_available": revocation_available,
443            "revocation_local_entries": local_revocations,
444        },
445    }));
446    if ready {
447        (StatusCode::OK, body).into_response()
448    } else {
449        (StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, body).into_response()
450    }
451}

453/// Explicit deny-CORS OPTIONS handler.
454///
455/// The harness is a same-origin proxy; no cross-origin client is
456/// expected or supported. Without this route, axum's default reply to
457/// a preflight (`OPTIONS /v1/chat/completions`) is `405 Method Not
458/// Allowed` with an `Allow: POST` header — inconsistent with the
459/// "no discoverable posture" hygiene, and confusing to any
460/// operator whose LAN browser client accidentally triggers a preflight.
461/// Reply with `204 No Content` and NO `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`
462/// header: browsers correctly treat this as "cross-origin denied" and
463/// refuse the actual request, making the posture explicit at the wire.
464async fn cors_deny() -> Response {
465    let mut response = Response::new(Body::empty());
466    *response.status_mut() = StatusCode::NO_CONTENT;
467    response.headers_mut().insert(
468        axum::http::header::CACHE_CONTROL,
469        HeaderValue::from_static("no-store"),
470    );
471    // Do not echo the requester's Origin. Do not include any
472    // Access-Control-Allow-* header. This deliberately fails the
473    // browser's preflight check.
474    response
475}

477async fn metrics(State(state): State<AppState>) -> Response {
478    // Refresh gauges immediately before rendering so the scrape
479    // reflects the live registry state. A gauge held
480    // as `Arc<Gauge>` in AppState would also work, but sampling
481    // once per scrape avoids inc/dec bookkeeping on every session
482    // insert/remove and cannot drift out of sync with the actual
483    // dashmap state.
484    state
485        .metrics
486        .gauge(
487            "pv_open_sessions",
488            "Currently-open sessions in the in-memory registry",
489        )
490        .set(state.sessions.len() as u64);
491    // Worker backlog + spool footprint, sampled per
492    // scrape. Queue depth is one atomic load; the spool walk is a
493    // single-level read_dir summing entry sizes (a few ms even at
494    // tens of thousands of files, amortized across the scrape
495    // interval).
496    state
497        .metrics
498        .gauge(
499            "pv_worker_queue_depth",
500            "Accepted-but-not-yet-completed worker jobs",
501        )
502        .set(state.worker.queue_depth());
503    // Move the synchronous `read_dir` + per-entry `metadata` calls to
504    // the blocking pool. Pre-fix this ran directly on the tokio worker
505    // polling the /metrics request, so any co-scheduled task on that
506    // worker (SSE frame writes, per-connection reads, close-session
507    // waits, the reconciler tick if it landed on the same worker)
508    // stalled for the walk's duration. Prometheus/OTel scrape every
509    // 15-30 s from every replica, so this was a periodic tail-
510    // latency step visible on the streaming path. Worse: a stuck
511    // NFS/EFS mount for the spool volume could hang the request
512    // handler entirely, letting `/readyz` and `/metrics` lie about
513    // liveness while workers hung. `spawn_blocking` isolates the
514    // syscall on the blocking pool and lets the tokio scheduler
515    // continue polling other futures.
516    let spool_dir = state.config.atif_spool_dir.clone();
517    let (spool_bytes, spool_files) =
518        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || spool_footprint(std::path::Path::new(&spool_dir)))
519            .await
520            .unwrap_or((0, 0));
521    state
522        .metrics
523        .gauge(
524            "pv_spool_bytes",
525            "Total bytes in the top-level ATIF spool directory",
526        )
527        .set(spool_bytes);
528    state
529        .metrics
530        .gauge(
531            "pv_spool_files",
532            "File count in the top-level ATIF spool directory",
533        )
534        .set(spool_files);
535    let mut response = Response::new(Body::from(state.metrics.render()));
536    response.headers_mut().insert(
537        axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE,
538        HeaderValue::from_static("text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8"),
539    );
540    response
541}
542
543/// Sum size and count of regular files in the top level of the spool
544/// directory. Non-recursive on purpose: subdirectories (broker-acks/,
545/// receipts/) have bounded per-session cost and a recursive walk per
546/// scrape would reintroduce the §8.1 O(spool) tax on another path.
547fn spool_footprint(dir: &std::path::Path) -> (u64, u64) {
548    let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else {
549        return (0, 0);
550    };
551    let mut bytes = 0u64;
552    let mut files = 0u64;
553    for entry in entries.flatten() {
554        if let Ok(metadata) = entry.metadata() {
555            if metadata.is_file() {
556                bytes = bytes.saturating_add(metadata.len());
557                files = files.saturating_add(1);
558            }
559        }
560    }
561    (bytes, files)
562}

564/// Refuse an inbound request whose declared `Content-Type` is not
565/// `application/json`. Shared by `chat_completions` and `mcp_call`
566/// so both trust-boundary ingress points agree on the same rules —
567/// a client sending e.g. `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` with a
568/// JSON body would otherwise process successfully on a route that
569/// forgot the check. Missing Content-Type is tolerated (minimal
570/// clients skip it and JSON parsers accept the body's shape).
571///
572/// `context_label` is inlined into the client-facing 400 body so
573/// operators reading the message know which endpoint refused.
574fn refuse_non_json_content_type(headers: &HeaderMap, context_label: &str) -> Option<Response> {
575    let value = headers.get(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE)?;
576    let is_json = value
577        .to_str()
578        .ok()
579        .and_then(|s| s.split(';').next())
580        .map(|main| main.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case("application/json"))
581        .unwrap_or(false);
582    if is_json {
583        return None;
584    }
585    let display = value.to_str().unwrap_or("<non-ascii>");
586    Some(pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request(
587        format!("{context_label} requires Content-Type: application/json, got {display:?}"),
588    )))
589}
590
591/// Refuse a request that a browser page sent cross-site. A server-side
592/// agent never sends `Origin`; a browser always does on a cross-origin
593/// `POST`, even in `no-cors` mode where no preflight runs. Without this
594/// check a hostile page could drive the chat, session and token routes
595/// of a loopback daemon in anonymous mode and spend the operator's
596/// provider budget. Same allowlist as the MCP routes
597/// (`mcp_allowed_origins`); the refusal uses the route's own error shape.
598pub(crate) fn refuse_foreign_origin(state: &AppState, headers: &HeaderMap) -> Option<Response> {
599    let mut origins = headers.get_all(axum::http::header::ORIGIN).iter();
600    let origin = origins.next()?;
601    let allowed = origins.next().is_none()
602        && origin.to_str().is_ok_and(|origin| {
603            state
604                .config
605                .mcp_allowed_origins
606                .iter()
607                .any(|allowed| allowed.trim_end_matches('/').eq_ignore_ascii_case(origin))
608        });
609    if allowed {
610        return None;
611    }
612    state
613        .metrics
614        .counter(
615            "pv_foreign_origin_refusals_total",
616            "Requests refused because their Origin header is not allowlisted",
617        )
618        .inc();
619    Some(
620        (
621            StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,
622            Json(openai_error_body(
623                StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,
624                "Origin is not allowed for this endpoint (see mcp_allowed_origins)",
625            )),
626        )
627            .into_response(),
628    )
629}
630
631async fn chat_completions(State(state): State<AppState>, headers: HeaderMap, body: Bytes) -> Response {
632    if let Some(refusal) = refuse_foreign_origin(&state, &headers) {
633        return refusal;
634    }
635    // Parity with the MCP path (routes.rs::mcp_call): refuse an
636    // inbound request whose declared `Content-Type` is not
637    // `application/json`. The chat endpoint historically accepted
638    // any Content-Type and relied on `serde_json::from_slice` to
639    // fail — that pattern falls back to a stringly-typed 400 on
640    // deserialise error instead of a specific "spec expects
641    // application/json" 400 the operator can triage. Missing
642    // Content-Type stays tolerated (minimal clients skip it and
643    // JSON parsers accept the body's shape anyway); an EXPLICIT
644    // non-JSON declaration is refused. Same helper as MCP for
645    // strictly one place to change the parsing rules.
646    if let Some(err) = refuse_non_json_content_type(&headers, "chat completions") {
647        return err;
648    }
649    // R71 F3 (landed R72): pre-admission identity gate. Before
650    // this, an unauthenticated client could force
651    // `refuse_duplicate_json_keys` (full byte scan) +
652    // `serde_json::from_slice` (full parse) + `depth_of` (full
653    // recursion) on a `max_request_bytes = 16 MiB` body BEFORE
654    // any admission decision — a DoS amplification surface (three
655    // full-body passes × concurrent unauthenticated clients).
656    // Authenticate once before parsing, then carry the validated caller into
657    // preparation for scope rechecks and principal binding. Configured identity
658    // validators run off the reactor because revocation may use synchronous I/O;
659    // the anonymous path stays local even when the blocking pool is saturated.
660    let caller = match state.authenticate_chat_nonblocking(&headers).await {
661        Ok(caller) => caller,
662        Err(error) => {
663            if let Err(audit_error) = state.audit_authentication_error(&headers, &error) {
664                return pipeline_error(audit_error);
665            }
666            return pipeline_error(error);
667        }
668    };
669    // Refuse duplicate top-level or
670    // nested JSON keys before parsing. `Json<Value>` used
671    // `serde_json` default "last-wins" semantics, so a hostile client
672    // could send `{"messages":[safe],"messages":[hostile]}` — the
673    // harness saw the hostile array, but any auditor/dashboard
674    // reading the raw request bytes (e.g. via
675    // `pv_events::atif_capture_from_request` chain input) sees an
676    // ambiguous document, breaking the "same signature ⇔ same
677    // bytes" auditor invariant pinned for receipts.
678    // Same fix as `parse_tool_call` on the MCP path — use the shared
679    // primitive.
680    if let Err(reason) = pv_sandbox::refuse_duplicate_json_keys(&body) {
681        return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request(format!(
682            "chat request rejected: {reason}"
683        )));
684    }
685    let payload: Value = match serde_json::from_slice(&body) {
686        Ok(value) => value,
687        Err(error) => return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request_source(error)),
688    };
689    // Parity with the MCP path (`pv_sandbox::parse_tool_call`) which
690    // caps `MAX_JSON_DEPTH = 64`. serde_json's built-in
691    // `RECURSION_LIMIT = 128` prevents stack blowout, but the chat
692    // trust-boundary discipline is uneven relative to the tool-call
693    // gate: a 4 MiB nested payload that MCP would refuse silently
694    // parsed on chat. Apply the same cap so both trust-boundary
695    // ingress points agree on JSON-shape limits.
696    if pv_sandbox::rpc::depth_of(&payload, 0) > pv_sandbox::rpc::MAX_JSON_DEPTH {
697        return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request(format!(
698            "chat request nesting depth exceeds {}",
699            pv_sandbox::rpc::MAX_JSON_DEPTH
700        )));
701    }
702    let admission_started = std::time::Instant::now();
703    let mut prepared = match state
704        .prepare_authenticated_chat(&headers, payload, body.len(), caller)
705        .await
706    {
707        Ok(prepared) => prepared,
708        Err(error) => return pipeline_error(error),
709    };
710    prepared.middleware_us = elapsed_us(admission_started);
711    let session = Arc::clone(&prepared.session);
712    let identity = prepared.identity.clone();
713    let session_id = prepared.session.id.clone();
714    let middleware_us = prepared.middleware_us;
715    let forwarded = match state.forward_chat(prepared).await {
716        Ok(response) => response,
717        Err(error) => return pipeline_error_for_session(error, &session_id),
718    };
719    let crate::pipeline::ForwardedResponse {
720        status,
721        headers: upstream_headers,
722        body: upstream_body,
723        billed_prompt_tokens,
724        lease,
725        mut capture_guard,
726    } = forwarded;
727    let Some(response_permit) = capture_guard.take_permit() else {
728        // Defensive: `prepare_chat` always reserves a permit. Even so,
729        // retire the durable marker and the journalled attempt through
730        // the plain worker queue before failing — returning directly
731        // would leak the spool/inflight-responses/ marker (crash
732        // recovery then quarantines the session) and leave a dangling
733        // non-terminal ResponseAttempt. If even that submit fails, fail
734        // the session closed rather than dropping the capture silently.
735        let (response_marker, response_attempt_id) = capture_guard.disarm();
736        let capture_session = Arc::clone(&session);
737        if state
738            .worker
739            .try_submit(crate::pipeline::refused_response_failure_job(
740                session,
741                identity,
742                "response_capture_permit_missing".to_owned(),
743                response_marker,
744                response_attempt_id,
745            ))
746            .is_err()
747        {
748            capture_session.mark_capture_failed();
749        }
750        let mut response = lifecycle_error("durable response capture permit is missing".to_owned());
751        if let Ok(value) = HeaderValue::from_str(&session_id) {
752            response
753                .headers_mut()
754                .insert(crate::pipeline::SESSION_HEADER, value);
755        }
756        return response;
757    };
758
759    // reqwest is built without the `gzip` feature (see Cargo.toml), so
760    // the client does not decode `Content-Encoding: gzip`. If the
761    // provider or a CDN in front of it compresses the SSE response,
762    // `absorb_network_chunk` immediately fails
763    // `std::str::from_utf8(&frame)` and aborts every stream. Refuse
764    // the response up front with a clear error rather than corrupt
765    // the audit trail with UTF-8-error frames.
766    //
767    // Multi-value / multi-line semantics: an upstream that sends
768    // `Content-Encoding: identity` on one line and
769    // `Content-Encoding: gzip` on another (some layered reverse
770    // proxies do this) would slip past a `.get(...)` that only reads
771    // the first value. Iterate `get_all` and require EVERY value to
772    // be empty or `identity` case-insensitively; also split each
773    // value on `,` so `gzip, identity` (single header, two tokens)
774    // is caught.
775    let mut refused_encoding: Option<(String, String)> = None;
776    'encodings: for value in upstream_headers.get_all(axum::http::header::CONTENT_ENCODING) {
777        let raw = value.to_str().unwrap_or_default();
778        for token in raw.split(',') {
779            let token = token.trim();
780            if token.is_empty() || token.eq_ignore_ascii_case("identity") {
781                continue;
782            }
783            refused_encoding = Some((token.to_owned(), raw.to_owned()));
784            break 'encodings;
785        }
786    }
787    if let Some((token, raw)) = refused_encoding {
788        // Retire the durable in-flight marker and terminally fail the
789        // journalled response attempt before refusing — mirroring
790        // forward_chat's Err arm. Returning without this leaked the
791        // marker (recover_spooled_sessions quarantined the session on
792        // every subsequent boot) and left a dangling non-terminal
793        // attempt while the session later closed with a "clean"
794        // receipt. Stable classifier only in the persisted record —
795        // the header token is upstream-controlled bytes. If the shard
796        // is full, fail the session closed rather than dropping the
797        // capture silently (same rationale as forward_chat's Err arm).
798        let (response_marker, response_attempt_id) = capture_guard.disarm();
799        let capture_session = Arc::clone(&session);
800        if response_permit
801            .submit(
802                &state.worker,
803                crate::pipeline::refused_response_failure_job(
804                    session,
805                    identity,
806                    "upstream_unsupported_content_encoding".to_owned(),
807                    response_marker,
808                    response_attempt_id,
809                ),
810            )
811            .is_err()
812        {
813            capture_session.mark_capture_failed();
814        }
815        return pipeline_error_for_session(
816            crate::pipeline::PipelineError::upstream(format!(
817                "upstream responded with unsupported Content-Encoding token {token:?} \
818                 (full header: {raw:?}) — the proxy is built without decompression \
819                 support; enable it upstream (Accept-Encoding: identity) or rebuild \
820                 with the reqwest `gzip` feature"
821            )),
822            &session_id,
823        );
824    }
825    // RFC 7231 §3.1.1.1 says media type/subtype are
826    // case-insensitive and the header value may carry parameters
827    // (`; charset=utf-8`). Byte-exact `starts_with("text/event-stream")`
828    // misses `Text/Event-Stream` (some CDNs re-title-case) and can also
829    // mis-fire on hypothetical `text/event-stream-json`. Split on `;`
830    // then compare with `eq_ignore_ascii_case` so SSE is detected
831    // regardless of casing and parameters. A misclassified SSE stream
832    // gets buffered to the 16 MiB provider cap in the non-SSE branch
833    // and either loses streaming semantics (client sees no deltas
834    // until upstream EOF) or is refused with 502 despite being valid.
835    let is_sse = is_sse_content_type(&upstream_headers);
836    // `AbortFinalizingStream` owns marker retirement and attempt
837    // termination from here (including on mid-stream client disconnect,
838    // via its own Drop); hand both over and disarm the guard.
839    let (response_marker, response_attempt_id) = capture_guard.disarm();
840    // Same gating as admission (`prepare_chat`): a configured
841    // [principal_budget] binds every request, keyed by
842    // `principal_id_for_budget` — anonymous deployments share one
843    // bucket by explicit opt-in.
844    let principal_budget = state
845        .config
846        .principal_budget
847        .as_ref()
848        .map(|spec| (crate::pipeline::principal_id_for_budget(&identity), spec.clone()));
849    let stream = AbortFinalizingStream {
850        inner: upstream_body,
851        session,
852        identity,
853        response_permit: Some(response_permit),
854        worker: state.worker.clone(),
855        store: Arc::clone(&state.store),
856        budget: state.effective_budget(),
857        rates: Arc::clone(&state.pushed_rates),
858        pushed: state.sandbox.pushed(),
859        local_budget: state.config.budget.clone(),
860        failure_policy: None,
861        emitted_any: false,
862        egress_scanned: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
863        egress_scanned_reasoning: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
864        egress_scanned_tools: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
865        hold_stream: false,
866        held_frames: Vec::new(),
867        egress_transforms: Vec::new(),
868        finalizer: state.finalizer.clone(),
869        _lease: lease,
870        response_marker,
871        response_attempt_id,
872        response_choices: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
873        response_model: None,
874        upstream_status: status,
875        response_cost_usd_micros: 0,
876        response_tool_calls: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
877        response_metrics: pv_events::EventMetrics::default(),
878        charged_completion_tokens: 0,
879        last_reported_completion_tokens: None,
880        last_reported_prompt_tokens: None,
881        last_reported_cached_tokens: None,
882        last_reported_cost_usd_micros: None,
883        saw_chunk: false,
884        capture_attempted: false,
885        is_sse,
886        protocol_buffer: Vec::new(),
887        frame_scratch: Vec::new(),
888        pending_output: std::collections::VecDeque::new(),
889        pending_budget: None,
890        principal_budget,
891        captured_bytes: 0,
892        billed_prompt_tokens,
893        completed: false,
894        // Validated single-value by `prepare_chat`; absence means the
895        // id was generated server-side this request.
896        ephemeral: !headers.contains_key(crate::pipeline::SESSION_HEADER),
897    };
898    let mut stream = stream;
899    // A pushed transform over model responses needs the whole text
900    // before it can rewrite it: hold a streamed response until it is
901    // complete and relay it rewritten (see `hold_stream`).
902    stream.hold_stream = is_sse && stream.pushed.rewrites_responses();
903    let mut response = if is_sse {
904        // Peek the FIRST item before committing the response head: when
905        // the first poll fails (empty 200 body, first frame invalid
906        // JSON, hostile usage fields), returning `Body::from_stream`
907        // directly made hyper abort the connection before flushing the
908        // status line — the client saw a raw empty reply (curl exit 52,
909        // http_code 000) instead of the clean 502/403 this file's own
910        // policy mandates. SDKs classify that as a network error and
911        // auto-retry, and each retry burns admission budget and seals
912        // another artifact-less session. Mid-stream failures (bytes
913        // already relayed) remain severed — unavoidable once the head
914        // is committed — but the pre-first-byte case surfaces as a real
915        // HTTP error exactly like the buffered non-SSE branch.
916        let mut relay = Box::pin(stream);
917        match relay.next().await {
918            Some(Err(error)) => {
919                let mapped = if matches!(
920                    error.kind(),
921                    std::io::ErrorKind::QuotaExceeded | std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied
922                ) {
923                    crate::pipeline::PipelineError::blocked_source(error)
924                } else {
925                    crate::pipeline::PipelineError::upstream_source(error)
926                };
927                // Dropping the relay runs its finalization Drop
928                // (evidence capture + session seal).
929                return pipeline_error_for_session(mapped, &session_id);
930            }
931            Some(Ok(first)) => {
932                let head = futures::stream::once(async move { Ok::<_, std::io::Error>(first) });
933                Response::new(Body::from_stream(head.chain(relay)))
934            }
935            // Clean zero-item stream: every capture gate already ran
936            // inside the relay's EOF arm and succeeded.
937            None => Response::new(Body::empty()),
938        }
939    } else {
940        // A non-SSE body is fully buffered inside the relay before any byte
941        // is released: worker capture and the completion-token budget gate
942        // run on the complete body. Handing axum a stream here would commit
943        // the upstream status line before those gates run, so a budget
944        // refusal degraded into a 200 head followed by an empty body with
945        // no explanation. Drain the relay first (no extra buffering beyond
946        // what the relay already does) and surface refusals as real errors.
947        let mut relay = Box::pin(stream);
948        let mut buffered: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
949        loop {
950            match relay.next().await {
951                Some(Ok(bytes)) => buffered.extend_from_slice(&bytes),
952                Some(Err(error)) => {
953                    // Route through
954                    // `pipeline_error` so the status class matches the
955                    // admission-time decision for the SAME condition
956                    // and the advisory headers are attached. The prior
957                    // hand-built 429 contradicted the deliberate
958                    // 403-not-429 choice for budget caps (a permanent
959                    // per-session refusal SDKs must not auto-retry)
960                    // and omitted the Retry-After that this file's own
961                    // policy mandates on every 502.
962                    let mapped = if matches!(
963                        error.kind(),
964                        std::io::ErrorKind::QuotaExceeded | std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied
965                    ) {
966                        crate::pipeline::PipelineError::blocked_source(error)
967                    } else {
968                        crate::pipeline::PipelineError::upstream_source(error)
969                    };
970                    // Dropping the relay here runs its finalization Drop
971                    // (evidence capture + session seal), same as when a
972                    // client observed the severed stream.
973                    return pipeline_error_for_session(mapped, &session_id);
974                }
975                None => break,
976            }
977        }
978        Response::new(Body::from(buffered))
979    };
980    *response.status_mut() = status;
981    for (name, value) in &upstream_headers {
982        if is_forwardable_upstream_header(name, &state.config.upstream_auth_header) {
983            // `append`, not `insert`: iterating a HeaderMap repeats the name
984            // for each value of a multi-valued header, and `insert` would
985            // keep only the last one.
986            response.headers_mut().append(name.clone(), value.clone());
987        }
988    }
989    if let Ok(value) = HeaderValue::from_str(&session_id) {
990        response
991            .headers_mut()
992            .insert(crate::pipeline::SESSION_HEADER, value);
993    }
994    if let Ok(value) = HeaderValue::from_str(&middleware_us.to_string()) {
995        response
996            .headers_mut()
997            .insert(crate::pipeline::MIDDLEWARE_US_HEADER, value);
998    }
999    // Pin `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every
1000    // upstream-relayed response. The relay forwards the upstream's
1001    // Content-Type verbatim (validated by our `is_sse_content_type`
1002    // for framing decisions, but not sanitised for the client).
1003    // A rogue upstream, MITM at egress, or CDN mis-config could
1004    // otherwise flip Content-Type to `text/html; charset=utf-8` on
1005    // a body carrying prompt-echoed attacker bytes — turning what
1006    // the audit trail attests as "assistant output" into HTML the
1007    // browser might render. `nosniff` prevents browser-side MIME
1008    // sniffing from disagreeing with the declared type and closes
1009    // the reflected-content path.
1010    response.headers_mut().insert(
1011        axum::http::HeaderName::from_static("x-content-type-options"),
1012        HeaderValue::from_static("nosniff"),
1013    );
1014    // SSE relays fronted by nginx (or an ingress that honours the
1015    // hint) must set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the response, or
1016    // nginx's default `proxy_buffering on` accumulates the entire
1017    // SSE body before flushing — the SDK sees no incremental
1018    // deltas until upstream EOF and the chat appears hung to
1019    // end-users. Same class of ops footgun even under GCP HTTPS LB
1020    // and other buffering front-ends that recognise this vendor
1021    // header. Non-SSE responses do not need or want the hint (it's
1022    // a no-op there).
1023    if is_sse {
1024        response.headers_mut().insert(
1025            axum::http::HeaderName::from_static("x-accel-buffering"),
1026            HeaderValue::from_static("no"),
1027        );
1028    }
1029    response
1030}
1031
1032/// Decide whether an upstream response header may be forwarded to the client.
1033///
1034/// This is a *proxy* trust boundary: the upstream LLM provider is not on the
1035/// same trust domain as our client, so blindly forwarding response headers
1036/// would let the upstream (or an attacker who influences the upstream)
1037/// - set cookies in our domain (`Set-Cookie` — cookie injection),
1038/// - open CORS on our origin (`Access-Control-Allow-*`),
1039/// - inject invalid or contradictory framing/hop-by-hop metadata
1040///   (`Transfer-Encoding`, `Content-Length`, `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`,
1041///   `Trailer`, `TE`, `Upgrade`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Authorization`),
1042/// - leak upstream implementation identity (`Server`, `X-Powered-By`,
1043///   `Via`, `X-Request-ID`).
1044///
1045/// Hyper computes framing metadata (`Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`)
1046/// itself when we build the response; forwarding the upstream's copies risks
1047/// double-encoded or contradictory headers and — with `Transfer-Encoding` —
1048/// classical HTTP request smuggling. Hop-by-hop headers are forbidden by
1049/// RFC 7230 §6.1 from crossing a proxy.
1050///
1051/// The denylist once covered `Authorization` (RFC 7235)
1052/// but NOT any custom-name auth header the harness itself uses to
1053/// authenticate to the upstream. Every LLM provider uses a distinct
1054/// custom header — `api-key` (Azure), `x-api-key` (Amazon Bedrock,
1055/// Together AI), `x-goog-api-key` (Google), `anthropic-api-key`
1056/// (Anthropic). A malicious or compromised upstream that echoes back
1057/// its request's auth header in the response would then leak the
1058/// operator's provider credential straight through to the caller.
1059/// Two-layer defense: (a) refuse every well-known API-key header name
1060/// by static allowlist below, AND (b) refuse the currently-configured
1061/// `upstream_auth_header` name so operator-specific choices are also
1062/// covered.
1063/// Apply the console-pushed `tool.args` transforms to a `tools/call`
1064/// body. A body the strict parser refuses is returned unchanged:
1065/// re-serialising it would hide the defect (a duplicate key, say) from
1066/// the parse gate that is about to refuse it.
1067fn apply_pushed_tool_transforms(state: &AppState, body: Bytes) -> Bytes {
1068    if state.sandbox.pushed().transforms.is_empty() || pv_sandbox::parse_tool_call(&body).is_err() {
1069        return body;
1070    }
1071    let Ok(mut request) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&body) else {
1072        return body;
1073    };
1074    let Some(tool) = request
1075        .pointer("/params/name")
1076        .and_then(Value::as_str)
1077        .map(str::to_owned)
1078    else {
1079        return body;
1080    };
1081    let Some(arguments) = request.pointer_mut("/params/arguments") else {
1082        return body;
1083    };
1084    let applied = state.sandbox.transform_tool_arguments(&tool, arguments);
1085    if applied.is_empty() {
1086        return body;
1087    }
1088    for transform in &applied {
1089        tracing::info!(
1090            tool = %tool,
1091            policy = %transform.policy,
1092            replacements = transform.replacements,
1093            "tool arguments rewritten by a console-pushed transform"
1094        );
1095    }
1096    state
1097        .metrics
1098        .counter(
1099            "pv_pushed_transform_rewrites_total",
1100            "Tool calls or chat requests rewritten by a console-pushed transform policy",
1101        )
1102        .inc();
1103    match serde_json::to_vec(&request) {
1104        Ok(bytes) => Bytes::from(bytes),
1105        Err(_) => body,
1106    }
1107}
1108
1109fn is_forwardable_upstream_header(name: &axum::http::HeaderName, upstream_auth_header: &str) -> bool {
1110    use axum::http::header;
1111    // Any header name whose lowercased ASCII equals the configured
1112    // upstream auth header MUST be stripped. `HeaderName` display is
1113    // already lowercase-normalised.
1114    if name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case(upstream_auth_header) {
1115        return false;
1116    }
1117    let is_denied = *name == header::CONTENT_LENGTH
1118        || *name == header::TRANSFER_ENCODING
1119        || *name == header::CONNECTION
1120        || *name == header::UPGRADE
1121        || *name == header::TE
1122        || *name == header::TRAILER
1123        || *name == header::PROXY_AUTHENTICATE
1124        || *name == header::PROXY_AUTHORIZATION
1125        // The harness holds the operator's provider credential; an upstream
1126        // that echoes the request's Authorization header back in its
1127        // response must not leak it to the client.
1128        || *name == header::AUTHORIZATION
1129        || *name == header::SET_COOKIE
1130        || *name == header::SERVER
1131        || *name == header::VIA
1132        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("keep-alive")
1133        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("x-powered-by")
1134        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("x-request-id")
1135        // Well-known provider API-key header names.
1136        // Verified against public docs of Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock,
1137        // Google Vertex, Anthropic, Cohere, DeepSeek, Together AI,
1138        // Groq, Mistral, and Fireworks.
1139        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("api-key")
1140        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("x-api-key")
1141        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("x-goog-api-key")
1142        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("anthropic-api-key")
1143        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("openai-api-key")
1144        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("x-auth-token")
1145        || name.as_str().eq_ignore_ascii_case("x-amz-security-token")
1146        // Never let the upstream open CORS on our origin — if we want CORS
1147        // we set it deliberately in our own router.
1148        || name.as_str().to_ascii_lowercase().starts_with("access-control-");
1149    !is_denied
1150}
1151
1152/// Detect `text/event-stream` in `Content-Type`
1153/// case-insensitively, accepting parameters like `; charset=utf-8`.
1154/// RFC 7231 §3.1.1.1 says media type/subtype are case-insensitive.
1155/// Byte-exact matching missed `Text/Event-Stream` (some CDNs
1156/// re-title-case) and mis-fired on hypothetical
1157/// `text/event-stream-json`. Misclassification cost: the non-SSE
1158/// branch buffers up to the 16 MiB provider cap and either loses
1159/// streaming semantics or refuses valid streams with 502.
1160fn is_sse_content_type(headers: &HeaderMap) -> bool {
1161    headers
1162        .get(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE)
1163        .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
1164        .is_some_and(|value| {
1165            let head = value.split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim();
1166            head.eq_ignore_ascii_case("text/event-stream")
1167        })
1168}
1169
1170/// Per-execution-key completion gate. Retains only gates that another
1171/// request currently holds (strong count > 1), so the map stays bounded
1172/// by in-flight completions rather than growing per historical key.
1173fn tool_audit_gate(state: &AppState, key: &str) -> Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>> {
1174    let mut gates = state.tool_audit_gates.lock();
1175    gates.retain(|_, gate| Arc::strong_count(gate) > 1);
1176    Arc::clone(gates.entry(key.to_owned()).or_default())
1177}

1179async fn mcp_call(State(state): State<AppState>, headers: HeaderMap, body: Bytes) -> Response {
1180    mcp_entry(state, headers, body, crate::mcp::Scope::All).await
1181}

1183/// `/mcp/{backend}`: the same MCP endpoint, restricted to one backend's
1184/// tools. Each backend gets its own route behind the one gateway host.
1185async fn mcp_backend_call(
1186    State(state): State<AppState>,
1187    Path(backend): Path<String>,
1188    headers: HeaderMap,
1189    body: Bytes,
1190) -> Response {
1191    if state.backend_router.get(&backend).is_none() {
1192        return (
1193            StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
1194            Json(openai_error_body(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "unknown MCP backend")),
1195        )
1196            .into_response();
1197    }
1198    mcp_entry(state, headers, body, crate::mcp::Scope::Backend(backend)).await
1199}

1201/// The gateway opens no server-to-client SSE stream, which the Streamable
1202/// HTTP transport allows by answering `GET` with 405.
1203async fn mcp_get(State(state): State<AppState>, headers: HeaderMap) -> Response {
1204    if let Err(response) = crate::mcp::check_origin(&state, &headers) {
1205        return *response;
1206    }
1207    let mut response = StatusCode::METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED.into_response();
1208    response.headers_mut().insert(
1209        axum::http::header::ALLOW,
1210        HeaderValue::from_static("POST, DELETE"),
1211    );
1212    response
1213}

1215/// `DELETE` with an `MCP-Session-Id` ends the MCP session: its ProofVisor
1216/// session is closed exactly like `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/close`, so the
1217/// session's receipt or trajectory is finalized.
1218async fn mcp_delete(State(state): State<AppState>, headers: HeaderMap) -> Response {
1219    if let Err(response) = crate::mcp::check_origin(&state, &headers) {
1220        return *response;
1221    }
1222    let caller = match lifecycle_caller(&state, &headers, &state.config.session_close_scope).await {
1223        Ok(caller) => caller,
1224        Err(error) => return pipeline_error(error),
1225    };
1226    let mut headers = headers;
1227    let session = match crate::mcp::bind_session(&state, &mut headers, &caller) {
1228        Ok(Some(session)) => session,
1229        Ok(None) => {
1230            return (
1231                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
1232                Json(openai_error_body(
1233                    StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
1234                    "MCP-Session-Id is required",
1235                )),
1236            )
1237                .into_response()
1238        }
1239        Err(response) => return *response,
1240    };
1241    state.mcp_backends.forget_agent_session(&session.agent_session);
1242    let Some(agent_session) = state.sessions.get(&session.agent_session) else {
1243        // No call ever opened the audited session: nothing to finalize.
1244        return StatusCode::NO_CONTENT.into_response();
1245    };
1246    if let Err(error) = caller.authorize_session(&state, &agent_session, &state.config.session_close_scope) {
1247        return pipeline_error(error);
1248    }
1249    match state
1250        .finalizer
1251        .close_session(agent_session, StopReason::SessionClosed)
1252        .await
1253    {
1254        Ok(outcome) => Json(outcome).into_response(),
1255        Err(error) => finalize_error_response(&error),
1256    }
1257}
1258
1259async fn mcp_entry(state: AppState, headers: HeaderMap, body: Bytes, scope: crate::mcp::Scope) -> Response {
1260    // Reject an inbound request whose declared
1261    // `Content-Type` is not `application/json`. MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0
1262    // (spec: MUST be `application/json`), and a client sending e.g.
1263    // `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` with a JSON body would
1264    // otherwise process successfully — a spec-violation surface with
1265    // no defensible use case. Missing Content-Type is tolerated
1266    // (some minimal clients skip it and JSON-RPC parsers accept the
1267    // body's shape).
1268    if let Some(err) = refuse_non_json_content_type(&headers, "MCP") {
1269        return err;
1270    }
1271    // R70 F1 (landed R71): admission cap before spawn. `mcp_call_inner`
1272    // buffers up to `MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_BYTES = 16 MiB` per call in
1273    // `read_limited_tool_response`; without a limiter, N concurrent
1274    // slow-tool-upstream callers stacked N × 16 MiB unbounded. Chat
1275    // path is capped via `worker.try_reserve_pair`; the MCP path was
1276    // the odd one out. `try_acquire_owned` is non-blocking: on
1277    // capacity refusal we return 503 (server-side capacity signal,
1278    // matches breaker-open discipline) with Retry-After: 1 so
1279    // well-behaved SDKs pace themselves.
1280    let admission_permit = match Arc::clone(&state.mcp_admission).try_acquire_owned() {
1281        Ok(permit) => permit,
1282        Err(_) => {
1283            // R72 review F2 (landed R74): direct `.inc()` on the
1284            // pre-resolved handle in AppState — no registry mutex
1285            // acquired on the refusal hot path. Matches HotMetrics
1286            // discipline.
1287            state.mcp_admission_refusals_counter.inc();
1288            let mut response = (
1289                StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
1290                Json(openai_error_body(
1291                    StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
1292                    "MCP admission at capacity; retry shortly",
1293                )),
1294            )
1295                .into_response();
1296            response
1297                .headers_mut()
1298                .insert(axum::http::header::RETRY_AFTER, HeaderValue::from_static("1"));
1299            return response;
1300        }
1301    };
1302    // The tool path mutates durable state at several awaits: the sandbox
1303    // gate debits the budget, `execution.claim()` claims the execution
1304    // key, the upstream call executes the tool, and persist/audit resolve
1305    // the outcome. Axum drops the handler future on client disconnect; a
1306    // cancellation between any two of those steps used to strand the
1307    // intermediate state with no owner — a claimed-but-unresolved key
1308    // answers every retry with 409 TOOL_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN while the
1309    // session lives (restart-time quarantine skips active sessions), and
1310    // a debited-but-unrefunded budget burns quota headroom per
1311    // disconnect. Run the whole body on a spawned task so it always runs
1312    // to completion; the handler merely awaits (and may abandon) the
1313    // result.
1314    //
1315    // The `mcp_inflight` guard is entered here on the outer handler and
1316    // moved into the spawn so its `Drop` decrements the tracker on the
1317    // spawn's completion path (including panic-caught unwind), NOT the
1318    // outer handler's cancellation. `finish_shutdown` in main.rs waits
1319    // for the tracker to drain before `worker.wait_idle`, so a detached
1320    // body cannot submit a fresh worker job after shutdown thinks it has
1321    // drained (which would trip `pv_shutdown_session_close_timeouts_
1322    // total` on an otherwise-recoverable session).
1323    let inflight_guard = state.mcp_inflight.enter();
1324    match tokio::spawn(async move {
1325        let _admission_permit = admission_permit;
1326        let _inflight_guard = inflight_guard;
1327        mcp_call_inner(state, headers, body, scope).await
1328    })
1329    .await
1330    {
1331        Ok(response) => response,
1332        Err(join_error) => lifecycle_error(format!("tool call task failed: {join_error}")),
1333    }
1334}
1335
1336/// Complete compensation before the detached MCP owner releases its permit.
1337/// StateStore is synchronous, so network-backed refunds must not run on Tokio.
1338async fn refund_tool_admission(
1339    state: &AppState,
1340    execution: &ToolExecution,
1341    payout_micros: u64,
1342    principal_id: Option<&str>,
1343) -> Result<(), String> {
1344    let store = Arc::clone(&state.store);
1345    let session_id = execution.session_id.clone();
1346    let tool = execution.tool.clone();
1347    let budget = state.effective_budget();
1348    let principal = principal_id
1349        .zip(state.config.principal_budget.as_ref())
1350        .map(|(id, spec)| (id.to_owned(), spec.clone()));
1351    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
1352        pv_state::ActionBudget::new(store.as_ref(), &session_id, &budget)
1353            .refund_tool_call(&tool, payout_micros);
1354        if let Some((principal_id, spec)) = principal {
1355            pv_state::ActionBudget::for_principal(store.as_ref(), &principal_id, &spec)
1356                .refund_tool_call(&tool, payout_micros);
1357        }
1358    })
1359    .await
1360    .map_err(|_| "tool admission refund task failed".to_owned())
1361}
1362
1363async fn mcp_call_inner(
1364    state: AppState,
1365    headers: HeaderMap,
1366    body: Bytes,
1367    scope: crate::mcp::Scope,
1368) -> Response {
1369    // Streamable HTTP transport rules come first: a refused Origin or an
1370    // unsupported protocol version never reaches authentication.
1371    if let Err(response) = crate::mcp::check_origin(&state, &headers) {
1372        return *response;
1373    }
1374    if let Err(response) = crate::mcp::check_protocol_version(&headers) {
1375        return *response;
1376    }
1377    let mut headers = headers;
1378    // Idempotent execution tracking is needed whenever a call CAN be
1379    // forwarded — through `tool_upstream_url` or any `[[backends]]` entry —
1380    // because the forwarding branch below has no other execution state.
1381    let forwarding_configured = state.config.tool_upstream_url.is_some() || !state.backend_router.is_empty();
1382    let auth_state = state.clone();
1383    let auth_headers = headers.clone();
1384    let authenticated =
1385        match tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || auth_state.authenticate(&auth_headers)).await {
1386            Ok(Ok(caller)) => caller,
1387            Ok(Err(error)) => {
1388                if let Err(audit_error) = state.audit_authentication_error(&headers, &error) {
1389                    return pipeline_error(audit_error);
1390                }
1391                return pipeline_error(error);
1392            }
1393            Err(error) => return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::unavailable_source(error)),
1394        };
1395    // An `MCP-Session-Id` names the audited session every call of that
1396    // MCP session belongs to; bind it as `X-PV-Session` for the tool path.
1397    let mcp_session = match crate::mcp::bind_session(&state, &mut headers, &authenticated) {
1398        Ok(session) => session,
1399        Err(response) => return *response,
1400    };
1401    match crate::mcp::answer(
1402        &state,
1403        &headers,
1404        &authenticated,
1405        crate::mcp::classify(&body),
1406        &scope,
1407        mcp_session.as_ref(),
1408    )
1409    .await
1410    {
1411        Ok(Some(response)) => return response,
1412        Ok(None) => {}
1413        Err(error) => {
1414            if let Err(audit_error) = state.audit_authentication_error(&headers, &error) {
1415                return pipeline_error(audit_error);
1416            }
1417            return pipeline_error(error);
1418        }
1419    }
1420    let (execution, unaudited_outcome) = if forwarding_configured {
1421        // Same cheap pre-parse identity gate as the intercept path
1422        // (pipeline::refuse_unauthenticated_tool_call): required
1423        // identity + no Authorization header can never be admitted —
1424        // refuse before `from_request` runs its parse/canonicalize/
1425        // hash work on anonymous bytes.
1426        if let Err(error) = state.refuse_unauthenticated_tool_call(&headers) {
1427            return pipeline_error(error);
1428        }
1429        match ToolExecution::from_request(&state.config.atif_spool_dir, &headers, &body, state.journal_key) {
1430            Ok(mut execution) => {
1431                let required_scope = crate::pipeline::tool_scope(&execution.tool);
1432                let identity = match authenticated.authorize(&state, Some(&required_scope)) {
1433                    Ok(identity) => identity,
1434                    Err(error) => {
1435                        if let Err(audit_error) = state.audit_authentication_error(&headers, &error) {
1436                            return pipeline_error(audit_error);
1437                        }
1438                        return pipeline_error(error);
1439                    }
1440                };
1441                if let Err(error) = execution.bind_principal(&identity) {
1442                    return pipeline_error(error);
1443                }
1444                if let Some(principal) = authenticated.principal_digest() {
1445                    execution.principal_digest = pv_core::digest::sha256_hex(
1446                        format!("{}:{principal}", execution.principal_digest).as_bytes(),
1447                    );
1448                }
1449                // The three cached-state arms below used
1450                // to repeat this lookup+authorize block verbatim,
1451                // differing only in the error string, and recomputed
1452                // `tool_scope` per arm. One helper, one scope.
1453                // Boxed Err keeps the closure's Result at pointer size
1454                // (clippy::result_large_err — Response is 128+ bytes).
1455                let authorized_session = |missing_context: &str| -> Result<(), Box<Response>> {
1456                    let Some(session) = state.sessions.get(&execution.session_id) else {
1457                        return Err(Box::new(pipeline_error(
1458                            crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request(format!(
1459                                "unknown session for {missing_context}"
1460                            )),
1461                        )));
1462                    };
1463                    authenticated
1464                        .authorize_session(&state, &session, &required_scope)
1465                        .map_err(|error| Box::new(pipeline_error(error)))
1466                };
1467                match execution.load().await {
1468                    Ok(ToolExecutionState::Completed(outcome)) => {
1469                        if let Err(response) = authorized_session("cached tool result") {
1470                            return *response;
1471                        }
1472                        return outcome.into_response();
1473                    }
1474                    Ok(ToolExecutionState::Unaudited(outcome)) => {
1475                        if let Err(response) = authorized_session("pending tool audit") {
1476                            return *response;
1477                        }
1478                        (Some(execution), Some(outcome))
1479                    }
1480                    Ok(ToolExecutionState::Pending) => {
1481                        if let Err(response) = authorized_session("pending tool execution") {
1482                            return *response;
1483                        }
1484                        return (
1485                            StatusCode::CONFLICT,
1486                            Json(json!({"error": TOOL_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN})),
1487                        )
1488                            .into_response();
1489                    }
1490                    Ok(ToolExecutionState::Missing) => (Some(execution), None),
1491                    Err(error) if error == TOOL_REQUEST_MISMATCH => {
1492                        // Same session-binding discipline as every other
1493                        // `load()` arm above: without it, any holder of a
1494                        // valid `tool:<name>`-scoped token could probe
1495                        // whether an execution key exists under a DIFFERENT
1496                        // request/principal (409 vs the Missing path) for
1497                        // sessions it is not bound to — a session-content
1498                        // oracle of the same shape as the fixed
1499                        // close/promote existence oracle.
1500                        let Some(session) = state.sessions.get(&execution.session_id) else {
1501                            return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request(
1502                                "unknown session for tool execution".to_owned(),
1503                            ));
1504                        };
1505                        if let Err(error) = authenticated.authorize_session(
1506                            &state,
1507                            &session,
1508                            &crate::pipeline::tool_scope(&execution.tool),
1509                        ) {
1510                            return pipeline_error(error);
1511                        }
1512                        return (
1513                            StatusCode::CONFLICT,
1514                            Json(json!({"error": TOOL_REQUEST_MISMATCH})),
1515                        )
1516                            .into_response();
1517                    }
1518                    Err(error) => return lifecycle_error(error),
1519                }
1520            }
1521            Err(error) => return pipeline_error(error),
1522        }
1523    } else {
1524        (None, None)
1525    };
1526    if let (Some(execution), Some(_)) = (execution.as_ref(), unaudited_outcome.as_ref()) {
1527        let _lease = match state.lease_session(&headers) {
1528            Ok(lease) => lease,
1529            Err(error) => return pipeline_error(error),
1530        };
1531        // Serialize with any racing completion of the same execution key
1532        // (fresh forward awaiting its audit, or another replay), then
1533        // re-check the on-disk state: without this, both requests would
1534        // submit a `tool_completed` job for one execution — two durable
1535        // execution records on the audit stream and in the signed chain.
1536        let gate = tool_audit_gate(&state, &execution.key);
1537        let _gate = gate.lock().await;
1538        let outcome = match execution.load().await {
1539            Ok(ToolExecutionState::Completed(outcome)) => return outcome.into_response(),
1540            Ok(ToolExecutionState::Unaudited(outcome)) => outcome,
1541            Ok(_) => return lifecycle_error("tool execution state changed during audit".to_owned()),
1542            Err(error) => return lifecycle_error(error),
1543        };
1544        let completion_permit = match state.worker.try_reserve(&execution.session_id) {
1545            Ok(permit) => permit,
1546            Err(error) => {
1547                return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::unavailable_source(error));
1548            }
1549        };
1550        let Some(session) = state.sessions.get(&execution.session_id) else {
1551            return lifecycle_error("tool session disappeared".to_owned());
1552        };
1553        return complete_tool_audit(&state, execution, outcome, completion_permit, session).await;
1554    }
1555    // Closes the concurrent-MCP budget
1556    // double-spend by threading the debited `payout_micros` out of
1557    // `ToolVerdict::Allowed` and calling `ActionBudget::refund_
1558    // tool_call` on the lost-claim branch. `refund` is best-effort
1559    // (backend errors are silently absorbed) so a Redis blip on the
1560    // compensation path cannot turn the CONFLICT response into 5xx.
1561    // Credential exchange is an authorization gate: finish it before the
1562    // sandbox charges budget or records an allowed verdict.
1563    let mut exchange_token = None;
1564    let mut preflight_denial = None;
1565    // A per-backend endpoint serves only its own backend's tools. The
1566    // refusal is an audited policy denial, decided before any budget spend.
1567    if let crate::mcp::Scope::Backend(name) = &scope {
1568        if let Ok(request) = pv_sandbox::parse_tool_call(&body) {
1569            let routed = state
1570                .backend_router
1571                .resolve(&request.tool)
1572                .map(|backend| backend.name.as_str());
1573            if routed != Some(name.as_str()) {
1574                let code = pv_sandbox::DenialCode::NoBackend;
1575                let reason = format!("tool {:?} is not served by backend {name:?}", request.tool);
1576                preflight_denial = Some(ToolVerdict::Blocked {
1577                    tool: request.tool.clone(),
1578                    stage: "policy",
1579                    policy: Some("backend.route".into()),
1580                    denial_code: code,
1581                    response: pv_sandbox::rpc::denial_error(request.id.as_ref(), code, &reason),
1582                    reason,
1583                    elapsed_us: 0,
1584                });
1585            }
1586        }
1587    }
1588    // External AuthZEN PDP: consulted only when the local intent map and
1589    // missions permit the call (a local denial is audited by the
1590    // intercept), before any budget is spent. Its denial is an audited
1591    // policy denial; an unreachable PDP fails closed with 503.
1592    if let (None, Some(authzen)) = (&preflight_denial, &state.authzen) {
1593        if let Ok(request) = pv_sandbox::parse_tool_call(&body) {
1594            let facts = authenticated.facts();
1595            let now_s = pv_core::time::now_ms() / 1000;
1596            if let crate::authz::AuthzDecision::Permit { intent } =
1597                state.pdp.decide_for(&request.tool, now_s, &facts)
1598            {
1599                let missions: Vec<String> = state
1600                    .pdp
1601                    .applicable_missions(&facts)
1602                    .into_iter()
1603                    .map(|mission| mission.id.clone())
1604                    .collect();
1605                let backend = state
1606                    .backend_router
1607                    .resolve(&request.tool)
1608                    .map(|backend| backend.name.as_str());
1609                let session = crate::pipeline::single_header(&headers, crate::pipeline::SESSION_HEADER)
1610                    .ok()
1611                    .flatten()
1612                    .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok());
1613                let evaluation = crate::authzen::evaluation_request(
1614                    &authenticated,
1615                    &request.tool,
1616                    &intent,
1617                    backend,
1618                    session,
1619                    &missions,
1620                    authzen.resources(),
1621                );
1622                match authzen.evaluate(&evaluation).await {
1623                    Ok(crate::authzen::AuthzenDecision::Permit) => {
1624                        state
1625                            .metrics
1626                            .counter(
1627                                "pv_authzen_decisions_total{decision=\"permit\"}",
1628                                "External AuthZEN decisions by outcome",
1629                            )
1630                            .inc();
1631                    }
1632                    Ok(crate::authzen::AuthzenDecision::Deny(reason)) => {
1633                        state
1634                            .metrics
1635                            .counter(
1636                                "pv_authzen_decisions_total{decision=\"deny\"}",
1637                                "External AuthZEN decisions by outcome",
