1638                            )
1639                            .inc();
1640                        let code = pv_sandbox::DenialCode::PdpDenied;
1641                        preflight_denial = Some(ToolVerdict::Blocked {
1642                            tool: request.tool.clone(),
1643                            stage: "policy",
1644                            policy: Some("pdp.authzen".into()),
1645                            denial_code: code,
1646                            response: pv_sandbox::rpc::denial_error(request.id.as_ref(), code, &reason),
1647                            reason,
1648                            elapsed_us: 0,
1649                        });
1650                    }
1651                    Err(error) => {
1652                        state
1653                            .metrics
1654                            .counter(
1655                                "pv_authzen_decisions_total{decision=\"error\"}",
1656                                "External AuthZEN decisions by outcome",
1657                            )
1658                            .inc();
1659                        tracing::warn!(%error, "external policy decision point unavailable; refusing the call");
1660                        return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::unavailable(
1661                            "the external policy decision point is unavailable; retry shortly".to_owned(),
1662                        ));
1663                    }
1664                }
1665            }
1666        }
1667    }
1668    if let (Some(execution), None) = (&execution, &preflight_denial) {
1669        if let Some(backend) = state
1670            .backend_router
1671            .resolve(&execution.tool)
1672            .filter(|backend| backend.auth_mode == crate::backend::BackendAuthMode::Exchange)
1673        {
1674            match exchange_for_backend(&state, &authenticated, &backend.name, &execution.tool) {
1675                Ok(token) => exchange_token = Some(token),
1676                Err(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::Blocked { context: reason, .. }) => {
1677                    let request = pv_sandbox::parse_tool_call(&body).ok();
1678                    let code = pv_sandbox::DenialCode::PolicyDenied;
1679                    preflight_denial = Some(ToolVerdict::Blocked {
1680                        tool: execution.tool.clone(),
1681                        stage: "policy",
1682                        policy: Some("backend.exchange".into()),
1683                        denial_code: code,
1684                        response: pv_sandbox::rpc::denial_error(
1685                            request.as_ref().and_then(|r| r.id.as_ref()),
1686                            code,
1687                            &reason,
1688                        ),
1689                        reason,
1690                        elapsed_us: 0,
1691                    });
1692                }
1693                Err(error) => return pipeline_error(error),
1694            }
1695        }
1696    }
1697    // Console-pushed transforms rewrite the arguments before the verdict
1698    // is taken, so every gate, the journal and the backend see the
1699    // rewritten call.
1700    let body = apply_pushed_tool_transforms(&state, body);
1701    // Kept for the intent token: the intercept consumes the caller.
1702    let intent_caller = authenticated.clone();
1703    match state
1704        .intercept_authenticated_nonblocking(&headers, &body, authenticated, preflight_denial)
1705        .await
1706    {
1707        Ok(ToolVerdict::Allowed {
1708            tool,
1709            budget_remaining,
1710            elapsed_us,
1711            payout_micros,
1712            principal_id,
1713        }) => {
1714            let resolved_backend = state.backend_router.resolve(&tool);
1715            if let Some(url) = resolved_backend
1716                .map(|b| b.url.as_str())
1717                .or(state.config.tool_upstream_url.as_deref())
1718            {
1719                let execution = match execution {
1720                    Some(execution) => execution,
1721                    None => return lifecycle_error("tool execution state is missing".to_owned()),
1722                };
1723                // The sandbox debited the budget when it returned Allowed —
1724                // on BOTH ledgers when a principal budget is bound. Every
1725                // failure between here and a successful `claim()` must
1726                // refund BOTH, or a saturated worker / close race / lost
1727                // claim drains `max_total_tool_calls` and payout headroom
1728                // (session AND principal — the principal ledger persists
1729                // across sessions, so a leak there never heals) with zero
1730                // tools executed; each client retry re-debits.
1731                let refund_admission =
1732                    || refund_tool_admission(&state, &execution, payout_micros, principal_id.as_deref());
1733                let now_s = pv_core::time::now_ms() / 1000;
1734                // The pipeline made (and audited) the PDP decision before
1735                // charging the budget; deciding again here could disagree
1736                // with that audit record, so only the intent is looked up.
1737                let intent = state.pdp.intent_for(&tool);
1738                let audience =
1739                    resolved_backend.map_or(crate::backend::DEFAULT_BACKEND_NAME, |b| b.name.as_str());
1740                let intent_token =
1741                    state
1742                        .pdp
1743                        .mint_intent_token(&tool, &intent, &intent_caller.facts(), audience, now_s);
1744                // The credential this backend (and only this backend)
1745                // receives, resolved before the execution is claimed so a
1746                // missing forwarded token fails without an uncertain claim.
1747                let credential: Option<(axum::http::HeaderName, HeaderValue)> =
1748                    if let Some(token) = &exchange_token {
1749                        crate::mcp::bearer_header(token)
1750                    } else if let Some(backend) = resolved_backend {
1751                        if backend.auth_mode == crate::backend::BackendAuthMode::ForwardToken {
1752                            let Some(header) = crate::mcp::caller_bearer(&headers) else {
1753                                if let Err(error) = refund_admission().await {
1754                                    return lifecycle_error(error);
1755                                }
1756                                return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::Unauthorized(
1757                                    "this backend requires the caller's bearer token".to_owned(),
1758                                ));
1759                            };
1760                            Some(header)
1761                        } else {
1762                            backend.auth_header.clone()
1763                        }
1764                    } else {
1765                        state
1766                            .tool_auth
1767                            .clone()
1768                            .map(|bearer| (axum::http::header::AUTHORIZATION, bearer))
1769                    };
1770                let intent_header = intent_token
1771                    .as_deref()
1772                    .and_then(|token| HeaderValue::from_str(token).ok())
1773                    .map(|value| (axum::http::HeaderName::from_static("x-pv-intent-token"), value));
1774                let _lease = match state.lease_session(&headers) {
1775                    Ok(lease) => lease,
1776                    Err(error) => {
1777                        if let Err(error) = refund_admission().await {
1778                            return lifecycle_error(error);
1779                        }
1780                        return pipeline_error(error);
1781                    }
1782                };
1783                let completion_permit = match state.worker.try_reserve(&execution.session_id) {
1784                    Ok(permit) => permit,
1785                    Err(error) => {
1786                        if let Err(error) = refund_admission().await {
1787                            return lifecycle_error(error);
1788                        }
1789                        return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::unavailable(
1790                            error.to_string(),
1791                        ));
1792                    }
1793                };
1794                match execution.claim().await {
1795                    Ok(()) => {}
1796                    Err(ClaimError::Race) => {
1797                        // A lost claim race means another in-flight request owns
1798                        // this execution; answer exactly like the Pending state
1799                        // and keep the underlying io detail out of the wire.
1800                        tracing::warn!(
1801                            session = %execution.session_id,
1802                            "concurrent tool execution claim lost; refunding budget"
1803                        );
1804                        // Refund the exact amount debited so
1805                        // the budget counters reflect only admitted work,
1806                        // not the lost race.
1807                        if let Err(error) = refund_admission().await {
1808                            return lifecycle_error(error);
1809                        }
1810                        return (
1811                            StatusCode::CONFLICT,
1812                            Json(json!({"error": TOOL_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN})),
1813                        )
1814                            .into_response();
1815                    }
1816                    Err(ClaimError::Backend(error)) => {
1817                        // Infrastructure failure — StorageFull, PermissionDenied,
1818                        // etc. The tool provably did not execute (we never
1819                        // reached upstream); refund the admission charge and
1820                        // surface a 503 so the client backs off, instead of a
1821                        // 409 that implies "someone else already ran it".
1822                        tracing::warn!(
1823                            session = %execution.session_id,
1824                            %error,
1825                            "tool execution claim failed; refunding budget"
1826                        );
1827                        if let Err(error) = refund_admission().await {
1828                            return lifecycle_error(error);
1829                        }
1830                        return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::unavailable(
1831                            "tool execution intent could not be persisted".to_owned(),
1832                        ));
1833                    }
1834                }
1835                // Once claimed, a failure to capture the result must poison
1836                // complete evidence before the session lease is released. A
1837                // successful durable outcome still follows the existing audit
1838                // retry path, including recoverable audited-marker failures.
1839                let mark_incomplete = || {
1840                    if let Some(session) = state.sessions.get(&execution.session_id) {
1841                        session.mark_capture_failed();
1842                    }
1843                };
1844                // A fixed request-local deadline follows the response
1845                // through body reads. Idle reads alone let a slow drip
1846                // occupy this detached task and its admission slot forever.
1847                let tool_timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(
1848                    state
1849                        .config
1850                        .mcp_request_timeout_s
1851                        .unwrap_or(crate::config::DEFAULT_MCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S),
1852                );
1853                if let Some(backend) = resolved_backend
1854                    .filter(|backend| backend.transport == crate::config::BackendTransport::Mcp)
1855                {
1856                    // MCP Streamable HTTP: the backend session of this
1857                    // agent session, SSE decoding, and one retry after a
1858                    // session-expiry 404 (see mcp_client.rs).
1859                    let request_id = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&body)
1860                        .ok()
1861                        .and_then(|request| request.get("id").cloned())
1862                        .unwrap_or(Value::Null);
1863                    let endpoint = crate::mcp_client::BackendEndpoint {
1864                        url: url.to_owned(),
1865                        auth: credential,
1866                        extra: intent_header.into_iter().collect(),
1867                        deadline: tokio::time::Instant::now() + tool_timeout,
1868                    };
1869                    let exchanged = state
1870                        .mcp_backends
1871                        .request(
1872                            &execution.session_id,
1873                            &backend.name,
1874                            &endpoint,
1875                            &body,
1876                            &request_id,
1877                        )
1878                        .await;
1879                    let outcome = match exchanged {
1880                        Ok((status, bytes, content_type)) => ToolOutcome {
1881                            status,
1882                            body_hex: hex::encode(&bytes),
1883                            content_type,
1884                        },
1885                        Err(crate::mcp_client::McpError::NotDelivered(category)) => {
1886                            // The call itself never reached the backend:
1887                            // release the claim and refund, exactly like a
1888                            // connect failure on the plain transport.
1889                            match execution.release_unexecuted().await {
1890                                Ok(()) => {
1891                                    if let Err(error) = refund_admission().await {
1892                                        return lifecycle_error(error);
1893                                    }
1894                                }
1895                                Err(release_error) => {
1896                                    mark_incomplete();
1897                                    tracing::warn!(
1898                                        session = %execution.session_id,
1899                                        error = %release_error,
1900                                        "failed to release undelivered MCP tool intent; charge kept, key stays claimed"
1901                                    );
1902                                }
1903                            }
1904                            return pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::upstream(format!(
1905                                "forward tool call: {category}"
1906                            )));
1907                        }
1908                        Err(crate::mcp_client::McpError::AfterDelivery(error)) => ToolOutcome {
1909                            status: StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY.as_u16(),
1910                            body_hex: hex::encode(
1911                                serde_json::to_vec(&json!({
1912                                    "error": format!("tool executed but its response could not be read: {error}"),
1913                                }))
1914                                .unwrap_or_default(),
1915                            ),
1916                            content_type: Some("application/json".to_owned()),
1917                        },
1918                    };
1919                    let gate = tool_audit_gate(&state, &execution.key);
1920                    let _gate = gate.lock().await;
1921                    if let Err(error) = execution.persist(&outcome).await {
1922                        mark_incomplete();
1923                        return lifecycle_error(error);
1924                    }
1925                    let Some(session) = state.sessions.get(&execution.session_id) else {
1926                        return lifecycle_error("tool session disappeared".to_owned());
1927                    };
1928                    return complete_tool_audit(&state, &execution, outcome, completion_permit, session)
1929                        .await;
1930                }
1931                let mut tool_request = state
1932                    .backend_client
1933                    .post(url)
1934                    .timeout(tool_timeout)
1935                    .header(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/json")
1936                    .body(body);
1937                if let Some((name, value)) = &credential {
1938                    tool_request = tool_request.header(name.clone(), value.clone());
1939                }
1940                if let Some((name, value)) = &intent_header {
1941                    tool_request = tool_request.header(name.clone(), value.clone());
1942                }
1943                match tool_request.send().await {
1944                    Ok(upstream) => {
1945                        let status = upstream.status();
1946                        // Reject non-identity
1947                        // Content-Encoding on the tool relay for the same
1948                        // reason the chat path does (reqwest 0.12 has no
1949                        // decompression features enabled). Without this
1950                        // guard the compressed bytes would be relayed to
1951                        // the MCP client with a plain application/json
1952                        // header, persisted as the durable ToolOutcome
1953                        // replayed on every retry, and journaled via
1954                        // from_utf8_lossy as the ATTESTED tool output —
1955                        // mojibake in the signed audit chain.
1956                        let upstream_headers = upstream.headers();
1957                        let mut refused_encoding: Option<(String, String)> = None;
1958                        'tool_encodings: for value in
1959                            upstream_headers.get_all(axum::http::header::CONTENT_ENCODING)
1960                        {
1961                            let raw = value.to_str().unwrap_or_default();
1962                            for token in raw.split(',') {
1963                                let token = token.trim();
1964                                if token.is_empty() || token.eq_ignore_ascii_case("identity") {
1965                                    continue;
1966                                }
1967                                refused_encoding = Some((token.to_owned(), raw.to_owned()));
1968                                break 'tool_encodings;
1969                            }
1970                        }
1971                        if let Some((token, raw)) = refused_encoding {
1972                            let failure = ToolOutcome {
1973                                status: StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY.as_u16(),
1974                                body_hex: hex::encode(
1975                                    serde_json::to_vec(&json!({
1976                                        "error": format!(
1977                                            "tool upstream responded with unsupported Content-Encoding token {token:?} (full header: {raw:?})",
1978                                        ),
1979                                    }))
1980                                    .unwrap_or_default(),
1981                                ),
1982                                content_type: Some("application/json".to_owned()),
1983                            };
1984                            let gate = tool_audit_gate(&state, &execution.key);
1985                            let _gate = gate.lock().await;
1986                            if let Err(error) = execution.persist(&failure).await {
1987                                mark_incomplete();
1988                                return lifecycle_error(error);
1989                            }
1990                            let session = match state.sessions.get(&execution.session_id) {
1991                                Some(session) => session,
1992                                None => return lifecycle_error("tool session disappeared".to_owned()),
1993                            };
1994                            return complete_tool_audit(
1995                                &state,
1996                                &execution,
1997                                failure,
1998                                completion_permit,
1999                                session,
2000                            )
2001                            .await;
2002                        }
2003                        match read_limited_tool_response(upstream).await {
2004                            Ok((bytes, content_type)) => {
2005                                let outcome = ToolOutcome {
2006                                    status: status.as_u16(),
2007                                    body_hex: hex::encode(&bytes),
2008                                    content_type,
2009                                };
2010                                // Hold the per-key gate across persist +
2011                                // audit so an Unaudited replay arriving
2012                                // between them serializes behind us and
2013                                // re-checks state instead of double-
2014                                // emitting the completion event.
2015                                let gate = tool_audit_gate(&state, &execution.key);
2016                                let _gate = gate.lock().await;
2017                                if let Err(error) = execution.persist(&outcome).await {
2018                                    mark_incomplete();
2019                                    return lifecycle_error(error);
2020                                }
2021                                let session = match state.sessions.get(&execution.session_id) {
2022                                    Some(session) => session,
2023                                    None => return lifecycle_error("tool session disappeared".to_owned()),
2024                                };
2025                                complete_tool_audit(&state, &execution, outcome, completion_permit, session)
2026                                    .await
2027                            }
2028                            Err(error) => {
2029                                // The upstream received the request and began
2030                                // responding: the tool executed (or may
2031                                // have). Record the failure as the outcome so
2032                                // the execution key resolves and the
2033                                // completion audit is emitted — otherwise the
2034                                // key strands at Pending (every retry gets
2035                                // 409) with an Allowed verdict and no
2036                                // completion on the audit stream, resolvable
2037                                // only by restart-time quarantine. `error`
2038                                // carries only the stable category / size
2039                                // text, never the upstream URL.
2040                                let failure = ToolOutcome {
2041                                    status: StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY.as_u16(),
2042                                    body_hex: hex::encode(
2043                                        serde_json::to_vec(&json!({
2044                                            "error": format!("tool executed but its response could not be read: {error}"),
2045                                        }))
2046                                        .unwrap_or_default(),
2047                                    ),
2048                                    content_type: Some("application/json".to_owned()),
2049                                };
2050                                let gate = tool_audit_gate(&state, &execution.key);
2051                                let _gate = gate.lock().await;
2052                                if execution.persist(&failure).await.is_ok() {
2053                                    if let Some(session) = state.sessions.get(&execution.session_id) {
2054                                        return complete_tool_audit(
2055                                            &state,
2056                                            &execution,
2057                                            failure,
2058                                            completion_permit,
2059                                            session,
2060                                        )
2061                                        .await;
2062                                    }
2063                                }
2064                                mark_incomplete();
2065                                pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::upstream(format!(
2066                                    "read tool response: {error}"
2067                                )))
2068                            }
2069                        }
2070                    }
2071                    Err(error) => {
2072                        // CWE-209: `reqwest::Error::Display` embeds the request URL —
2073                        // returning it verbatim would leak the operator-configured
2074                        // tool-upstream URL (potentially an internal hostname) to
2075                        // whichever client called `/mcp`. Report a stable category
2076                        // and preserve the raw detail server-side for operators.
2077                        //
2078                        // Also do not log the raw error to
2079                        // tracing::warn — `reqwest::Error::Display` embeds
2080                        // the same URL, and the tracing subscriber flows
2081                        // to Vector -> OTLP -> SIEM per the deploy
2082                        // topology. If OTLP is exported to a third party
2083                        // with a lower trust boundary than the operator,
2084                        // the internal `tool_upstream_url` leaks there.
2085                        // Log structured fields only.
2086                        let category = crate::pipeline::classify_upstream_error(&error);
2087                        tracing::warn!(
2088                            category = category,
2089                            error.status = ?error.status(),
2090                            error.is_timeout = error.is_timeout(),
2091                            error.is_connect = error.is_connect(),
2092                            error.is_request = error.is_request(),
2093                            "tool upstream forwarding failed"
2094                        );
2095                        // A connect failure means the connection never
2096                        // opened: the upstream provably did not execute the
2097                        // tool. Release the claimed execution key and refund
2098                        // the admission charge so the client's retry is
2099                        // clean, instead of stranded at "outcome uncertain"
2100                        // with a burned budget slot. Release-then-refund
2101                        // ordering: a crash between the two leaves the
2102                        // charge in place (conservative) rather than a
2103                        // refunded-but-claimed key. Timeout/read/request
2104                        // failures stay claimed — the tool may have executed.
2105                        if error.is_connect() {
2106                            match execution.release_unexecuted().await {
2107                                Ok(()) => {
2108                                    if let Err(error) = refund_admission().await {
2109                                        return lifecycle_error(error);
2110                                    }
2111                                }
2112                                Err(release_error) => {
2113                                    mark_incomplete();
2114                                    tracing::warn!(
2115                                        session = %execution.session_id,
2116                                        error = %release_error,
2117                                        "failed to release unexecuted tool intent; charge kept, key stays claimed"
2118                                    );
2119                                }
2120                            }
2121                        } else {
2122                            // No headers does not prove the tool never executed.
2123                            // Preserve its durable claim and the charged budget.
2124                            mark_incomplete();
2125                        }
2126                        // Upstream faults must surface as 502 (as the chat
2127                        // relay does), not 500: a 500 blames the harness and
2128                        // misroutes operator alerting/retry policy.
2129                        pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::upstream(format!(
2130                            "forward tool call: {category}"
2131                        )))
2132                    }
2133                }
2134            } else {
2135                // verdict-only mode must
2136                // return a conformant JSON-RPC response — the Blocked
2137                // arm already does (id echo + error object), so a
2138                // client could correlate failures but not successes.
2139                // Echo the request id (string/number/null per spec).
2140                let request_id = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&body)
2141                    .ok()
2142                    .and_then(|request| request.get("id").cloned())
2143                    .unwrap_or(Value::Null);
2144                (
2145                    StatusCode::OK,
2146                    Json(json!({
2147                        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
2148                        "id": request_id,
2149                        "result": {
2150                            "allowed": true,
2151                            "tool": tool,
2152                            "budget_remaining": budget_remaining,
2153                            "decision_us": elapsed_us,
2154                        },
2155                    })),
2156                )
2157                    .into_response()
2158            }
2159        }
2160        Ok(ToolVerdict::Blocked { response, stage, .. }) => {
2161            // A request that never parsed
2162            // (stage "parse") gets 400, not 403 — no authorization
2163            // decision was made. Policy/schema/budget refusals keep 403.
2164            let status = if stage == "parse" {
2165                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST
2166            } else {
2167                StatusCode::FORBIDDEN
2168            };
2169            (status, Json(response)).into_response()
2170        }
2171        Err(error) => pipeline_error(error),
2172        // `ToolVerdict` is `#[non_exhaustive]` (R56 SemVer-hardening).
2173        // A future variant reaching this matcher must fail closed:
2174        // emit a 503 with a stable message rather than silently
2175        // returning success. Mirrors the pipeline-level unhandled-
2176        // verdict handling at pipeline.rs's `check_with_principal`
2177        // matcher, so both entry points to the tool sandbox agree on
2178        // the defensive posture.
2179        Ok(_) => {
2180            tracing::error!(
2181                "unhandled ToolVerdict variant reached routes::tool_forward; failing closed. \
2182                 This is a bug — extend the match to handle the new variant."
2183            );
2184            pipeline_error(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::unavailable(
2185                "tool sandbox produced an unhandled verdict; refusing to proceed".to_owned(),
2186            ))
2187        }
2188    }
2189}
2190
2191const MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
2192
2193/// Capture and preserve the upstream tool response's
2194/// `Content-Type` so the MCP client sees exactly what the tool
2195/// upstream sent. Without this, `Bytes: IntoResponse` stamps
2196/// `application/octet-stream`, which strict JSON-RPC 2.0 clients
2197/// (spec: MUST be `application/json`) reject and downstream SIEM
2198/// filters mis-classify as binary. We store the string (not
2199/// HeaderValue) so it round-trips through the on-disk `ToolOutcome`
2200/// journal for cached-outcome replay.
2201async fn read_limited_tool_response(response: reqwest::Response) -> Result<(Bytes, Option<String>), String> {
2202    let content_type = response
2203        .headers()
2204        .get(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE)
2205        .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
2206        .map(str::to_owned);
2207    let mut stream = response.bytes_stream();
2208    let mut body = Vec::new();
2209    while let Some(chunk) = stream.next().await {
2210        // CWE-209: `reqwest::Error::Display` embeds the request URL — leaking
2211        // the operator-configured tool-upstream URL to the client if we
2212        // returned it verbatim. Use the stable classifier and log
2213        // structured fields for operators (never `%error`
2214        // — that renders the URL into any downstream OTLP sink).
2215        let chunk = chunk.map_err(|error| {
2216            let category = crate::pipeline::classify_upstream_error(&error);
2217            tracing::warn!(
2218                category = category,
2219                error.status = ?error.status(),
2220                error.is_timeout = error.is_timeout(),
2221                error.is_connect = error.is_connect(),
2222                error.is_body = error.is_body(),
2223                "tool upstream stream chunk failed"
2224            );
2225            category.to_owned()
2226        })?;
2227        let next = body
2228            .len()
2229            .checked_add(chunk.len())
2230            .ok_or_else(|| "tool response size overflow".to_owned())?;
2231        if next > MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_BYTES {
2232            return Err(format!("tool response exceeds {MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_BYTES} bytes"));
2233        }
2234        body.extend_from_slice(&chunk);
2235    }
2236    Ok((Bytes::from(body), content_type))
2237}
2238
2239/// Build a tool-response with the upstream Content-Type
2240/// preserved. Defaults to `application/json` — MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0
2241/// by convention — when the upstream did not set one or set an
2242/// unrepresentable value.
2243fn tool_response(status: StatusCode, bytes: Bytes, content_type: Option<&str>) -> Response {
2244    let mut response = (status, bytes).into_response();
2245    let value = content_type
2246        .and_then(|ct| HeaderValue::from_str(ct).ok())
2247        .unwrap_or_else(|| HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"));
2248    response
2249        .headers_mut()
2250        .insert(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE, value);
2251    // The MCP relay forwards the tool upstream's
2252    // Content-Type verbatim; pin nosniff exactly like the chat relay
2253    // so a rogue tool upstream flipping the type to
2254    // text/html cannot get attacker-echoed bytes rendered by a
2255    // browser-side MIME sniff.
2256    response.headers_mut().insert(
2257        axum::http::HeaderName::from_static("x-content-type-options"),
2258        HeaderValue::from_static("nosniff"),
2259    );
2260    response
2261}
2262
2263async fn complete_tool_audit(
2264    state: &AppState,
2265    execution: &ToolExecution,
2266    outcome: ToolOutcome,
2267    completion_permit: crate::worker::WorkerPermit,
2268    session: Arc<crate::session::Session>,
2269) -> Response {
2270    let status = StatusCode::from_u16(outcome.status).unwrap_or(StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY);
2271    let bytes = match decode_cached_tool_body(&outcome.body_hex) {
2272        Ok(bytes) => bytes,
2273        Err(response) => return *response,
2274    };
2275    let success = status.is_success();
2276    // If a prior attempt in this process already journaled the completion
2277    // event but failed to write the `.audited` marker, re-attempt only the
2278    // marker — re-submitting the job would put a second execution record
2279    // (with a fresh event uid) on the audit stream and in the signed chain.
2280    let already_emitted = state.tool_audits_emitted.lock().contains(&execution.key);
2281    if !already_emitted {
2282        completion_permit.submit(crate::worker::WorkerJob {
2283            session: Arc::clone(&session),
2284            identity: session.current_identity(),
2285            class: pv_events::EventClass::Session,
2286            payload: json!({
2287                "action": "tool_completed",
2288                "tool": &execution.tool,
2289                "execution_key": &execution.key,
2290                "status": status.as_u16(),
2291                "response_sha256": pv_core::digest::sha256_hex(&bytes),
2292            }),
2293            text: String::new(),
2294            analyze_loop: false,
2295            status: if success {
2296                pv_events::StatusId::Success
2297            } else {
2298                pv_events::StatusId::Failure
2299            },
2300            stop_reason: (!success).then_some(StopReason::Other),
2301            native_stop_reason: None,
2302            metrics: pv_events::EventMetrics::default(),
2303            cost_usd_micros: 0,
2304            prompt_token_correction: 0,
2305            atif: Some(crate::worker::AtifCapture {
2306                source: pv_atif::Source::System,
2307                message: Value::String(String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned()),
2308                reasoning_content: None,
2309                model_name: None,
2310                tool_calls: None,
2311                observation: None,
2312                llm_call_count: None,
2313            }),
2314            response_marker: None,
2315            response_attempt: None,
2316        });
2317        session.wait_for_worker_jobs().await;
2318        if session.capture_failed() {
2319            return lifecycle_error("tool completed but completion audit failed".to_owned());
2320        }
2321        // The event is durably journaled; remember that before attempting
2322        // the marker so a marker failure retries without re-emitting.
2323        state.tool_audits_emitted.lock().insert(execution.key.clone());
2324    }
2325    if let Err(error) = execution.mark_audited().await {
2326        return lifecycle_error(error);
2327    }
2328    state.tool_audits_emitted.lock().remove(&execution.key);
2329    // Preserve the upstream Content-Type so a spec-
2330    // conforming JSON-RPC 2.0 client sees `application/json`
2331    // (default) or whatever the tool upstream declared, not axum's
2332    // `application/octet-stream`.
2333    tool_response(status, bytes, outcome.content_type.as_deref())
2334}
2335
2336#[derive(Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
2337struct ToolOutcome {
2338    status: u16,
2339    body_hex: String,
2340    /// MCP client requires the upstream tool response's
2341    /// `Content-Type` to round-trip on cached-outcome replay too, so
2342    /// strict JSON-RPC 2.0 clients see `application/json` on replay
2343    /// just as they did on the fresh forward. `#[serde(default)]` so
2344    /// journals persisted before the field existed decode as `None`
2345    /// (which the response builder will map to the JSON default).
2346    #[serde(default)]
2347    content_type: Option<String>,
2348}
2349
2350impl ToolOutcome {
2351    fn into_response(self) -> Response {
2352        let status = StatusCode::from_u16(self.status).unwrap_or(StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY);
2353        match decode_cached_tool_body(&self.body_hex) {
2354            Ok(body) => tool_response(status, body, self.content_type.as_deref()),
2355            Err(response) => *response,
2356        }
2357    }
2358}
2359
2360/// Decode a MAC-sealed cached tool outcome's `body_hex` payload into
2361/// wire bytes. Shared by both consumers — `ToolOutcome::into_response`
2362/// (the Completed fast-path replay) and `complete_tool_audit` (the
2363/// Unaudited path that runs the completion-audit job) — so a future
2364/// refactor cannot asymmetrically regress the leak-free error
2365/// contract on one branch while preserving it on the other.
2366///
2367/// The body_hex is server-authored + MAC-sealed by
2368/// `ToolExecution::load` (which opens the outcome file through
2369/// `crate::journal::open` under the MAC `TOOL_OUTCOME_DOMAIN`), so a
2370/// decode failure implies either a control-key compromise or an
2371/// on-disk MAC bypass — not attacker-influencable from the wire.
2372/// Even so, echoing the `hex::FromHexError` Display (which includes
2373/// the offending byte offset and hex character) leaks internal
2374/// spool detail into the client-facing 500 body. Return a stable
2375/// string on the wire; log the decode error separately at
2376/// `tracing::error!` so operators still get the diagnostic without
2377/// the client seeing it.
2378///
2379/// Returns `Err(Box<Response>)` on failure rather than `Err(Response)`
2380/// so the discriminant stays small (`clippy::result_large_err`).
2381fn decode_cached_tool_body(body_hex: &str) -> Result<Bytes, Box<Response>> {
2382    match hex::decode(body_hex) {
2383        Ok(bytes) => Ok(Bytes::from(bytes)),
2384        Err(error) => {
2385            tracing::error!(
2386                %error,
2387                "cached tool outcome body_hex failed to decode; \
2388                 possible control-key compromise or on-disk MAC bypass"
2389            );
2390            Err(Box::new(lifecycle_error(
2391                "cached tool outcome is corrupt".to_owned(),
2392            )))
2393        }
2394    }
2395}
2396
2397enum ToolExecutionState {
2398    Missing,
2399    Pending,
2400    Unaudited(ToolOutcome),
2401    Completed(ToolOutcome),
2402}
2403
2404/// Two distinct failure modes for `ToolExecution::claim` that must
2405/// produce different client responses. Previously
2406/// `claim_sync` mapped ALL failures to a `String` and the caller in
2407/// `mcp_call_inner` answered every one with `409 TOOL_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`
2408/// — reporting infrastructure faults (StorageFull, PermissionDenied,
2409/// ReadOnlyFilesystem, Interrupted) as if the client had lost a
2410/// concurrent race, so retries looped on the underlying disk fault
2411/// while the client learned nothing useful.
2412#[derive(Debug)]
2413enum ClaimError {
2414    /// The intent file already existed (`create_new` returned
2415    /// `AlreadyExists`). Another in-flight request owns this
2416    /// execution key — the legitimate race case that `409
2417    /// TOOL_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` was designed for.
2418    Race,
2419    /// An I/O or MAC-seal failure independent of concurrent claim
2420    /// contention. Maps to a 5xx so operators are alerted to a real
2421    /// infrastructure problem instead of retrying on false uncertainty.
2422    Backend(String),
2423}
2424
2425const TOOL_REQUEST_MISMATCH: &str = "JSON-RPC id is already bound to a different tool request or principal";
2426/// Canonical duplicate-execution refusal, shared by the pre-flight Pending
2427/// state and a lost concurrent claim race so neither reveals more than the
2428/// other (a raw claim error would leak filesystem detail, CWE-209).
2429const TOOL_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN: &str = "tool execution outcome is uncertain; refusing duplicate execution";
2430
2431/// Read-only lifecycle barrier. Unlike startup recovery, this check never
2432/// renames incomplete evidence belonging to another concurrent live request.
2433pub(crate) async fn ensure_tool_executions_resolved(
2434    spool: &std::path::Path,
2435    session_id: &str,
2436    control_key: &[u8; 32],
2437) -> Result<(), String> {
2438    let directory = spool.join(crate::spool::TOOL_EXECUTIONS);
2439    let session_id = session_id.to_owned();
2440    let control_key = *control_key;
2441    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
2442        ensure_tool_executions_resolved_with_limit(
2443            &directory,
2444            &session_id,
2445            &control_key,
2446            crate::reconciler::MAX_RECOVERY_DIRENTS_PER_TICK,
2447        )
2448    })
2449    .await
2450    .map_err(|_| "tool evidence lookup task failed".to_owned())?
2451}
2452
2453fn ensure_tool_executions_resolved_with_limit(
2454    directory: &std::path::Path,
2455    session_id: &str,
2456    control_key: &[u8; 32],
2457    max_dirents: usize,
2458) -> Result<(), String> {
2459    let entries = match crate::spool::list_tool_executions(directory, max_dirents) {
2460        Ok(entries) => entries,
2461        Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),
2462        Err(_) => return Err("tool evidence directory is unavailable".to_owned()),
2463    };
2464    if entries.len() > max_dirents {
2465        return Err("tool evidence directory exceeds the bounded scan limit".to_owned());
2466    }
2467    for path in entries {
2468        let Some(name) = path.file_name().and_then(std::ffi::OsStr::to_str) else {
2469            continue;
2470        };
2471        let Some(key) = name.strip_suffix(crate::spool::TOOL_INTENT_SUFFIX) else {
2472            continue;
2473        };
2474        let bytes = match crate::spool::read_tool_intent(&path) {
2475            Ok(bytes) => bytes,
2476            // Listed, then gone: another session's close archived its own
2477            // intent between the listing and this read. That intent is
2478            // resolved, and it was not this session's (this session is
2479            // closing here). Concurrent closes, such as shutdown's, hit
2480            // this; failing would leave the session for recovery.
2481            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => continue,
2482            Err(_) => return Err("tool execution intent is unavailable".to_owned()),
2483        };
2484        let intent: ToolIntent = crate::journal::open(
2485            control_key,
2486            &format!("{}:{key}", crate::journal::TOOL_INTENT_DOMAIN),
2487            0,
2488            &bytes,
2489        )
2490        .map_err(|_| "tool execution intent could not be authenticated".to_owned())?;
2491        if intent.execution_key != key {
2492            return Err("tool intent path does not match its authenticated key".to_owned());
2493        }
2494        if intent.session_id == session_id && !tool_completion_is_authenticated(directory, key, control_key) {
2495            return Err("tool execution outcome or completion audit is unresolved".to_owned());
2496        }
2497    }
2498    Ok(())
2499}
2500
2501/// A capture-failed close may archive only independently authenticated
2502/// completed tool records. Callers authenticate the intent and session first.
2503/// Missing, corrupt or unreadable evidence remains active for recovery.
2504pub(crate) fn tool_completion_is_authenticated(
2505    directory: &std::path::Path,
2506    key: &str,
2507    control_key: &[u8; 32],
2508) -> bool {
2509    let outcome_path = directory.join(format!("{key}{}", crate::spool::TOOL_OUTCOME_SUFFIX));
2510    let Ok(outcome_bytes) = pv_core::fsutil::read_capped(&outcome_path, pv_core::fsutil::MAX_ATIF_BYTES)
2511    else {
2512        return false;
2513    };
2514    if crate::journal::open::<ToolOutcome>(
2515        control_key,
2516        &format!("{}:{key}", crate::journal::TOOL_OUTCOME_DOMAIN),
2517        0,
2518        &outcome_bytes,
2519    )
2520    .is_err()
2521    {
2522        return false;
2523    }
2524    let audited_path = directory.join(format!("{key}{}", crate::spool::TOOL_AUDITED_SUFFIX));
2525    let Ok(audited_bytes) = pv_core::fsutil::read_capped(&audited_path, pv_core::fsutil::MAX_CONTROL_BYTES)
2526    else {
2527        return false;
2528    };
2529    crate::journal::open::<serde_json::Value>(
2530        control_key,
2531        &format!("{}:{key}", crate::journal::TOOL_AUDITED_DOMAIN),
2532        0,
2533        &audited_bytes,
2534    )
2535    .is_ok()
2536}
2537
2538#[derive(PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
2539struct ToolIntent {
2540    pub(crate) execution_key: String,
2541    pub(crate) session_id: String,
2542    pub(crate) tool: String,
2543    pub(crate) request_digest: String,
2544    pub(crate) principal_digest: String,
2545}
2546
2547#[cfg(test)]
2548pub(crate) async fn ensure_no_unresolved_tool_executions(
2549    spool: &std::path::Path,
2550    control_key: &[u8; 32],
2551) -> Result<(), String> {
2552    let sessions = unresolved_tool_sessions(spool, control_key).await?;
2553    if let Some(session_id) = sessions.into_iter().next() {
2554        Err(format!("session {session_id} has an unresolved tool execution"))
2555    } else {
2556        Ok(())
2557    }
2558}
2559
2560pub(crate) async fn unresolved_tool_sessions(
2561    spool: &std::path::Path,
2562    control_key: &[u8; 32],
2563) -> Result<std::collections::HashSet<String>, String> {
2564    let directory = spool.join(crate::spool::TOOL_EXECUTIONS);
2565    let control_key = *control_key;
2566    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
2567        let entries = match crate::spool::list_tool_executions(
2568            &directory,
2569            crate::reconciler::MAX_RECOVERY_DIRENTS_PER_TICK,
2570        ) {
2571            Ok(entries) => entries,
2572            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
2573                return Ok(std::collections::HashSet::new());
2574            }
2575            Err(error) => return Err(error.to_string()),
2576        };
2577        let mut intent_keys = std::collections::HashSet::new();
2578        let mut unresolved_sessions = std::collections::HashSet::new();
2579        let mut dirents_seen = 0usize;
2580        for path in entries {
2581            // Dirent cap: every other spool scan bounds its directory
2582            // walk (MAX_RECOVERY_DIRENTS_PER_TICK); this one also
2583            // accumulates one HashSet key per `*.intent.json` name
2584            // BEFORE MAC validation, so a poisoned directory with
2585            // millions of planted names meant unbounded memory + CPU
2586            // on every recovery tick and every session close. Unlike
2587            // the per-tick scans, a TRUNCATED result here is unsafe —
2588            // callers use it to prove "no unresolved executions"
2589            // before finalizing — so fail closed instead of returning
2590            // a partial set: the close refuses, and the operator sees
2591            // the poisoned directory instead of a silently incomplete
2592            // audit.
2593            dirents_seen = dirents_seen.saturating_add(1);
2594            if dirents_seen > crate::reconciler::MAX_RECOVERY_DIRENTS_PER_TICK {
2595                return Err(format!(
2596                    "tool-executions scan aborted: more than {} directory entries; \
2597                     the spool directory is poisoned or leaking files",
2598                    crate::reconciler::MAX_RECOVERY_DIRENTS_PER_TICK
2599                ));
2600            }
2601            let Some(name) = path.file_name().and_then(std::ffi::OsStr::to_str) else {
2602                continue;
2603            };
2604            let Some(key) = name.strip_suffix(crate::spool::TOOL_INTENT_SUFFIX) else {
2605                continue;
2606            };
2607            intent_keys.insert(key.to_owned());
2608            // A torn intent (crash between create_new and sync_all in
2609            // claim_sync) leaves a 0-byte or partial file at the final
2610            // intent_path. If we bubble the journal::open error via `?`
2611            // the recovery loop aborts on the first torn intent and
2612            // every subsequent tool session stays unrecovered
2613            // indefinitely. Quarantine the file so the reconciler makes
2614            // progress on the rest of the spool; the tool execution
2615            // itself is still uncertain — a subsequent retry by the
2616            // client will get TOOL_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN and can decide.
2617            // Bounded read: every other recovery scan reads spool files
2618            // through `read_capped` — these three reads were the
2619            // unbounded stragglers, so one planted multi-GB file under
2620            // `tool_executions/` could stall or OOM startup recovery.
2621            // Cap-class failures (oversize, non-regular file) route to
2622            // the same quarantine arm as a torn MAC so the scan keeps
2623            // making progress; only genuine IO faults abort.
2624            let intent_check: Result<ToolIntent, String> = match crate::spool::read_tool_intent(&path) {
2625                Ok(intent_bytes) => crate::journal::open(
2626                    &control_key,
2627                    &format!("{}:{key}", crate::journal::TOOL_INTENT_DOMAIN),
2628                    0,
2629                    &intent_bytes,
2630                ),
2631                // The session's close legitimately removes its tool-execution
2632                // files between the directory listing and this read.
2633                Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
2634                    intent_keys.remove(key);
2635                    continue;
2636                }
2637                Err(error)
2638                    if matches!(
2639                        error.kind(),
2640                        std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData | std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput
2641                    ) =>
2642                {
2643                    Err(error.to_string())
2644                }
2645                Err(error) => return Err(error.to_string()),
2646            };
2647            let intent: ToolIntent = match intent_check {
2648                Ok(intent) => intent,
2649                Err(error) => {
2650                    // Build
2651                    // the quarantine name EXPLICITLY. The prior use
2652                    // of `path.with_extension("intent.torn")` on a
2653                    // `<key>.intent.json` path replaces only the
2654                    // `json` component and produces
2655                    // `<key>.intent.intent.torn` — the ugly
2656                    // double-`intent` form. Explicit join gives the
2657                    // clean `<key>.intent.torn` name that
2658                    // remove_tool_executions's defense-in-depth
2659                    // cleanup expects.
2660                    let file_name = path
2661                        .file_stem()
2662                        .and_then(std::ffi::OsStr::to_str)
2663                        .and_then(|stem| stem.strip_suffix(".intent"))
2664                        .map(|key| format!("{key}.intent.torn"));
2665                    let quarantine = match file_name {
2666                        Some(name) => path.with_file_name(name),
2667                        None => path.with_extension("intent.torn"),
2668                    };
2669                    tracing::warn!(
2670                        %error,
2671                        original = %pv_core::fsutil::basename(&path),
2672                        quarantine = %pv_core::fsutil::basename(&quarantine),
2673                        "torn tool-execution intent quarantined so recovery can proceed"
2674                    );
2675                    if let Err(rename_err) = crate::spool::change_tool_executions(&directory, || {
2676                        std::fs::rename(&path, &quarantine)
2677                    }) {
2678                        tracing::warn!(%rename_err, "failed to quarantine torn intent — leaving in place");
2679                    }
2680                    // Also quarantine the outcome
2681                    // and audited siblings. Leaving them behind trips
2682                    // the orphan-outcome check below in the same tick
2683                    // and every tick thereafter, permanently stalling
2684                    // recovery — the exact brick this quarantine
2685                    // discipline exists to prevent.
2686                    quarantine_orphan_sibling(&directory, key, crate::spool::TOOL_OUTCOME_SUFFIX, "outcome");
2687                    quarantine_orphan_sibling(&directory, key, crate::spool::TOOL_AUDITED_SUFFIX, "audited");
2688                    intent_keys.remove(key);
2689                    continue;
2690                }
2691            };
2692            if intent.execution_key != key {
2693                return Err("tool intent path does not match authenticated execution key".to_owned());
2694            }
2695            let outcome_path = directory.join(format!("{key}{}", crate::spool::TOOL_OUTCOME_SUFFIX));
2696            // NotFound between the exists-style check and the read: the
2697            // outcome is genuinely absent (or was GC'd with its session's
2698            // close mid-scan) — record unresolved and move on rather than
2699            // aborting the whole recovery pass. Cap: a legitimate outcome
2700            // carries up to MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_BYTES hex-encoded (~2×), so
2701            // MAX_ATIF_BYTES (64 MiB) clears every legal blob while still
2702            // refusing a planted multi-GB file (routed to quarantine).
2703            let outcome_check: Result<ToolOutcome, String> =
2704                match pv_core::fsutil::read_capped(&outcome_path, pv_core::fsutil::MAX_ATIF_BYTES) {
2705                    Ok(outcome_bytes) => crate::journal::open(
2706                        &control_key,
2707                        &format!("{}:{key}", crate::journal::TOOL_OUTCOME_DOMAIN),
2708                        0,
2709                        &outcome_bytes,
2710                    ),
2711                    Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
2712                        unresolved_sessions.insert(intent.session_id);
2713                        continue;
2714                    }
2715                    Err(error)
2716                        if matches!(
2717                            error.kind(),
2718                            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData | std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput
2719                        ) =>
2720                    {
2721                        Err(error.to_string())
2722                    }
2723                    Err(error) => return Err(error.to_string()),
2724                };
2725            let _: ToolOutcome = match outcome_check {
2726                Ok(outcome) => outcome,
2727                Err(error) => {
2728                    // warn+quarantine the unverifiable
2729                    // outcome (and any sibling audited file) instead of
2730                    // aborting the whole recovery pass and bricking the
2731                    // startup.
2732                    tracing::warn!(
2733                        %error,
2734                        key = %key,
2735                        "torn tool-execution outcome quarantined so recovery can proceed"
2736                    );
2737                    quarantine_orphan_sibling(&directory, key, crate::spool::TOOL_OUTCOME_SUFFIX, "outcome");
2738                    quarantine_orphan_sibling(&directory, key, crate::spool::TOOL_AUDITED_SUFFIX, "audited");
2739                    unresolved_sessions.insert(intent.session_id);
2740                    continue;
2741                }
2742            };
2743            let audited_path = directory.join(format!("{key}{}", crate::spool::TOOL_AUDITED_SUFFIX));
2744            let audited_check: Result<serde_json::Value, String> =
2745                match pv_core::fsutil::read_capped(&audited_path, pv_core::fsutil::MAX_CONTROL_BYTES) {
2746                    Ok(audited_bytes) => crate::journal::open(
2747                        &control_key,
2748                        &format!("{}:{key}", crate::journal::TOOL_AUDITED_DOMAIN),
2749                        0,
2750                        &audited_bytes,
2751                    ),
2752                    Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
2753                        unresolved_sessions.insert(intent.session_id);
2754                        continue;
2755                    }
2756                    Err(error)
2757                        if matches!(
2758                            error.kind(),
2759                            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData | std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput
2760                        ) =>
2761                    {
2762                        Err(error.to_string())
2763                    }
2764                    Err(error) => return Err(error.to_string()),
2765                };
2766            let _: serde_json::Value = match audited_check {
2767                Ok(value) => value,
2768                Err(error) => {
2769                    tracing::warn!(
2770                        %error,
2771                        key = %key,
2772                        "torn tool-execution audited record quarantined so recovery can proceed"
2773                    );
2774                    quarantine_orphan_sibling(&directory, key, crate::spool::TOOL_AUDITED_SUFFIX, "audited");
2775                    unresolved_sessions.insert(intent.session_id);
2776                    continue;
2777                }
2778            };
2779        }
2780        let mut orphan_dirents = 0usize;
2781        let orphan_entries =
2782            crate::spool::list_tool_executions(&directory, crate::reconciler::MAX_RECOVERY_DIRENTS_PER_TICK)
2783                .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
2784        for path in orphan_entries {
2785            // Same fail-closed dirent cap as the intent pass above.
2786            orphan_dirents = orphan_dirents.saturating_add(1);
2787            if orphan_dirents > crate::reconciler::MAX_RECOVERY_DIRENTS_PER_TICK {
2788                return Err(format!(
2789                    "tool-executions orphan scan aborted: more than {} directory entries; \
2790                     the spool directory is poisoned or leaking files",
2791                    crate::reconciler::MAX_RECOVERY_DIRENTS_PER_TICK
2792                ));
2793            }
2794            let Some(name) = path.file_name().and_then(std::ffi::OsStr::to_str) else {
2795                continue;
2796            };
2797            if let Some(key) = name.strip_suffix(crate::spool::TOOL_OUTCOME_SUFFIX) {
2798                // Checked again in a turn: a call that claimed its intent
2799                // after the first listing has a live outcome, not an orphan.
2800                let intent = directory.join(format!("{key}{}", crate::spool::TOOL_INTENT_SUFFIX));
2801                if !intent_keys.contains(key)
2802                    && !crate::spool::change_tool_executions(&directory, || intent.exists())
2803                {
2804                    // An orphan outcome must not
2805                    // return Err — that turns the recovery tick into a
2806                    // permanent brick, especially at boot where
2807                    // recover_spooled_sessions is fatal. Rename the
2808                    // outcome (and any sibling audited) to a
2809                    // `.corrupt-*` name so nothing scans them again.
2810                    tracing::warn!(
2811                        key = %key,
2812                        "orphan tool outcome without authenticated intent quarantined"
2813                    );
2814                    quarantine_orphan_sibling(&directory, key, crate::spool::TOOL_OUTCOME_SUFFIX, "outcome");
2815                    quarantine_orphan_sibling(&directory, key, crate::spool::TOOL_AUDITED_SUFFIX, "audited");
2816                }
2817            }
2818        }
2819        Ok(unresolved_sessions)
2820    })
2821    .await
2822    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
2823}
2824
2825/// Rename `<directory>/<key><suffix>` to a `.corrupt-<uid>` name so
2826/// nothing else scans it. Silent-ok when the sibling doesn't exist
2827/// (the common case).
2828fn quarantine_orphan_sibling(directory: &std::path::Path, key: &str, suffix: &str, role: &str) {
2829    let path = directory.join(format!("{key}{suffix}"));
2830    if !path.exists() {
2831        return;
2832    }
2833    let uid = pv_core::new_event_uid();
2834    let quarantine = directory.join(format!("{key}{suffix}.corrupt-{uid}"));
2835    if let Err(rename_err) =
2836        crate::spool::change_tool_executions(directory, || std::fs::rename(&path, &quarantine))
2837    {
2838        tracing::warn!(
2839            %rename_err,
2840            role = %role,
2841            original = %pv_core::fsutil::basename(&path),
2842            "failed to quarantine orphan tool-execution sibling — leaving in place"
2843        );
2844    } else {
2845        tracing::warn!(
2846            role = %role,
2847            original = %pv_core::fsutil::basename(&path),
2848            quarantine = %pv_core::fsutil::basename(&quarantine),
2849            "orphan tool-execution sibling quarantined"
2850        );
2851    }
2852}
2853
2854#[derive(Clone)]
2855struct ToolExecution {
2856    key: String,
2857    session_id: String,
2858    tool: String,
2859    request_digest: String,
2860    principal_digest: String,
2861    control_key: [u8; 32],
2862    intent_path: std::path::PathBuf,
2863    outcome_path: std::path::PathBuf,
2864    audited_path: std::path::PathBuf,
2865}
2866
2867impl ToolExecution {
2868    /// The tool-execution folder this execution's files are in.
2869    fn directory(&self) -> &std::path::Path {
2870        self.intent_path.parent().unwrap_or(std::path::Path::new(""))
2871    }
2872
2873    fn from_request(
2874        spool: &str,
2875        headers: &HeaderMap,
2876        body: &[u8],
2877        control_key: [u8; 32],
2878    ) -> Result<Self, crate::pipeline::PipelineError> {
2879        // Refuse duplicate x-pv-session headers (see
2880        // `pipeline::single_header` for the rationale — proxies
2881        // sometimes merge duplicates on the wire and log aggregators
2882        // can then observe a comma-joined value that leaks a
2883        // client-desync into audit).
2884        // Distinguish "header not present" from "header value is not
2885        // valid UTF-8 text" — the chat path at pipeline.rs::session_id
2886        // emits the specific "X-PV-Session is not valid text" 400 for
2887        // the non-UTF-8 case, and the tool path historically reported
2888        // the same non-UTF-8 case as "missing" — misleading operator
2889        // triage. Same discipline as the chat path now.
2890        let raw_header = crate::pipeline::single_header(headers, crate::pipeline::SESSION_HEADER)?;
2891        let session_id = match raw_header {
2892            None => {
2893                return Err(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request(
2894                    "missing x-pv-session".to_owned(),
2895                ));
2896            }
2897            Some(value) => value.to_str().map_err(|_| {
2898                crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request("X-PV-Session is not valid text".to_owned())
2899            })?,
2900        };
2901        // Same validation as the pipeline's `session_id`: an id the intercept
2902        // path would reject must not key a tool-execution intent either.
2903        let session_id = pv_core::SessionId::parse(session_id)
2904            .map(|id| id.to_string())
2905            .map_err(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request_source)?;
2906        let call =
2907            pv_sandbox::parse_tool_call(body).map_err(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request_source)?;
2908        // `parse_tool_call` accepts `"id": null` per JSON-RPC 2.0, but the
2909        // forwarded-execution key is `sha256("{session}:{id}")` — a null id
2910        // would collapse every null-id call in a session onto one execution
2911        // key, replaying the first call's cached outcome for later,
2912        // different calls. Require a concrete id here.
2913        let id = call.id.filter(|id| !id.is_null()).ok_or_else(|| {
2914            crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request(
2915                "forwarded tool calls require a non-null JSON-RPC id for idempotency".to_owned(),
2916            )
2917        })?;
2918        let request: Value =
2919            serde_json::from_slice(body).map_err(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request_source)?;
2920        let canonical = pv_receipts::canonicalize(&request)
2921            .map_err(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request_source)?;
2922        let request_digest = pv_core::digest::sha256_hex(canonical.as_bytes());
2923        let key_material = format!("{session_id}:{}", id);
2924        let key = pv_core::digest::sha256_hex(key_material.as_bytes());
2925        let directory = std::path::Path::new(spool).join(crate::spool::TOOL_EXECUTIONS);
2926        Ok(Self {
2927            intent_path: directory.join(format!("{key}{}", crate::spool::TOOL_INTENT_SUFFIX)),
2928            outcome_path: directory.join(format!("{key}{}", crate::spool::TOOL_OUTCOME_SUFFIX)),
2929            audited_path: directory.join(format!("{key}{}", crate::spool::TOOL_AUDITED_SUFFIX)),
2930            key,
2931            session_id,
2932            tool: call.tool,
2933            request_digest,
2934            principal_digest: String::new(),
2935            control_key,
2936        })
2937    }
2938
2939    fn bind_principal(
2940        &mut self,
2941        identity: &pv_events::AgentIdentity,
2942    ) -> Result<(), crate::pipeline::PipelineError> {
2943        let stable_identity = json!({
2944            "version": identity.version,
2945            "charter": identity.charter,
2946            "instance_uid": identity.instance_uid,
2947        });
2948        let canonical = pv_receipts::canonicalize(&stable_identity)
2949            .map_err(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::bad_request_source)?;
2950        self.principal_digest = pv_core::digest::sha256_hex(canonical.as_bytes());
2951        Ok(())
2952    }
2953
2954    async fn load(&self) -> Result<ToolExecutionState, String> {
2955        let execution = self.clone();
2956        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || execution.load_sync())
2957            .await
2958            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
2959    }
2960
2961    fn load_sync(&self) -> Result<ToolExecutionState, String> {
2962        // Read directly instead of `exists()` + `read()`: a concurrent
2963        // `release_unexecuted()` (client abandoned the call) or close-time
2964        // cleanup can unlink between the two, turning a retryable
2965        // Missing/Pending state into an opaque "No such file" lifecycle
2966        // error for the caller.
2967        let intent_bytes = match std::fs::read(&self.intent_path) {
2968            Ok(bytes) => Some(bytes),
2969            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => None,
2970            Err(error) => return Err(error.to_string()),
2971        };
2972        let Some(intent_bytes) = intent_bytes else {
2973            if self.outcome_path.exists() || self.audited_path.exists() {
2974                return Err("tool outcome exists without an authenticated intent".to_owned());
2975            }
2976            return Ok(ToolExecutionState::Missing);
2977        };
2978        let intent: ToolIntent = crate::journal::open(
2979            &self.control_key,
2980            &format!("{}:{}", crate::journal::TOOL_INTENT_DOMAIN, self.key),
2981            0,
2982            &intent_bytes,
2983        )?;
2984        if intent != self.intent() {
2985            return Err(TOOL_REQUEST_MISMATCH.to_owned());
2986        }
2987        let outcome_bytes = match std::fs::read(&self.outcome_path) {
2988            Ok(bytes) => Some(bytes),
2989            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => None,
2990            Err(error) => return Err(error.to_string()),
2991        };
2992        if let Some(outcome_bytes) = outcome_bytes {
2993            let outcome: ToolOutcome = crate::journal::open(
2994                &self.control_key,
2995                &format!("{}:{}", crate::journal::TOOL_OUTCOME_DOMAIN, self.key),
2996                0,
2997                &outcome_bytes,
2998            )?;
2999            let audited = match std::fs::read(&self.audited_path) {
3000                Ok(bytes) => crate::journal::open::<serde_json::Value>(
3001                    &self.control_key,
3002                    &format!("{}:{}", crate::journal::TOOL_AUDITED_DOMAIN, self.key),
3003                    0,
3004                    &bytes,
3005                )
3006                .is_ok(),
3007                Err(_) => false,
3008            };
3009            return if audited {
3010                Ok(ToolExecutionState::Completed(outcome))
3011            } else {
3012                Ok(ToolExecutionState::Unaudited(outcome))
3013            };
3014        }
3015        Ok(ToolExecutionState::Pending)
3016    }
3017
3018    async fn claim(&self) -> Result<(), ClaimError> {
3019        let execution = self.clone();
3020        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || execution.claim_sync())
3021            .await
3022            .map_err(|error| ClaimError::Backend(error.to_string()))?
3023    }
3024
3025    /// Delete this execution's intent file after a provably-not-executed
3026    /// forward (connect failure), restoring the key for a clean retry.
3027    /// NotFound is tolerated — the claim was ours, so a missing file only
3028    /// means a prior release already ran.
3029    ///
3030    /// The post-remove directory fsync is best-effort.
3031    /// `remove_file` returning Ok is durable-enough for the release
3032    /// semantics — a crash before the dir fsync makes the intent file
3033    /// resurrect on recovery, at which point `unresolved_tool_sessions`
3034    /// correctly quarantines the session (fail-closed). Previously any
3035    /// fsync failure returned Err and the caller at `mcp_call_inner`'s
3036    /// connect-failure branch skipped the budget refund, leaving the
3037    /// key unclaimed AND the budget debited — the exact bug the
3038    /// release-then-refund ordering was supposed to prevent.
3039    async fn release_unexecuted(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
3040        let execution = self.clone();
3041        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
3042            match crate::spool::change_tool_executions(execution.directory(), || {
3043                std::fs::remove_file(&execution.intent_path)
3044            }) {
3045                Ok(()) => {}
3046                Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),
3047                Err(error) => return Err(error.to_string()),
3048            }
3049            if let Some(directory) = execution.intent_path.parent() {
3050                if let Err(error) = pv_core::fsutil::sync_directory(directory) {
3051                    tracing::warn!(
3052                        path = %pv_core::fsutil::basename(&execution.intent_path),
3053                        %error,
3054                        "release_unexecuted: intent removed but directory fsync failed; treating as released"
3055                    );
3056                }
3057            }
3058            Ok(())
3059        })
3060        .await
3061        .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
3062    }
3063
3064    fn claim_sync(&self) -> Result<(), ClaimError> {
3065        use std::io::Write as _;
3066        let directory = self
3067            .intent_path
3068            .parent()
3069            .ok_or_else(|| ClaimError::Backend("tool execution directory is missing".to_owned()))?;
3070        // Skip the mkdir on the (steady-state) existing
3071        // directory — `create_dir_all` on an existing path still issues
3072        // an EEXIST mkdir syscall on the tool-claim hot path.
3073        if !directory.is_dir() {
3074            // `create_dir_all_synced` (not `create_dir_all`) so the
3075            // first-write path applies the 0o700 dir mode discipline
3076            // — pairs with the 0o600 file mode below so the tool
3077            // intents subtree cannot be enumerated by a co-tenant.
3078            pv_core::fsutil::create_dir_all_synced(directory)
3079                .map_err(|error| ClaimError::Backend(error.to_string()))?;
3080        }
3081        // `create_new(true)` is atomic on the underlying filesystem —
3082        // its only reason to return `AlreadyExists` is that another
3083        // in-flight request has already claimed this execution key
3084        // (the sole legitimate race source). Any other IoError kind
3085        // (StorageFull, PermissionDenied, InvalidInput, ReadOnlyFilesystem,
3086        // Interrupted, etc.) is a genuine infrastructure failure and
3087        // must NOT be reported to the client as a lost race — the
3088        // caller would answer 409 TOOL_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN and retries
3089        // would loop on the same underlying disk fault while the
3090        // client learns nothing useful. Split the two shapes at the
3091        // source so the caller can respond appropriately.
3092        //
3093        // This path deliberately bypasses `write_atomic` (the sibling
3094        // `persist`/`mark_audited` calls go through it) because the
3095        // AlreadyExists→Race distinction is destroyed by the temp+
3096        // rename pattern (a colliding claim would land on a fresh
3097        // temp path with a UUIDv7 suffix). That bypass means we need
3098        // to set the 0o600 mode explicitly here — otherwise this
3099        // intent file (sealed but plaintext session_id, tool name,
3100        // and request digest) inherits the ambient umask, typically
3101        // 0022 → 0o644, and becomes co-tenant readable.
3102        let mut open_options = std::fs::OpenOptions::new();
3103        open_options.write(true).create_new(true);
3104        #[cfg(unix)]
3105        {
3106            use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt as _;
3107            open_options.mode(0o600);
3108        }
3109        let intent = crate::journal::seal(
3110            &self.control_key,
3111            &format!("{}:{}", crate::journal::TOOL_INTENT_DOMAIN, self.key),
3112            0,
3113            &self.intent(),
3114        )
3115        .map_err(ClaimError::Backend)?;
3116        // Created and written in one turn: a scan reads intents in turns
3117        // too, so it never finds this one empty and takes it for one a
3118        // crash left torn (it would move it aside, and a retry could then
3119        // run the tool again). The sync runs after, outside the turn.
3120        let file = crate::spool::change_tool_executions(self.directory(), || {
3121            let mut file = open_options
3122                .open(&self.intent_path)
3123                .map_err(|error| match error.kind() {
3124                    std::io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => ClaimError::Race,
