3125                    _ => ClaimError::Backend(format!("tool execution intent unavailable: {error}")),
3126                })?;
3127            file.write_all(&intent)
3128                .map_err(|error| ClaimError::Backend(error.to_string()))?;
3129            Ok::<_, ClaimError>(file)
3130        })?;
3131        file.sync_all()
3132            .map_err(|error| ClaimError::Backend(error.to_string()))?;
3133        pv_core::fsutil::sync_directory(directory).map_err(|error| ClaimError::Backend(error.to_string()))
3134    }
3135
3136    async fn persist(&self, outcome: &ToolOutcome) -> Result<(), String> {
3137        let execution = self.clone();
3138        let outcome = outcome.clone();
3139        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
3140            let sealed = crate::journal::seal(
3141                &execution.control_key,
3142                &format!("{}:{}", crate::journal::TOOL_OUTCOME_DOMAIN, execution.key),
3143                0,
3144                &outcome,
3145            )?;
3146            write_atomic_bytes(&execution.outcome_path, &sealed)
3147        })
3148        .await
3149        .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
3150    }
3151
3152    async fn mark_audited(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
3153        let execution = self.clone();
3154        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
3155            let sealed = crate::journal::seal(
3156                &execution.control_key,
3157                &format!("{}:{}", crate::journal::TOOL_AUDITED_DOMAIN, execution.key),
3158                0,
3159                &json!({"audited": true}),
3160            )?;
3161            write_atomic_bytes(&execution.audited_path, &sealed)
3162        })
3163        .await
3164        .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
3165    }
3166
3167    fn intent(&self) -> ToolIntent {
3168        ToolIntent {
3169            execution_key: self.key.clone(),
3170            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),
3171            tool: self.tool.clone(),
3172            request_digest: self.request_digest.clone(),
3173            principal_digest: self.principal_digest.clone(),
3174        }
3175    }
3176}
3177
3178fn write_atomic_bytes(path: &std::path::Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
3179    pv_core::fsutil::write_atomic(path, bytes).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
3180}
3181
3182async fn lifecycle_caller(
3183    state: &AppState,
3184    headers: &HeaderMap,
3185    scope: &str,
3186) -> Result<crate::pipeline::AuthenticatedCaller, crate::pipeline::PipelineError> {
3187    let state = state.clone();
3188    let headers = headers.clone();
3189    let scope = scope.to_owned();
3190    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
3191        let caller = state.authenticate(&headers)?;
3192        caller.authorize(&state, Some(&scope))?;
3193        Ok(caller)
3194    })
3195    .await
3196    .map_err(crate::pipeline::PipelineError::unavailable_source)?
3197}
3198
3199async fn close_session(
3200    State(state): State<AppState>,
3201    Path(id): Path<String>,
3202    headers: HeaderMap,
3203) -> Response {
3204    if let Some(refusal) = refuse_foreign_origin(&state, &headers) {
3205        return refusal;
3206    }
3207    let caller = match lifecycle_caller(&state, &headers, &state.config.session_close_scope).await {
3208        Ok(caller) => caller,
3209        Err(error) => return pipeline_error(error),
3210    };
3211    let Some(session) = state.sessions.get(&id) else {
3212        return (
3213            StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
3214            Json(openai_error_body(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "unknown session")),
3215        )
3216            .into_response();
3217    };
3218    if let Err(error) = caller.authorize_session(&state, &session, &state.config.session_close_scope) {
3219        return pipeline_error(error);
3220    }
3221    match state
3222        .finalizer
3223        .close_session(session, StopReason::SessionClosed)
3224        .await
3225    {
3226        Ok(outcome) => Json(outcome).into_response(),
3227        Err(error) => finalize_error_response(&error),
3228    }
3229}
3230
3231async fn promote_session(
3232    State(state): State<AppState>,
3233    Path(id): Path<String>,
3234    headers: HeaderMap,
3235) -> Response {
3236    if let Some(refusal) = refuse_foreign_origin(&state, &headers) {
3237        return refusal;
3238    }
3239    let caller = match lifecycle_caller(&state, &headers, &state.config.session_promote_scope).await {
3240        Ok(caller) => caller,
3241        Err(error) => return pipeline_error(error),
3242    };
3243    let Some(session) = state.sessions.get(&id) else {
3244        return (
3245            StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
3246            Json(openai_error_body(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "unknown session")),
3247        )
3248            .into_response();
3249    };
3250    if let Err(error) = caller.authorize_session(&state, &session, &state.config.session_promote_scope) {
3251        return pipeline_error(error);
3252    }
3253    // `promote()` silently drives `close_session_locked`
3254    // on any still-open session. If an operator split the two scopes
3255    // (compliance auditor gets `session:promote`, on-call gets
3256    // `session:close`), a `session:promote`-only bearer could
3257    // otherwise force-close any live agent session by promoting it —
3258    // bypassing `session:close` entirely. When the session is still
3259    // open, additionally require the close scope so promote ⊇ close
3260    // in the scope authority sense.
3261    if !session.is_closed() {
3262        if let Err(error) = caller.authorize_session(&state, &session, &state.config.session_close_scope) {
3263            return pipeline_error(error);
3264        }
3265    }
3266    match state.finalizer.promote(session).await {
3267        Ok(receipt) => Json(receipt).into_response(),
3268        Err(error) => finalize_error_response(&error),
3269    }
3270}
3271
3272/// JWKS endpoint exposing the exchange signer's public key so backends
3273/// can verify signed tokens offline.
3274async fn jwks(State(state): State<AppState>) -> Response {
3275    match &state.token_signer {
3276        Some(signer) => Json(signer.jwks_json()).into_response(),
3277        None => Json(serde_json::json!({"keys": []})).into_response(),
3278    }
3279}
3280
3281/// RFC 8693 token exchange endpoint. Accepts a form-encoded request,
3282/// validates the inbound subject token, narrows scopes to their
3283/// intersection with the requested set, and returns a fresh JWT
3284/// scoped to the target backend audience.
3285async fn token_exchange(State(state): State<AppState>, headers: HeaderMap, body: Bytes) -> Response {
3286    if let Some(refusal) = refuse_foreign_origin(&state, &headers) {
3287        return refusal;
3288    }
3289    crate::token_routes::control_request(state, move |state| async move {
3290        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || token_exchange_inner(state, body))
3291            .await
3292            .unwrap_or_else(|_| oauth_unavailable())
3293    })
3294    .await
3295}
3296
3297fn token_exchange_inner(state: AppState, body: Bytes) -> Response {
3298    // RFC 7523 workload assertions have their own grant and their own gate
3299    // (`[workload_identity]`), independent of `token_exchange_enabled`.
3300    let grant_type = serde_urlencoded::from_bytes::<Vec<(String, String)>>(&body)
3301        .ok()
3302        .and_then(|pairs| pairs.into_iter().find(|(key, _)| key == "grant_type"))
3303        .map(|(_, value)| value);
3304    if grant_type.as_deref() == Some(pv_identity::JWT_BEARER_GRANT_TYPE) {
3305        return crate::workload::grant(&state, &body);
3306    }
3307    if !state.config.token_exchange_enabled {
3308        return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
3309    }
3310    let validator = match &state.identity {
3311        Some(v) => v,
3312        None => {
3313            return (
3314                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
3315                Json(oauth_error(
3316                    "server_error",
3317                    "token exchange requires an identity validator",
3318                )),
3319            )
3320                .into_response();
3321        }
3322    };
3323    let req: pv_identity::TokenExchangeRequest = match serde_urlencoded::from_bytes(&body) {
3324        Ok(r) => r,
3325        Err(e) => {
3326            return (
3327                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
3328                Json(oauth_error(
3329                    "invalid_request",
3330                    &format!("invalid token exchange request: {e}"),
3331                )),
3332            )
3333                .into_response();
3334        }
3335    };
3336    if req.grant_type != pv_identity::TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE {
3337        return (
3338            StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
3339            Json(oauth_error(
3340                "unsupported_grant_type",
3341                &format!("unsupported grant_type: {:?}", req.grant_type),
3342            )),
3343        )
3344            .into_response();
3345    }
3346    if req.subject_token_type != pv_identity::exchange::JWT_TOKEN_TYPE {
3347        return (
3348            StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
3349            Json(oauth_error(
3350                "invalid_request",
3351                &format!("unsupported subject_token_type: {:?}", req.subject_token_type),
3352            )),
3353        )
3354            .into_response();
3355    }
3356    state
3357        .metrics
3358        .counter(
3359            "pv_identity_validations_total",
3360            "Full inbound identity validations",
3361        )
3362        .inc();
3363    let validated = match validator.validate(&req.subject_token) {
3364        Ok(v) => v,
3365        Err(pv_identity::IdentityError::RevocationUnavailable(detail)) => {
3366            tracing::error!(%detail, "identity revocation list unavailable; refusing token exchange");
3367            return oauth_unavailable();
3368        }
3369        Err(e) => {
3370            tracing::warn!(error = %e, "token exchange subject token rejected");
3371            // Same opaque description as the proxy routes: the detailed
3372            // error names configured kids, issuers, and algorithms.
3373            return (
3374                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
3375                Json(oauth_error(
3376                    "invalid_request",
3377                    crate::pipeline::classify_identity_error(&e),
3378                )),
3379            )
3380                .into_response();
3381        }
3382    };
3383    let now_s = pv_core::time::now_ms() / 1000;
3384    let ttl = state.config.token_exchange_ttl_s.min(900);
3385    let azp = &validated.claims.instance_uid;
3386    let allowed_audiences: Vec<String> = state.config.backends.iter().map(|b| b.name.clone()).collect();
3387    // `build_exchanged_claims` reads an empty allow-list as "any audience".
3388    // The gateway must sign only for audiences it knows (RFC 8693 §2.2.2),
3389    // so with no backends configured every target is refused.
3390    if allowed_audiences.is_empty() {
3391        return (
3392            StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
3393            Json(oauth_error(
3394                "invalid_target",
3395                "no [[backends]] are configured, so no exchange audience is permitted",
3396            )),
3397        )
3398            .into_response();
3399    }
3400    // RFC 8693 §2.1: `actor_token_type` is REQUIRED when `actor_token` is
3401    // present and MUST NOT be sent without it. The actor is validated
3402    // exactly like the subject (signature, revocation, human subject).
3403    let actor = match (req.actor_token.as_deref(), req.actor_token_type.as_deref()) {
3404        (None, None) => None,
3405        (Some(token), Some(pv_identity::exchange::JWT_TOKEN_TYPE)) => match validator.validate(token) {
3406            Ok(actor) => Some(actor),
3407            Err(pv_identity::IdentityError::RevocationUnavailable(detail)) => {
3408                tracing::error!(%detail, "identity revocation list unavailable; refusing token exchange");
3409                return oauth_unavailable();
3410            }
3411            Err(error) => {
3412                tracing::warn!(%error, "token exchange actor token rejected");
3413                return (
3414                    StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
3415                    Json(oauth_error(
3416                        "invalid_request",
3417                        crate::pipeline::classify_identity_error(&error),
3418                    )),
3419                )
3420                    .into_response();
3421            }
3422        },
3423        (Some(_), Some(other)) => {
3424            return (
3425                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
3426                Json(oauth_error(
3427                    "invalid_request",
3428                    &format!("unsupported actor_token_type: {other:?}"),
3429                )),
3430            )
3431                .into_response();
3432        }
3433        _ => {
3434            return (
3435                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
3436                Json(oauth_error(
3437                    "invalid_request",
3438                    "actor_token and actor_token_type must be sent together",
3439                )),
3440            )
3441                .into_response();
3442        }
3443    };
3444    let params = pv_identity::ExchangeParams {
3445        subject: &validated.claims,
3446        subject_chain: &validated.chain_tokens,
3447        subject_delegation_depth: validated.total_delegation_depth,
3448        target_audience: &req.audience,
3449        requested_scopes: req.scope.as_deref(),
3450        azp,
3451        now_s,
3452        ttl_s: ttl,
3453        issuer: &state.config.audience,
3454        max_depth: state.config.max_delegation_depth,
3455        allowed_audiences: &allowed_audiences,
3456    };
3457    let actor = actor.as_ref().map(|actor| pv_identity::ExchangeActor {
3458        claims: &actor.claims,
3459        chain: &actor.chain_tokens,
3460    });
3461    let exchanged = match pv_identity::build_exchanged_claims_with_actor(&params, actor.as_ref()) {
3462        Ok(c) => c,
3463        Err(e) => {
3464            let code = match &e {
3465                pv_identity::ExchangeError::EmptyIntersection
3466                | pv_identity::ExchangeError::ScopeExceedsSubject(_)
3467                | pv_identity::ExchangeError::InvalidScopes => "invalid_scope",
3468                pv_identity::ExchangeError::DelegationExceeded { .. }
3469                | pv_identity::ExchangeError::ActorNotDirect => "invalid_grant",
3470                pv_identity::ExchangeError::TargetNotAllowed(_) => "invalid_target",
3471                _ => "invalid_request",
3472            };
3473            return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, Json(oauth_error(code, &e.to_string()))).into_response();
3474        }
3475    };
3476    let signer = match &state.token_signer {
3477        Some(s) => s,
3478        None => {
3479            return (
3480                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
3481                Json(oauth_error(
3482                    "server_error",
3483                    "token exchange is enabled but no signing key is configured",
3484                )),
3485            )
3486                .into_response();
3487        }
3488    };
3489    let access_token = match signer.sign(&exchanged) {
3490        Ok(jwt) => jwt,
3491        Err(e) => {
3492            return (
3493                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
3494                Json(oauth_error("server_error", &format!("token signing failed: {e}"))),
3495            )
3496                .into_response();
3497        }
3498    };
3499    let resp = pv_identity::TokenExchangeResponse {
3500        access_token,
3501        issued_token_type: pv_identity::exchange::JWT_TOKEN_TYPE.to_owned(),
3502        token_type: "Bearer".to_owned(),
3503        expires_in: exchanged.exp.saturating_sub(now_s),
3504        scope: if exchanged.scopes.is_empty() {
3505            None
3506        } else {
3507            Some(exchanged.scopes.join(" "))
3508        },
3509    };
3510    (
3511        [
3512            (axum::http::header::CACHE_CONTROL, "no-store"),
3513            (axum::http::header::PRAGMA, "no-cache"),
3514        ],
3515        Json(resp),
3516    )
3517        .into_response()
3518}
3519
3520/// Typed status mapping for close/promote failures. Flattening every
3521/// `FinalizeError` to 500 (the old behavior) misclassified deterministic
3522/// fail-closed refusals as server faults: SDKs retry 500s pointlessly
3523/// against a permanently-quarantined session, and operators page on 5xx
3524/// rates for what is working policy (the same rationale as the breaker's
3525/// deliberate 403-not-429 choice, and the tool path's CONFLICT mapping).
3526fn finalize_error_response(error: &crate::reconciler::FinalizeError) -> Response {
3527    use crate::reconciler::FinalizeError;
3528    // Transient I/O (spool disk full, read-only filesystem,
3529    // temporarily unavailable storage) wrapping an Atif or Receipt
3530    // failure gets 503 + Retry-After, mirroring the `/readyz` probe
3531    // policy that already treats ENOSPC/EROFS as transient. Without
3532    // this split the same incident produced `readyz=503` (correct)
3533    // but `close=500` (misclassified as a permanent server bug),
3534    // making SDKs configured with default retry-on-503 stop
3535    // retrying and paging operators for a disk-full infra event.
3536    // Same permanence-split discipline as `Bridge` vs `BridgeConfig`
3537    // — the underlying `io::ErrorKind` is the discriminant.
3538    if error.is_transient_io() {
3539        let mut response = (
3540            StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
3541            Json(openai_error_body(
3542                StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
3543                &error.to_string(),
3544            )),
3545        )
3546            .into_response();
3547        response
3548            .headers_mut()
3549            .insert(axum::http::header::RETRY_AFTER, HeaderValue::from_static("5"));
3550        return response;
3551    }
3552    let status = match error {
3553        // Deterministic state conflicts: the request conflicts with the
3554        // session's current state and retrying cannot change the outcome
3555        // (quarantined capture, no artifact to promote, promotion already
3556        // in progress).
3557        FinalizeError::CaptureIncomplete | FinalizeError::Promotion(_) => StatusCode::CONFLICT,
3558        // Permanent bridge misconfiguration (unknown
3559        // topic, unresolvable schema) — retrying without operator
3560        // action cannot succeed. Map to 400 so SDKs stop retrying
3561        // and pagers fire on operator config errors, not on
3562        // transient outages.
3563        FinalizeError::BridgeConfig { .. } => StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
3564        // Transient infrastructure: the broker is unreachable; the close
3565        // stays pending and a retry (or the reconciler sweep) completes it.
3566        FinalizeError::Bridge { .. } | FinalizeError::ToolEvidence(_) => StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
3567        // Everything else is a genuine internal fault.
3568        _ => StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
3569    };
3570    let mut response = (status, Json(openai_error_body(status, &error.to_string()))).into_response();
3571    if status == StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE {
3572        // Same advisory as pipeline_error's retryable class.
3573        response
3574            .headers_mut()
3575            .insert(axum::http::header::RETRY_AFTER, HeaderValue::from_static("5"));
3576    }
3577    response
3578}
3579
3580/// OpenAI-shape error body used by `pipeline_error`,
3581/// `lifecycle_error`, and `finalize_error_response` (R66 F1).
3582/// SDKs dispatch on `error.type` / `error.code`
3583/// (`openai.APIError.code`); the flat `{"error": <string>}` shape the
3584/// close/promote handlers previously emitted left retry classifiers
3585/// dead, silently retrying `409 CaptureIncomplete` and `409
3586/// Promotion(...)` until the SDK's request budget expired against a
3587/// permanently-quarantined session. Centralising the body construction
3588/// here also fixes the earlier five-different-shapes drift across
3589/// sibling routes.
3590fn openai_error_body(status: StatusCode, message: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
3591    let error_type = match status.as_u16() {
3592        400 | 404 | 409 | 413 => "invalid_request_error",
3593        401 => "authentication_error",
3594        403 => "permission_error",
3595        429 => "rate_limit_error",
3596        _ => "api_error",
3597    };
3598    json!({
3599        "error": {
3600            "message": message,
3601            "type": error_type,
3602            "param": null,
3603            "code": status.as_u16(),
3604        }
3605    })
3606}

3608pub(crate) const TOKENS_REVOKED_METRIC: &str = "pv_tokens_revoked_total";
3609pub(crate) const TOKENS_REVOKED_HELP: &str = "Successful holder revocations and operator revocation commands";

3611/// Exchange the caller's NHI bearer for a token scoped to one backend and
3612/// one tool. Refusals (no bearer, exchange rules) are 403; faults on the
3613/// gateway's side (missing validator or signer, unreachable revocation
3614/// list, signing failure) are 503 so they never read as the caller's fault.
3615fn exchange_for_backend(
3616    state: &AppState,
3617    caller: &crate::pipeline::AuthenticatedCaller,
3618    target_audience: &str,
3619    tool: &str,
3620) -> Result<String, crate::pipeline::PipelineError> {
3621    exchange_token_for(state, caller, target_audience, &crate::pipeline::tool_scope(tool))
3622}
3623
3624/// Mint a gateway-signed, backend-scoped token for `caller` holding
3625/// `requested_scopes ∩ caller scopes` (space-separated request).
3626pub(crate) fn exchange_token_for(
3627    state: &AppState,
3628    caller: &crate::pipeline::AuthenticatedCaller,
3629    target_audience: &str,
3630    requested_scopes: &str,
3631) -> Result<String, crate::pipeline::PipelineError> {
3632    use crate::pipeline::PipelineError;
3633    let refused = |reason: String| PipelineError::blocked(format!("backend token exchange failed: {reason}"));
3634    let Some(signer) = state.token_signer.as_ref() else {
3635        return Err(PipelineError::unavailable(
3636            "backend token exchange is not configured on this gateway".to_owned(),
3637        ));
3638    };
3639    let validated = caller
3640        .validated
3641        .as_ref()
3642        .ok_or_else(|| refused("no validated caller identity".into()))?;
3643    let now_s = pv_core::time::now_ms() / 1000;
3644    let ttl = state.config.token_exchange_ttl_s.min(900);
3645    let allowed_audiences: Vec<String> = state.config.backends.iter().map(|b| b.name.clone()).collect();
3646    let params = pv_identity::ExchangeParams {
3647        subject: &validated.claims,
3648        subject_chain: &validated.chain_tokens,
3649        subject_delegation_depth: validated.total_delegation_depth,
3650        target_audience,
3651        requested_scopes: Some(requested_scopes),
3652        azp: &validated.claims.instance_uid,
3653        now_s,
3654        ttl_s: ttl,
3655        issuer: &state.config.audience,
3656        max_depth: state.config.max_delegation_depth,
3657        allowed_audiences: &allowed_audiences,
3658    };
3659    let exchanged = pv_identity::build_exchanged_claims(&params).map_err(|e| refused(e.to_string()))?;
3660    signer.sign_with_typ(&exchanged, "av-tool+jwt").map_err(|error| {
3661        tracing::error!(%error, "exchanged token signing failed");
3662        PipelineError::unavailable("backend token exchange could not sign a token".to_owned())
3663    })
3664}
3665
3666fn oauth_error(error: &str, description: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
3667    json!({
3668        "error": error,
3669        "error_description": description,
3670    })
3671}
3672
3673/// 503 for OAuth endpoints when a dependency (the revocation list) is
3674/// down; `Retry-After` tells the client when to try again.
3675fn oauth_unavailable() -> Response {
3676    let mut response = (
3677        StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
3678        Json(oauth_error(
3679            "temporarily_unavailable",
3680            "the token revocation list is unavailable; retry shortly",
3681        )),
3682    )
3683        .into_response();
3684    response
3685        .headers_mut()
3686        .insert(axum::http::header::RETRY_AFTER, HeaderValue::from_static("5"));
3687    response
3688}
3689
3690/// `pipeline_error` plus the `X-PV-Session` echo. Once a request is
3691/// admitted, its session is captured to the spool and finalizes into an
3692/// audit artifact even when the upstream call fails — but the id of a
3693/// server-generated session was only revealed on the success path, so
3694/// `pvctl receipt-locate` was impossible for exactly the failed calls
3695/// an auditor most wants (the documented contract echoes the id so the
3696/// artifact can be located later). Use this for every error return
3697/// that occurs after admission bound a session.
3698fn pipeline_error_for_session(error: crate::pipeline::PipelineError, session_id: &str) -> Response {
3699    let mut response = pipeline_error(error);
3700    if let Ok(value) = HeaderValue::from_str(session_id) {
3701        response
3702            .headers_mut()
3703            .insert(crate::pipeline::SESSION_HEADER, value);
3704    }
3705    response
3706}
3707
3708pub(crate) fn pipeline_error(error: crate::pipeline::PipelineError) -> Response {
3709    use crate::pipeline::PipelineError;
3710    let close = matches!(error, PipelineError::Abort(_));
3711    let status = error.status();
3712    let mut response = (status, Json(openai_error_body(status, &error.to_string()))).into_response();
3713    if close {
3714        response
3715            .headers_mut()
3716            .insert(axum::http::header::CONNECTION, HeaderValue::from_static("close"));
3717    }
3718    // Drive advisory-header attachment off the numeric HTTP status
3719    // rather than variant identity. `PipelineError` is
3720    // `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a future variant (e.g. `Timeout` → 504,
3721    // `RateLimited` → 429) would silently skip Retry-After under a
3722    // `matches!(error, PipelineError::Unavailable { .. })` chain — exactly
3723    // the SDK-hammering regression this arm exists to prevent. Using
3724    // the status code centralises the semantic once and covers every
3725    // present and future variant that maps to the same class.
3726    match status.as_u16() {
3727        // 429 / 502 / 503 / 504 — retryable per RFC 7231 §7.1.3; the
3728        // header value is deliberately short so the audit-capture
3729        // recovery window is fast, but long enough that clients do not
3730        // hammer during transient failures.
3731        429 | 502 | 503 | 504 => {
3732            response
3733                .headers_mut()
3734                .insert(axum::http::header::RETRY_AFTER, HeaderValue::from_static("5"));
3735        }
3736        // 401 — RFC 7235 §3.1 MUST send `WWW-Authenticate`; RFC 6750 §3
3737        // defines the Bearer challenge shape used with NHI JWTs.
3738        401 => {
3739            response.headers_mut().insert(
3740                axum::http::header::WWW_AUTHENTICATE,
3741                HeaderValue::from_static("Bearer realm=\"proofvisor\", error=\"invalid_token\""),
3742            );
3743        }
3744        _ => {}
3745    }
3746    response
3747}
3748
3749fn lifecycle_error(error: String) -> Response {
3750    // Same OpenAI-shaped body as `pipeline_error` and
3751    // `finalize_error_response` so all four sibling routes agree on
3752    // one error contract. Central via `openai_error_body` (R66 F1).
3753    (
3754        StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
3755        Json(openai_error_body(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, &error)),
3756    )
3757        .into_response()
3758}

3760struct AbortFinalizingStream {
3761    inner: BoxStream<'static, Result<Bytes, std::io::Error>>,
3762    session: Arc<crate::session::Session>,
3763    identity: pv_events::AgentIdentity,
3764    response_permit: Option<crate::worker::ResponsePermit>,
3765    /// Handle to submit the response-capture job at end-of-stream. The
3766    /// permit above only holds the `response_capacity` semaphore slot
3767    /// — the mpsc queue slot is re-acquired at submit time via
3768    /// `ResponsePermit::submit(&worker, job)`.
3769    worker: crate::worker::WorkerHandle,
3770    store: Arc<dyn pv_state::StateStore>,
3771    budget: pv_state::BudgetSpec,
3772    /// Console-pushed token-rate windows; completion tokens are recorded
3773    /// as the provider reports them.
3774    rates: Arc<crate::policy_push::RateLimits>,
3775    /// Console-pushed rules at request time: egress guardrails over the
3776    /// captured response text, and the budget policy names a mid-stream
3777    /// refusal is attributed to.
3778    pushed: Arc<pv_sandbox::PushedRules>,
3779    /// The local budget, so a mid-stream refusal can say which pushed
3780    /// policy set the cap it hit.
3781    local_budget: pv_state::BudgetSpec,
3782    /// Console policy the next failure capture is attributed to.
3783    failure_policy: Option<String>,
3784    /// True once a body byte reached the client (SSE only): after that
3785    /// a refusal can only end the stream, not change the status.
3786    emitted_any: bool,
3787    /// Bytes of each choice's content the egress guardrails already
3788    /// scanned, so a streamed response is scanned incrementally.
3789    egress_scanned: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, usize>,
3790    /// Same, for each choice's reasoning text.
3791    egress_scanned_reasoning: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, usize>,
3792    /// Same, for each tool call's arguments, by `(choice, call)`.
3793    egress_scanned_tools: std::collections::BTreeMap<(u64, u64), usize>,
3794    /// True when a console-pushed `llm.egress` transform is in force on
3795    /// a streamed response: frames are held and relayed, rewritten,
3796    /// once the response is complete (a match may straddle frames).
3797    hold_stream: bool,
3798    /// The frames held back while `hold_stream` is set, verbatim.
3799    held_frames: Vec<String>,
3800    /// `(policy, replacements)` for every egress transform that rewrote
3801    /// this response, recorded in the capture payload.
3802    egress_transforms: Vec<(String, usize)>,
3803    finalizer: crate::reconciler::Finalizer,
3804    _lease: crate::session::SessionLease,
3805    response_marker: Option<String>,
3806    response_attempt_id: String,
3807    /// Captured text, reasoning and finish reason per `choices[].index`.
3808    /// A single-choice response lives at index 0; `n > 1` responses
3809    /// keep every choice apart so the attested step never carries a
3810    /// text no model produced.
3811    response_choices: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, ChoiceCapture>,
3812    response_model: Option<String>,
3813    upstream_status: StatusCode,
3814    response_cost_usd_micros: u64,
3815    response_tool_calls: std::collections::BTreeMap<(u64, u64), PartialToolCall>,
3816    response_metrics: pv_events::EventMetrics,
3817    charged_completion_tokens: u64,
3818    last_reported_completion_tokens: Option<u64>,
3819    last_reported_prompt_tokens: Option<u64>,
3820    last_reported_cached_tokens: Option<u64>,
3821    last_reported_cost_usd_micros: Option<u64>,
3822    saw_chunk: bool,
3823    /// At-most-once guard for `submit_response_capture`. Set BEFORE the
3824    /// fallible `ResponsePermit::submit` on purpose: if the shard is full
3825    /// the capture event is intentionally dropped (counted in
3826    /// `pv_events_dropped_total{stage="response_slot"}`) and MUST NOT be
3827    /// retried by a later call. Do not "fix" the ordering by setting this
3828    /// after the submit — that would reintroduce double-submit attempts
3829    /// against a consumed permit.
3830    capture_attempted: bool,
3831    is_sse: bool,
3832    protocol_buffer: Vec<u8>,
3833    /// Reusable per-frame parse buffer. R62 perf optimisation: the
3834    /// SSE absorb loop previously did `let frame: Vec<u8> = self
3835    /// .protocol_buffer.drain(..end).collect();` per frame — one
3836    /// heap alloc per frame × 50-500 frames per streamed completion.
3837    /// Reusing a single Vec (drained-then-refilled from
3838    /// `protocol_buffer[..end]`) drops that to ONE amortised alloc
3839    /// per stream. The scratch is `mem::take`'d into a local across
3840    /// the absorb loop to satisfy the borrow checker against
3841    /// `self.absorb_frame(&mut self, &str)`.
3842    frame_scratch: Vec<u8>,
3843    pending_output: std::collections::VecDeque<Bytes>,
3844    pending_budget: Option<PendingBudget>,
3845    /// Principal-scoped ledger (id + spec) when `[principal_budget]` is
3846    /// configured. Mid-stream completion tokens must debit BOTH ledgers:
3847    /// the principal ledger is the only one that binds under the
3848    /// session-header-rotation attack, and before it was threaded here
3849    /// every streamed completion token was invisible to it — a rotating
3850    /// caller consumed >10× the principal cap in live testing because
3851    /// only the ~admission prompt heuristic ever landed on the
3852    /// principal counter.
3853    principal_budget: Option<(String, pv_state::BudgetSpec)>,
3854    captured_bytes: usize,
3855    /// admission-time prompt-token heuristic, reconciled
3856    /// against the provider's `usage.prompt_tokens` at terminal capture.
3857    billed_prompt_tokens: u64,
3858    completed: bool,
3859    /// True when the client sent no `X-PV-Session` header and the id
3860    /// was server-generated. The client cannot address this session
3861    /// again (the id only travels back in the response header), so
3862    /// OPENAI-COMPATIBILITY.md promises "the session then closes
3863    /// immediately after the response — one turn, one audit event".
3864    /// Before this flag existed, a completed one-shot lingered OPEN
3865    /// until the idle sweeper (`session_idle_close_s`, default 900 s):
3866    /// a stock SDK caller got no receipt for 15 minutes.
3867    ephemeral: bool,
3868}
3869
3870const MAX_PROVIDER_CAPTURE_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
3871const MAX_PROVIDER_FIELD_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;
3872const MAX_PROVIDER_TOOL_CALLS: usize = 128;
3873
3874impl AbortFinalizingStream {
3875    fn absorb_network_chunk(&mut self, raw: &[u8]) -> Result<u64, String> {
3876        self.saw_chunk |= !raw.is_empty();
3877        self.captured_bytes = self
3878            .captured_bytes
3879            .checked_add(raw.len())
3880            .ok_or_else(|| "provider response size overflow".to_owned())?;
3881        if self.captured_bytes > MAX_PROVIDER_CAPTURE_BYTES {
3882            return Err(format!(
3883                "provider response exceeds {MAX_PROVIDER_CAPTURE_BYTES} capture bytes"
3884            ));
3885        }
3886        self.protocol_buffer.extend_from_slice(raw);
3887        if !self.is_sse {
3888            return Ok(0);
3889        }
3890        // non-success upstream bodies are relayed
3891        // verbatim; do NOT try to parse them as chat-completion SSE
3892        // frames. An `event: error` / `data: {"error":...}` frame
3893        // from a 4xx/5xx stream would otherwise fail the strict
3894        // parser and collapse the true status into a 502. Drop the
3895        // buffered bytes on the floor (the wire body has already
3896        // been relayed to the client via `pending_output`) and
3897        // let flush_protocol_buffer's own guard finalise.
3898        if !self.upstream_status.is_success() {
3899            self.protocol_buffer.clear();
3900            return Ok(0);
3901        }
3902        let mut budget_delta = 0u64;
3903        // R62 perf: reuse `frame_scratch` across iterations instead
3904        // of the prior `let frame: Vec<u8> = self.protocol_buffer
3905        // .drain(..end).collect();` which allocated a fresh Vec per
3906        // frame (50-500 frames per streamed completion). `mem::take`
3907        // moves the buffer into a local so the loop body can `&scratch`
3908        // in a &str while simultaneously calling `&mut self` methods
3909        // (borrow checker won't allow the direct `&self.frame_scratch`
3910        // + `&mut self` pattern). Restored to `self` after the loop
3911        // so subsequent `absorb_network_chunk` calls reuse the same
3912        // capacity.
3913        let mut scratch: Vec<u8> = std::mem::take(&mut self.frame_scratch);
3914        let absorb_result = loop {
3915            let Some(end) = sse_frame_end(&self.protocol_buffer) else {
3916                break Ok(());
3917            };
3918            scratch.clear();
3919            // Safe: `sse_frame_end` returns `end <= self.protocol_buffer.len()`
3920            // by construction (it locates a frame boundary within the buffer).
3921            #[allow(clippy::indexing_slicing)]
3922            scratch.extend_from_slice(&self.protocol_buffer[..end]);
3923            self.protocol_buffer.drain(..end);
3924            let frame = match std::str::from_utf8(&scratch) {
3925                Ok(frame) => frame,
3926                Err(error) => break Err(format!("provider SSE frame is not UTF-8: {error}")),
3927            };
3928            if self.hold_stream {
3929                self.held_frames.push(frame.to_owned());
3930            }
3931            match self.absorb_frame(frame) {
3932                Ok(delta) => match budget_delta.checked_add(delta) {
3933                    Some(total) => budget_delta = total,
3934                    None => break Err("provider completion-token delta overflow".to_owned()),
3935                },
3936                Err(error) => break Err(error),
3937            }
3938        };
3939        self.frame_scratch = scratch;
3940        if let Err(error) = absorb_result {
3941            // A chunk's deltas are only debited AFTER this loop (one
3942            // budget check per network chunk), but `absorb_frame` bumps
3943            // `charged_completion_tokens` per frame. An error on a later
3944            // frame abandons the never-debited `budget_delta` while the
3945            // earlier frames' bumps stay in `charged` — and the terminal
3946            // over-charge refund computes `charged − reported`, so it
3947            // would credit tokens that were never debited (a hostile
3948            // upstream could replenish the session ledger at will). Roll
3949            // `charged` back to exactly what was debited. `absorb_frame`
3950            // errors strictly before charging its own frame, so the
3951            // accumulated `budget_delta` is precisely the undebited part.
3952            self.charged_completion_tokens = self.charged_completion_tokens.saturating_sub(budget_delta);
3953            return Err(error);
3954        }
3955        if self.protocol_buffer.len() > MAX_PROVIDER_FIELD_BYTES {
3956            // Same rollback as above: this Err also means
3957            // `begin_budget_check` never debits the frames this call DID
3958            // drain successfully, so their charges must not survive into
3959            // the terminal refund either.
3960            self.charged_completion_tokens = self.charged_completion_tokens.saturating_sub(budget_delta);
3961            return Err("unterminated provider SSE frame exceeds limit".to_owned());
3962        }
3963        Ok(budget_delta)
3964    }
3965
3966    fn flush_protocol_buffer(&mut self) -> Result<u64, String> {
3967        if self.protocol_buffer.is_empty() {
3968            return Ok(0);
3969        }
3970        // Never fail-closed on a non-success upstream body.
3971        // Providers ship text/plain and HTML error pages on 4xx/5xx
3972        // (OpenAI's Cloudflare frontend returns text/html on 429;
3973        // Anthropic ships 503 HTML from AWS ALBs during backend
3974        // restarts). The strict JSON parse below would fail and be
3975        // mapped to a fresh 502, silently dropping the real status +
3976        // Retry-After header. SDKs treat "502 without Retry-After" as
3977        // an immediate retry candidate, so a rate-limited upstream
3978        // gets hammered instead of backed off. Skip the parse for
3979        // non-success responses; the buffered body still relays
3980        // through the buffered non-SSE branch and the true
3981        // upstream_status is preserved into the response later.
3982        if !self.upstream_status.is_success() {
3983            let _ = std::mem::take(&mut self.protocol_buffer);
3984            return Ok(0);
3985        }
3986        let frame = std::mem::take(&mut self.protocol_buffer);
3987        let frame = std::str::from_utf8(&frame)
3988            .map_err(|error| format!("provider response is not UTF-8: {error}"))?;
3989        if self.hold_stream {
3990            self.held_frames.push(frame.to_owned());
3991        }
3992        self.absorb_frame(frame)
3993    }
3994
3995    fn absorb_frame(&mut self, raw: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {
3996        // Every dialect reaches this relay OpenAI-shaped (the native
3997        // adapters translate in `forward_chat`), so one parser serves
3998        // all providers.
3999        let Some(parsed) = parse_provider_chunk(raw)? else {
4000            return Ok(0);
4001        };
4002        if self.upstream_status.is_success() && !parsed.has_choices {
4003            return Err("successful provider response has no choices array".to_owned());
4004        }
4005        for choice in parsed.choices {
4006            if choice.index >= MAX_CHOICE_INDEX {
4007                return Err(format!("provider choice index {} is out of range", choice.index));
4008            }
4009            let capture = self.response_choices.entry(choice.index).or_default();
4010            push_bounded(&mut capture.content, &choice.content, "response message")?;
4011            push_bounded(&mut capture.reasoning, &choice.reasoning, "response reasoning")?;
4012            if choice.finish_reason.is_some() {
4013                capture.finish_reason = choice.finish_reason;
4014            }
4015        }
4016        if self.response_model.is_none() {
4017            self.response_model = parsed.model_name;
4018        }
4019        // Cumulative-cost contract: providers
4020        // that report `cost_usd` are expected to report it CUMULATIVELY
4021        // (OpenRouter-style final/rolling usage frames) — `max()` folds
4022        // that correctly and tolerates repeated identical frames. A
4023        // provider emitting per-chunk INCREMENTAL costs is mostly
4024        // caught by `reject_metric_regression` (any decrease fails the
4025        // stream), but a monotone non-decreasing incremental sequence
4026        // (e.g. equal per-chunk costs) passes the guard and attests
4027        // only the LAST chunk's amount. That shape is indistinguishable
4028        // from legitimate repeated cumulative frames on the wire, so it
4029        // cannot be rejected without breaking conformant providers —
4030        // recorded here as the documented accepted limitation
4031        // (undercount is bounded by the true total; never an
4032        // overcharge).
4033        self.response_cost_usd_micros = self.response_cost_usd_micros.max(parsed.cost_usd_micros);
4034        for delta in parsed.tool_call_deltas {
4035            let key = if delta.complete {
4036                // A complete delta's `index` is frame-local (Gemini part
4037                // position, restarting at 0 every chunk): two whole
4038                // calls arriving in separate chunks would collide at
4039                // (choice, 0) and either concatenate into one corrupt
4040                // attested call or hard-fail a legitimate stream on the
4041                // name-conflict guard below. Allocate the next free
4042                // per-choice slot instead; arrival order is preserved
4043                // by the BTreeMap key.
4044                let next = self
4045                    .response_tool_calls
4046                    .range((delta.choice_index, 0)..=(delta.choice_index, u64::MAX))
4047                    .next_back()
4048                    .map_or(0, |(&(_, index), _)| index.saturating_add(1));
4049                (delta.choice_index, next)
4050            } else {
4051                if delta.index >= MAX_PROVIDER_TOOL_CALLS as u64 {
4052                    return Err(format!(
4053                        "provider tool-call index {} is out of range",
4054                        delta.index
4055                    ));
4056                }
4057                (delta.choice_index, delta.index)
4058            };
4059            if !self.response_tool_calls.contains_key(&key)
4060                && self.response_tool_calls.len() >= MAX_PROVIDER_TOOL_CALLS
4061            {
4062                return Err(format!(
4063                    "provider response exceeds {MAX_PROVIDER_TOOL_CALLS} tool calls"
4064                ));
4065            }
4066            let partial = self.response_tool_calls.entry(key).or_default();
4067            // An upstream that reuses an accumulated (choice, index) slot
4068            // with a DIFFERENT id or name is emitting a malformed stream:
4069            // silently overwriting would merge two distinct calls into one
4070            // synthetic record (last id/name + concatenated arguments) in
4071            // the attested trajectory. Fail the stream instead, mirroring
4072            // `reject_metric_regression`. Late repeats of the SAME values
4073            // remain accepted.
4074            if let (Some(existing), Some(new)) = (partial.id.as_deref(), delta.id.as_deref()) {
4075                if existing != new {
4076                    return Err(format!(
4077                        "provider reused tool-call index {} with conflicting id",
4078                        delta.index
4079                    ));
4080                }
4081            }
4082            if let (Some(existing), Some(new)) = (partial.name.as_deref(), delta.name.as_deref()) {
4083                if existing != new {
4084                    return Err(format!(
4085                        "provider reused tool-call index {} with conflicting name",
4086                        delta.index
4087                    ));
4088                }
4089            }
4090            if delta.id.is_some() {
4091                partial.id = delta.id;
4092            }
4093            if delta.name.is_some() {
4094                partial.name = delta.name;
4095            }
4096            push_bounded(&mut partial.arguments, &delta.arguments, "tool-call arguments")?;
4097        }
4098        if parsed.usage_reported {
4099            reject_metric_regression(
4100                "prompt tokens",
4101                &mut self.last_reported_prompt_tokens,
4102                parsed.metrics.prompt_tokens,
4103            )?;
4104            reject_metric_regression(
4105                "cached tokens",
4106                &mut self.last_reported_cached_tokens,
4107                parsed.metrics.cached_tokens,
4108            )?;
4109        }
4110        if parsed.cost_reported {
4111            reject_metric_regression(
4112                "cost",
4113                &mut self.last_reported_cost_usd_micros,
4114                Some(parsed.cost_usd_micros),
4115            )?;
4116        }
4117        if let Some(prompt) = parsed.metrics.prompt_tokens {
4118            self.response_metrics.prompt_tokens = Some(
4119                self.response_metrics
4120                    .prompt_tokens
4121                    .map_or(prompt, |current| current.max(prompt)),
4122            );
4123        }
4124        if let Some(cached) = parsed.metrics.cached_tokens {
4125            self.response_metrics.cached_tokens = Some(
4126                self.response_metrics
4127                    .cached_tokens
4128                    .map_or(cached, |current| current.max(cached)),
4129            );
4130        }
4131        let reported_completion = parsed.metrics.completion_tokens.unwrap_or(0);
4132        // Cumulative-usage contract (same accepted limitation as the
4133        // `cost_usd` note above): providers reporting `completion_tokens`
4134        // in usage frames are expected to report CUMULATIVELY (OpenAI
4135        // `stream_options.include_usage`, Anthropic message_delta).
4136        // A hostile/broken upstream emitting monotone non-decreasing
4137        // INCREMENTAL counts is indistinguishable from repeated
4138        // cumulative frames on the wire, so only the LAST frame's value
4139        // is charged/attested — an undercount bounded by the true
4140        // total, never an overcharge; the regression guard below still
4141        // fails the stream on any decrease.
4142        let delta = if parsed.usage_reported && parsed.completion_reported {
4143            let previous = self.last_reported_completion_tokens.unwrap_or(0);
4144            if reported_completion < previous {
4145                return Err("provider completion usage regressed".to_owned());
4146            }
4147            self.last_reported_completion_tokens = Some(reported_completion);
4148            let delta = reported_completion.saturating_sub(self.charged_completion_tokens);
4149            // Authoritative usage overrides any prior estimate. The
4150            // regression check above guarantees monotonicity across
4151            // authoritative frames, so `max()` here would only keep a
4152            // stale estimate that happened to exceed the true count —
4153            // and that estimate lands in the attested `completion_tokens`
4154            // recorded on the ATIF step, signed receipt, and session
4155            // totals. Trigger: content chunks land with `"usage": null`
4156            // (OpenAI `stream_options.include_usage`), the parser fills
4157            // in `approx_tokens`, and those estimates get folded into
4158            // `response_metrics.completion_tokens` via the estimate
4159            // branch below; a final cumulative `{"usage":{"completion_tokens":6}}`
4160            // with the accumulated estimate at 10 would attest 10.
4161            self.response_metrics.completion_tokens = Some(reported_completion);
4162            delta
4163        } else {
4164            let total = self
4165                .response_metrics
4166                .completion_tokens
4167                .unwrap_or(0)
4168                .checked_add(reported_completion)
4169                .filter(|total| *total <= pv_core::error::JCS_SAFE_MAX)
4170                .ok_or_else(|| "provider completion-token total exceeds JCS-safe bounds".to_owned())?;
4171            self.response_metrics.completion_tokens = Some(total);
4172            reported_completion
4173        };
4174        if delta == 0 {
4175            return Ok(0);
4176        }
4177        self.charged_completion_tokens = self
4178            .charged_completion_tokens
4179            .checked_add(delta)
4180            .ok_or_else(|| "charged completion-token counter overflow".to_owned())?;
4181        self.rates
4182            .record(&crate::pipeline::principal_id_for_budget(&self.identity), delta);
4183        Ok(delta)
4184    }
4185
4186    fn begin_budget_check(&mut self, delta: u64, continuation: BudgetContinuation) {
4187        let store = Arc::clone(&self.store);
4188        let session_id = self.session.id.clone();
4189        let budget = self.budget.clone();
4190        let principal = self.principal_budget.clone();
4191        let task = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
4192            // Principal first, mirroring admission's debit order and its
4193            // refund discipline: if the principal debit lands but the
4194            // session ledger refuses, the principal amount is refunded so
4195            // a refused stream tail is non-consumptive on both ledgers.
4196            if let Some((principal_id, spec)) = principal.as_ref() {
4197                match pv_state::ActionBudget::for_principal(store.as_ref(), principal_id, spec)
4198                    .try_tokens(delta)
4199                    .map_err(|error| format!("token budget backend failed closed (principal): {error}"))?
4200                {
4201                    pv_state::BudgetDecision::Refused { limit, cap } => {
4202                        return Ok(pv_state::BudgetDecision::Refused {
4203                            limit: format!("principal.{limit}"),
4204                            cap,
4205                        });
4206                    }
4207                    pv_state::BudgetDecision::Allowed { .. } => {}
4208                }
4209            }
4210            // Mirror admission's backend-ERROR arm too
4211            // (`prepare_chat`): a session-ledger backend failure after
4212            // the principal debit landed must also refund, or every
4213            // transient store blip mid-stream leaks the delta on the
4214            // principal ledger — which persists across sessions and
4215            // never heals.
4216            let decision =
4217                match pv_state::ActionBudget::new(store.as_ref(), &session_id, &budget).try_tokens(delta) {
4218                    Ok(decision) => decision,
4219                    Err(error) => {
4220                        if let Some((principal_id, spec)) = principal.as_ref() {
4221                            pv_state::ActionBudget::for_principal(store.as_ref(), principal_id, spec)
4222                                .refund_tokens(delta);
4223                        }
4224                        return Err(format!("token budget backend failed closed: {error}"));
4225                    }
4226                };
4227            if matches!(decision, pv_state::BudgetDecision::Refused { .. }) {
4228                if let Some((principal_id, spec)) = principal.as_ref() {
4229                    pv_state::ActionBudget::for_principal(store.as_ref(), principal_id, spec)
4230                        .refund_tokens(delta);
4231                }
4232            }
4233            Ok(decision)
4234        });
4235        self.pending_budget = Some(PendingBudget {
4236            task,
4237            continuation,
4238            delta,
4239        });
4240    }
4241
4242    fn submit_response_capture(
4243        &mut self,
4244        failure: Option<(pv_events::StopReason, String)>,
4245    ) -> Result<(), crate::worker::SubmitError> {
4246        if self.capture_attempted {
4247            return Ok(());
4248        }
4249        self.capture_attempted = true;
4250        let choices = std::mem::take(&mut self.response_choices);
4251        let multi_choice = choices.len() > 1;
4252        let reasoning = {
4253            let joined = choices
4254                .values()
4255                .filter(|capture| !capture.reasoning.is_empty())
4256                .map(|capture| capture.reasoning.as_str())
4257                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
4258                .join("\n\n");
4259            (!joined.is_empty()).then_some(joined)
4260        };
4261        // The attested message: the plain string for one choice, one
4262        // text part per choice (tagged with its index) for `n > 1`.
4263        let message_text = choices
4264            .values()
4265            .map(|capture| capture.content.as_str())
4266            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
4267            .join("\n");
4268        let message = if multi_choice {
4269            Value::Array(
4270                choices
4271                    .iter()
4272                    .map(|(index, capture)| {
4273                        json!({"type": "text", "text": capture.content, "choice_index": index})
4274                    })
4275                    .collect(),
4276            )
4277        } else {
4278            Value::String(message_text.clone())
4279        };
4280        let native_finish_reason = aggregate_finish_reason(&choices);
4281        // Materialize the tool-call list up front so we can fall back to
4282        // its content when the response body has neither an assistant
4283        // message nor reasoning. Without this, tool-only
4284        // responses (a legitimate agent mode: "return only tool_calls,
4285        // no assistant text") collapsed to an all-zero embedding at
4286        // `pv_loopdetect::embed`, which the breaker treats as a hostile
4287        // duplicate and grows the loop streak on — so a healthy agent
4288        // that just happened to be tool-driven would get flagged as
4289        // looping after the min-tokens threshold.
4290        let tool_calls: Vec<pv_atif::ToolCall> = std::mem::take(&mut self.response_tool_calls)
4291            .into_iter()
4292            .map(|((choice_index, _), partial)| {
4293                let arguments = normalize_tool_call_arguments(&partial.arguments);
4294                pv_atif::ToolCall {
4295                    tool_call_id: partial.id.unwrap_or_else(pv_core::new_event_uid),
4296                    function_name: partial.name.unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".to_owned()),
4297                    arguments,
4298                    // Only a multi-choice response needs to say which
4299                    // choice issued the call; single-choice steps keep
4300                    // the historical shape.
4301                    extra: multi_choice.then(|| json!({"choice_index": choice_index})),
4302                }
4303            })
4304            .collect();
4305        let analysis_text = if let Some(text) = reasoning.clone() {
4306            text
4307        } else if !message_text.is_empty() {
4308            message_text.clone()
4309        } else if !tool_calls.is_empty() {
4310            tool_calls
4311                .iter()
4312                .map(|tc| format!("{}({})", tc.function_name, tc.arguments))
4313                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
4314                .join(" ")
4315        } else {
4316            String::new()
4317        };
4318        // Skip loop analysis when the response is genuinely empty (no
4319        // reasoning, no message, no tool calls) — a zero-vector embed
4320        // would otherwise poison the breaker's duplicate detection.
4321        let analyze_loop = !analysis_text.is_empty();
4322        // The failure arm records the CALLER's stop-reason verdict:
4323        // BudgetExceeded only for the genuine mid-stream cap refusal,
4324        // Other for everything else (network cuts, garbled frames,
4325        // quota-backend outages, client disconnects). Hard-coding
4326        // BudgetExceeded here previously attested every one of those
4327        // as an enforcement stop.
4328        let (class, status, stop_reason, payload) = if let Some((failure_reason, reason)) = failure {
4329            let mut payload = json!({"reason": reason, "direction": "upstream_response"});
4330            if let (Some(policy), Some(object)) = (self.failure_policy.take(), payload.as_object_mut()) {
4331                object.insert("policy".to_owned(), Value::String(policy));
4332            }
4333            (
4334                pv_events::EventClass::StopReason,
4335                pv_events::StatusId::Failure,
4336                Some(failure_reason),
4337                payload,
4338            )
4339        } else if !self.upstream_status.is_success() {
4340            (
4341                pv_events::EventClass::StopReason,
4342                pv_events::StatusId::Failure,
4343                Some(pv_events::StopReason::Other),
4344                json!({
4345                    "direction": "upstream_response",
4346                    "http_status": self.upstream_status.as_u16(),
4347                }),
4348            )
4349        } else if let Some(native) = &native_finish_reason {
4350            // Cross-provider stop-reason normalization for the tool-use
4351            // shape. OpenAI emits `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` and
4352            // Anthropic emits `stop_reason: "tool_use"` when the model
4353            // decides to invoke tools; both map cleanly to
4354            // StopReason::ToolUse. Gemini does NOT: it emits
4355            // `finishReason: STOP` and expects the client to notice
4356            // `functionCall` parts in the candidate content. Left un-
4357            // normalized, a receipt attests StopReason::Stop for the
4358            // Gemini flow — an auditor grouping sessions by stop_reason
4359            // would count Gemini tool sessions as clean stops and
4360            // OpenAI/Anthropic tool sessions as tool_use, corrupting
4361            // any cross-provider tool-invocation analytics. This is the
4362            // adapter-leak `ProviderAdapter` exists to prevent. Verified
4363            // live pre-fix: a Gemini stream with a functionCall part
4364            // followed by finishReason:STOP journalled stop_reason_id=1.
4365            let mapped = map_finish_reason(native);
4366            let normalized = if mapped == pv_events::StopReason::Stop && !tool_calls.is_empty() {
4367                pv_events::StopReason::ToolUse
4368            } else {
4369                mapped
4370            };
4371            (
4372                pv_events::EventClass::StopReason,
4373                pv_events::StatusId::Success,
4374                Some(normalized),
4375                json!({
4376                    "direction": "upstream_response",
4377                    "finish_reason": native,
4378                    "http_status": self.upstream_status.as_u16(),
4379                }),
4380            )
4381        } else if self.is_sse {
4382            // An SSE stream that
4383            // ended without ANY finish_reason chunk is a truncated
4384            // generation — provider crash, LB idle-timeout, worker
4385            // OOM. OpenAI-protocol streams always carry a
4386            // finish_reason chunk before [DONE], so its absence must
4387            // not be attested as a complete success: a compliance
4388            // reviewer could not otherwise distinguish a truncated
4389            // response from a finished one (previously this shape
4390            // recorded StatusId::Success with no stop reason — and a
4391            // zero-byte 200 stream looked identical to a real one).
4392            (
4393                pv_events::EventClass::StopReason,
4394                pv_events::StatusId::Unknown,
4395                Some(pv_events::StopReason::Other),
4396                json!({
4397                    "direction": "upstream_response",
4398                    "http_status": self.upstream_status.as_u16(),
4399                    "truncated": true,
4400                    "reason": "stream ended without a finish_reason chunk",
4401                }),
4402            )
4403        } else if message_text.is_empty() && reasoning.is_none() && tool_calls.is_empty() {
4404            // Non-SSE 200 whose body carried NO finish_reason and NO
4405            // content — e.g. a bare `{"choices":[]}` (or `{}`-shaped)
4406            // body from a broken shim. Every compliant non-streaming
4407            // completion carries choices[0].finish_reason, so this is
4408            // not attestable as a clean success: previously it recorded
4409            // StatusId::Success with no stop reason, making an
4410            // empty-response failure indistinguishable from a real
4411            // completion in the signed audit trail (the SSE sibling
4412            // branch above closed the same hole for streams).
4413            (
4414                pv_events::EventClass::StopReason,
4415                pv_events::StatusId::Unknown,
4416                Some(pv_events::StopReason::Other),
4417                json!({
4418                    "direction": "upstream_response",
4419                    "http_status": self.upstream_status.as_u16(),
4420                    "truncated": true,
4421                    "reason": "response carried no choices, content, or finish_reason",
4422                }),
4423            )
4424        } else {
4425            (
4426                pv_events::EventClass::Session,
4427                pv_events::StatusId::Success,
4428                None,
4429                json!({
4430                    "direction": "upstream_response",
4431                    "http_status": self.upstream_status.as_u16(),
4432                }),
4433            )
4434        };
4435        // Enforcement side of the correction: refund the heuristic
4436        // over-charge to the session ledger — an SDK retry loop on a
4437        // CJK-heavy conversation otherwise drains max_tokens 3-4×
4438        // faster than the provider actually bills. Only the
4439        // over-charge direction is compensated (provider < billed);
4440        // an under-estimate conservatively stands (charging more
4441        // mid-stream could turn a delivered response into a
4442        // retroactive refusal). The principal ledger keeps the
4443        // conservative debit — its caps are coarse anti-abuse bounds,
4444        // not billing.
4445        if let Some(provider) = self.response_metrics.prompt_tokens {
4446            let over_charge = self.billed_prompt_tokens.saturating_sub(provider);
4447            if over_charge > 0 {
4448                pv_state::ActionBudget::new(self.store.as_ref(), &self.session.id, &self.budget)
4449                    .refund_tokens(over_charge);
4450            }
4451        }
4452        // Same correction for the completion side: per-chunk estimates
4453        // (content frames with `"usage": null`) debit the ledger as the
4454        // stream progresses, and an authoritative final usage frame LOWER
4455        // than the accumulated estimate leaves `charged_completion_tokens`
4456        // above the attested count with no refund path — the over-debit
4457        // outlives the response and starves the session's remaining
4458        // budget. Only the over-charge direction is compensated,
4459        // mirroring the prompt-side rationale above.
4460        if let Some(provider) = self.response_metrics.completion_tokens {
4461            let over_charge = self.charged_completion_tokens.saturating_sub(provider);
4462            if over_charge > 0 {
4463                pv_state::ActionBudget::new(self.store.as_ref(), &self.session.id, &self.budget)
4464                    .refund_tokens(over_charge);
4465            }
4466        }
4467        let permit = self
4468            .response_permit
4469            .take()
4470            .ok_or(crate::worker::SubmitError::Closed)?;
4471        permit.submit(
4472            &self.worker,
4473            crate::worker::WorkerJob {
4474                session: Arc::clone(&self.session),
4475                identity: self.identity.clone(),
4476                class,
4477                payload: {
4478                    let mut payload = payload;
4479                    if let (false, Some(object)) = (self.egress_transforms.is_empty(), payload.as_object_mut()) {
4480                        object.insert(
4481                            "transforms".to_owned(),
4482                            Value::Array(
4483                                self.egress_transforms
4484                                    .iter()
4485                                    .map(|(policy, replacements)| json!({"policy": policy, "replacements": replacements}))
4486                                    .collect(),
4487                            ),
4488                        );
4489                    }
4490                    payload
4491                },
4492                text: analysis_text,
4493                analyze_loop,
4494                status,
4495                stop_reason,
4496                native_stop_reason: native_finish_reason,
4497                metrics: self.response_metrics,
4498                cost_usd_micros: self.response_cost_usd_micros,
4499                // Reconcile the admission-time heuristic
4500                // against the provider's reported usage. The correction
4501                // rides the terminal record so ALL folds (live + both
4502                // recovery paths, via the unified
4503                // ActiveJournalRecord fold) attest the provider-true
4504                // prompt count; CJK-heavy workloads previously
4505                // over-reported 3-4× into the signed receipt.
4506                prompt_token_correction: self.response_metrics.prompt_tokens.map_or(0i64, |provider| {
4507                    let provider = i64::try_from(provider).unwrap_or(i64::MAX);
4508                    let billed = i64::try_from(self.billed_prompt_tokens).unwrap_or(i64::MAX);
4509                    provider.saturating_sub(billed)
4510                }),
4511                atif: Some(crate::worker::AtifCapture {
4512                    source: pv_atif::Source::Agent,
4513                    message,
4514                    reasoning_content: reasoning,
4515                    model_name: self.response_model.take(),
4516                    tool_calls: (!tool_calls.is_empty()).then_some(tool_calls),
4517                    observation: None,
4518                    llm_call_count: Some(1),
4519                }),
4520                response_marker: self.response_marker.take(),
4521                response_attempt: Some(crate::worker::ResponseAttempt {
4522                    id: self.response_attempt_id.clone(),
4523                    terminal: true,
4524                }),
4525            },
4526        )?;
4527        Ok(())
4528    }
4529}

4531enum BudgetContinuation {
4532    Emit(Bytes),
4533    ContinueNonSse,
4534    FinishSse,
4535    FinishNonSse,
4536    /// A held stream: keep reading, relay nothing yet.
4537    Hold,
4538}
4539
4540struct PendingBudget {
4541    task: tokio::task::JoinHandle<Result<pv_state::BudgetDecision, String>>,
4542    continuation: BudgetContinuation,
4543    /// The completion-token delta this check would debit. `absorb_frame`
4544    /// already folded it into `charged_completion_tokens`, but the debit
4545    /// only lands when the task resolves `Allowed` — every other outcome
4546    /// (mid-stream refusal, backend outage, drop-abort) must roll the
4547    /// delta back out of `charged`, or the terminal over-charge refund
4548    /// (`charged − reported`) credits tokens that were never debited
4549    /// (same invariant as the drain-loop rollback in
4550    /// `drain_protocol_frames`).
4551    delta: u64,
4552}
4553
4554#[derive(Default)]
4555struct PartialToolCall {
4556    id: Option<String>,
4557    name: Option<String>,
4558    arguments: String,
4559}
4560
4561/// Highest `choices[].index` the relay accumulates (exclusive). Matches
4562/// the request-side `n` cap with headroom for providers that number
4563/// choices sparsely.
4564const MAX_CHOICE_INDEX: u64 = 128;
4565
4566/// What the relay has captured for one choice of a response.
4567#[derive(Default, Debug)]
4568struct ChoiceCapture {
4569    content: String,
4570    reasoning: String,
4571    finish_reason: Option<String>,
4572}
4573
4574/// The finish reason attested for a whole response. One choice: its
4575/// own reason. Several choices: the most consequential reason wins
4576/// (content filter over length over tool use over anything else over
4577/// a plain stop), and a choice that never finished makes the response
4578/// truncated (`None`), exactly like a single truncated stream.
4579fn aggregate_finish_reason(choices: &std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, ChoiceCapture>) -> Option<String> {
4580    if choices.is_empty() || choices.values().any(|capture| capture.finish_reason.is_none()) {
4581        return None;
4582    }
4583    let rank = |reason: &str| match map_finish_reason(reason) {
4584        pv_events::StopReason::ContentFilter => 4,
4585        pv_events::StopReason::MaxTokens => 3,
4586        pv_events::StopReason::ToolUse => 2,
4587        pv_events::StopReason::Stop => 0,
4588        _ => 1,
4589    };
4590    choices
4591        .values()
4592        .filter_map(|capture| capture.finish_reason.as_deref())
4593        .max_by_key(|reason| rank(reason))
4594        .map(str::to_owned)
4595}
4596
4597/// One choice's share of a parsed frame.
4598#[derive(Debug, Default)]
4599pub(crate) struct ParsedChoiceDelta {
4600    pub(crate) index: u64,
4601    pub(crate) content: String,
4602    pub(crate) reasoning: String,
4603    pub(crate) finish_reason: Option<String>,
4604}

4606#[derive(Debug)]
4607pub(crate) struct ProviderToolCallDelta {
4608    /// The `choices[].index` this delta belongs to. Multi-choice
4609    /// (`n > 1`) responses reuse tool-call index 0 in every choice, so
4610    /// reassembly must key on (choice, tool index) or distinct calls
4611    /// merge into one corrupt audit record. (Anthropic has no choices;
4612    /// its adapter always uses 0.)
4613    pub(crate) choice_index: u64,
4614    /// Stream-global tool-call slot within the choice for incremental
4615    /// dialects (OpenAI `tool_calls[].index`, Anthropic content-block
4616    /// index). For `complete` deltas this is only the part's position
4617    /// within the CURRENT frame and is NOT stable across frames —
4618    /// `absorb_frame` must ignore it and allocate a fresh slot.
4619    pub(crate) index: u64,
4620    /// True when the delta carries an entire tool call (Gemini
4621    /// `functionCall` parts arrive whole, never split across frames).
4622    /// Complete deltas never need cross-frame accumulation keyed on
4623    /// `index`; merging them by frame-local position collides distinct
4624    /// calls emitted in separate chunks.
4625    pub(crate) complete: bool,
4626    pub(crate) id: Option<String>,
4627    pub(crate) name: Option<String>,
4628    pub(crate) arguments: String,
4629}

4631#[derive(Debug)]
4632pub(crate) struct ParsedProviderChunk {
4633    pub(crate) model_name: Option<String>,
4634    pub(crate) metrics: pv_events::EventMetrics,
4635    pub(crate) usage_reported: bool,
4636    /// True only when the provider itself supplied `completion_tokens`
4637    /// (as opposed to the per-chunk heuristic estimate filled in below).
4638    /// `absorb_frame`'s cumulative-usage branch must key on this, not on
4639    /// `usage_reported` alone: a usage object without a completion count
4640    /// (`{"prompt_tokens": 7}` or `"completion_tokens": null`) would
4641    /// otherwise feed a non-cumulative estimate into cumulative math.
4642    pub(crate) completion_reported: bool,
4643    pub(crate) cost_usd_micros: u64,
4644    pub(crate) cost_reported: bool,
4645    pub(crate) has_choices: bool,
4646    pub(crate) tool_call_deltas: Vec<ProviderToolCallDelta>,
4647    /// Per-choice text, reasoning and finish reason, keyed by the
4648    /// provider's `choices[].index`.
4649    pub(crate) choices: Vec<ParsedChoiceDelta>,
4650}
4651
4652fn reject_metric_regression(
4653    field: &str,
4654    previous: &mut Option<u64>,
4655    current: Option<u64>,
4656) -> Result<(), String> {
4657    let Some(current) = current else {
4658        return Ok(());
4659    };
4660    if previous.is_some_and(|previous| current < previous) {
4661        return Err(format!("provider {field} regressed"));
4662    }
4663    *previous = Some(current);
4664    Ok(())
4665}
4666
4667fn push_bounded(target: &mut String, value: &str, field: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
4668    let size = target
4669        .len()
4670        .checked_add(value.len())
4671        .ok_or_else(|| format!("{field} size overflow"))?;
4672    if size > MAX_PROVIDER_FIELD_BYTES {
4673        return Err(format!("{field} exceeds {MAX_PROVIDER_FIELD_BYTES} bytes"));
4674    }
4675    target.push_str(value);
4676    Ok(())
4677}

4679/// Fuzz-only shim over the internal `parse_provider_chunk` — accepts
4680/// arbitrary bytes and returns nothing (the fuzz harness just cares
4681/// that the parser is total under Unicode / SSE malformation). Not
4682/// part of the stable API; see [`crate::fuzz`] for the documented
4683/// re-export path.
4684#[doc(hidden)]
4685pub fn __fuzz_parse_provider_chunk(raw: &[u8]) {
4686    if let Ok(s) = std::str::from_utf8(raw) {
4687        let _ = parse_provider_chunk(s);
4688    }
4689}
4690
4691/// Fuzz-only shim over the internal `sse_frame_end` framing scanner.
4692/// See [`__fuzz_parse_provider_chunk`] for rationale.
4693#[doc(hidden)]
4694pub fn __fuzz_sse_frame_end(raw: &[u8]) {
4695    let _ = sse_frame_end(raw);
4696}
4697
4698pub(crate) fn sse_frame_end(buffer: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
4699    let mut line_start = 0usize;
4700    let mut index = 0usize;
4701    while index < buffer.len() {
4702        let byte = buffer.get(index).copied()?;
4703        let newline = match byte {
4704            b'\r' if buffer.get(index + 1) == Some(&b'\n') => 2,
4705            b'\r' if buffer.get(index + 1).is_none() => return None,
4706            b'\r' | b'\n' => 1,
4707            _ => {
4708                index += 1;
4709                continue;
4710            }
4711        };
4712        if index == line_start {
4713            return Some(index + newline);
4714        }
4715        index += newline;
4716        line_start = index;
4717    }
4718    None
4719}
