10768    #[test]
10769    #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)] // xorshift indices; truncation is harmless fuzz entropy
10770    fn fuzz_parse_provider_chunk_is_total() {
10771        // Randomized totality check (hand-rolled xorshift so no
10772        // new dev-dependency): mutations of valid frames plus raw garbage
10773        // must never panic the parser, only return Ok/Err.
10774        let mut state = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15u64;
10775        let mut next = move || {
10776            state ^= state << 13;
10777            state ^= state >> 7;
10778            state ^= state << 17;
10779            state
10780        };
10781        let seeds: Vec<&str> = vec![
10782            "data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"hi\"}}],\"usage\":null}\n\n",
10783            "data: {\"model\":\"m\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"a\",\"reasoning_content\":\"r\"},\"finish_reason\":\"stop\"}],\"usage\":{\"prompt_tokens\":10,\"completion_tokens\":3,\"cost_usd\":0.001,\"prompt_tokens_details\":{\"cached_tokens\":4}}}\n\n",
10784            "data: {\"choices\":[{\"index\":1,\"delta\":{\"tool_calls\":[{\"index\":0,\"id\":\"c\",\"function\":{\"name\":\"f\",\"arguments\":\"{}\"}}]}}]}\n\n",
10785            "data: [DONE]\n\n",
10786            "event: message\ndata: {\"choices\":[]}\n\n",
10787            "{\"choices\":[{\"message\":{\"content\":\"x\",\"tool_calls\":[{\"id\":\"a\",\"function\":{\"name\":\"n\",\"arguments\":\"{}\"}}]}}],\"usage\":{\"completion_tokens\":1}}",
10788        ];
10789        for _ in 0..200_000 {
10790            let seed = seeds[(next() as usize) % seeds.len()];
10791            let mut bytes = seed.as_bytes().to_vec();
10792            for _ in 0..=(next() % 8) {
10793                match next() % 3 {
10794                    0 if !bytes.is_empty() => {
10795                        let idx = (next() as usize) % bytes.len();
10796                        bytes[idx] = (next() & 0xFF) as u8;
10797                    }
10798                    1 if !bytes.is_empty() => {
10799                        let idx = (next() as usize) % bytes.len();
10800                        bytes.truncate(idx);
10801                    }
10802                    _ => {
10803                        let idx = if bytes.is_empty() {
10804                            0
10805                        } else {
10806                            (next() as usize) % bytes.len()
10807                        };
10808                        bytes.insert(idx, (next() & 0xFF) as u8);
10809                    }
10810                }
10811            }
10812            let raw = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned();
10813            let _ = parse_provider_chunk(&raw);
10814            let _ = sse_frame_end(&bytes);
10815        }
10816    }

10839    #[test]
10840    fn null_usage_chunks_are_not_reported_usage() {
10841        // OpenAI `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` emits
10842        // `"usage": null` on every content chunk; only the final chunk
10843        // carries the real object. A null usage must behave exactly like
10844        // an absent key: usage_reported = false, completion tokens
10845        // estimated. Treating it as reported previously fed absorb_frame's
10846        // cumulative branch per-chunk estimates → spurious "usage
10847        // regressed" stream kill + session quarantine.
10848        let raw = r#"data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello"}}],"usage":null}"#;
10849        let parsed = parse_provider_chunk(raw).unwrap().unwrap();
10850        assert!(!parsed.usage_reported, "null usage must not count as reported");
10851        assert!(!parsed.completion_reported);
10852        assert_eq!(parsed.choices[0].content, "Hello");
10853        // Estimated from the delta text, not taken from the null object.
10854        assert_eq!(
10855            parsed.metrics.completion_tokens,
10856            Some(pv_core::tokens::approx_tokens("Hello"))
10857        );
10858        // Null fields inside a real usage object are tolerated like
10859        // absent keys (some OpenAI-compatible shims emit them).
10860        let raw = r#"data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"x"}}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":7,"completion_tokens":null}}"#;
10861        let parsed = parse_provider_chunk(raw).unwrap().unwrap();
10862        assert!(parsed.usage_reported);
10863        assert!(
10864            !parsed.completion_reported,
10865            "a null completion count must not drive cumulative-usage math"
10866        );
10867        assert_eq!(parsed.metrics.prompt_tokens, Some(7));
10868        assert_eq!(
10869            parsed.metrics.completion_tokens,
10870            Some(pv_core::tokens::approx_tokens("x"))
10871        );
10872    }

10933    /// Leading BOM (U+FEFF) on an SSE stream must be stripped per
10934    /// §9.2.4. Rust's `.trim()` and `.trim_start()` do NOT remove
10935    /// U+FEFF (char::is_whitespace returns false for it), so without
10936    /// an explicit strip the very first `data:` line would parse as
10937    /// `"\u{FEFF}data:"` and the frame would take the non-SSE path
10938    /// where `serde_json::from_str` chokes on the BOM prefix.
10939    #[test]
10940    fn parse_provider_chunk_strips_leading_bom() {
10941        let raw = "\u{feff}data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"hi\"}}]}\n\n";
10942        let parsed = parse_provider_chunk(raw)
10943            .expect("BOM-prefixed SSE frame must parse")
10944            .expect("must yield a chunk");
10945        assert_eq!(parsed.choices[0].content, "hi");
10946    }

10948    /// SSE §9.2.8: an SSE client dispatches events by name, so
10949    /// `event: error\ndata: {model-shaped-JSON}` is delivered to the
10950    /// browser/SDK's `error` listener — NOT the default `message`
10951    /// listener. ProofVisor attributes captured `data:` payloads to
10952    /// the signed receipt / ATIF as if they were model output, so a
10953    /// hostile upstream (rogue provider, TLS-MITM at egress mesh, a
10954    /// misconfigured caching proxy) could forge receipt content while
10955    /// the user's UI showed nothing suspicious. Refuse the frame with
10956    /// a diagnostic so the caller marks capture-failed rather than
10957    /// signs attributable content that never was displayed.
10958    #[test]
10959    fn parse_provider_chunk_refuses_non_message_sse_event_types() {
10960        for event in ["error", "ping", "custom_signal"] {
10961            let raw = format!(
10962                "event: {event}\ndata: {{\"choices\":[{{\"delta\":{{\"content\":\"forged\"}}}}]}}\n\n"
10963            );
10964            let err = match parse_provider_chunk(&raw) {
10965                Ok(_) => panic!("event type {event:?} must be refused"),
10966                Err(error) => error,
10967            };
10968            assert!(
10969                err.contains("unsupported event type") && err.contains(event),
10970                "expected diagnostic naming event type {event:?}, got: {err}"
10971            );
10972        }
10973        // Explicit `event: message` is accepted (spec default) — must
10974        // NOT be refused by the same guard.
10975        let ok_raw = "event: message\ndata: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"hi\"}}]}\n\n";
10976        let parsed = match parse_provider_chunk(ok_raw) {
10977            Ok(Some(chunk)) => chunk,
10978            Ok(None) => panic!("explicit event: message must yield a chunk"),
10979            Err(error) => panic!("explicit event: message must be accepted, got: {error}"),
10980        };
10981        assert_eq!(parsed.choices[0].content, "hi");
10982    }
10983
10984    /// A named SSE event with EMPTY
10985    /// `data:` (or no `data:` at all) is a keepalive/heartbeat that
10986    /// carries no audit surface — refusing it (and thereby aborting
10987    /// the whole client stream + sealing the session) was
10988    /// over-restrictive. Such frames must be treated as skip
10989    /// (returning `Ok(None)`), leaving the full-refusal semantics
10990    /// intact for frames whose `data:` field would otherwise be
10991    /// attributed to the model output under the wrong event name.
10992    #[test]
10993    fn parse_provider_chunk_treats_dataless_named_events_as_keepalives() {
10994        for raw in [
10995            "event: ping\n\n",
10996            "event: heartbeat\n\n",
10997            "event: keep-alive\ndata:\n\n",
10998            "event: status\ndata:   \n\n",
10999        ] {
11000            match parse_provider_chunk(raw) {
11001                Ok(None) => {}
11002                Ok(Some(_)) => panic!("dataless named event must not yield a chunk: {raw:?}"),
11003                Err(error) => panic!("dataless named event {raw:?} must not fail the stream (D7): {error}"),
11004            }
11005        }
11006        // A named event that DOES carry attributable data must still
11007        // be refused — the security posture the original guard exists
11008        // for is preserved.
11009        let poison = "event: error\ndata: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"x\"}}]}\n\n";
11010        assert!(
11011            parse_provider_chunk(poison).is_err(),
11012            "named event with non-empty data must still be refused"
11013        );
11014    }

11016    #[test]
11017    fn parse_provider_chunk_treats_done_variants_as_stream_end() {
11018        for raw in [
11019            "data: [DONE]\ndata: [DONE]\n\n",
11020            "data: [DONE]  \n\n",
11021            "data:\ndata: [DONE]\n\n",
11022        ] {
11023            let result = parse_provider_chunk(raw);
11024            match result {
11025                Ok(None) => {}
11026                Ok(Some(_)) => panic!("[DONE] variant must terminate stream (None) for {raw:?}"),
11027                Err(error) => panic!("[DONE] variant must not fail parse: {raw:?}: {error}"),
11028            }
11029        }
11030    }

11032    /// R44 Finding 3: OpenAI-compat gateways that batch a final
11033    /// `[DONE]` under a summary event name (e.g.
11034    /// `event: summary\ndata: [DONE]\n\n`) must not fail-close the
11035    /// stream tail. `[DONE]` carries no attributable content, so the
11036    /// named-event refusal at parse_provider_chunk's line ~3465 must
11037    /// treat `data:` lines that are ALL `[DONE]` or empty as a
11038    /// keepalive, matching the Anthropic parser's ordering which
11039    /// short-circuits `[DONE]` before its event-type check.
11040    #[test]
11041    fn parse_provider_chunk_done_under_named_event_is_keepalive() {
11042        for raw in [
11043            "event: summary\ndata: [DONE]\n\n",
11044            "event: error\ndata: [DONE]\n\n",
11045            "event: custom\ndata:\ndata: [DONE]\n\n",
11046            "event: batched\ndata: [DONE]\ndata: [DONE]\n\n",
11047        ] {
11048            match parse_provider_chunk(raw) {
11049                Ok(None) => {}
11050                Ok(Some(_)) => panic!(
11051                    "[DONE] under named event {raw:?} must not yield a chunk (no attributable content)"
11052                ),
11053                Err(error) => {
11054                    panic!("[DONE] under named event {raw:?} must not fail-close the stream: {error}")
11055                }
11056            }
11057        }
11058        // A named event with a mix of [DONE] AND real content must
11059        // still refuse — the content bytes would otherwise be
11060        // attributed to the wrong SSE listener per §9.2.8.
11061        let mixed = "event: error\ndata: [DONE]\ndata: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"x\"}}]}\n\n";
11062        assert!(
11063            parse_provider_chunk(mixed).is_err(),
11064            "named event with mixed [DONE] + real content must still refuse: {mixed:?}"
11065        );
11066    }

11068    /// SSE §9.2.6: the `data:` field strips exactly one leading
11069    /// U+0020 SPACE — no more, and no other whitespace class. A
11070    /// regression to `.trim_start()` would eat runs of Unicode
11071    /// whitespace and silently corrupt payloads whose second byte
11072    /// after `data:` is another space or a tab.
11073    ///
11074    /// Distinguishing input: `data:  hi\n\n` — two spaces then a
11075    /// literal `hi`. Non-SSE parse via serde_json would fail on
11076    /// `"hi"` unquoted, so the frame goes through the SSE path where
11077    /// the `data:` accumulator kept one leading space (spec-compliant)
11078    /// and serde_json then fails on ` hi` — this is exactly what the
11079    /// spec's "leave everything after the first space verbatim"
11080    /// behaviour dictates. A `.trim_start()` regression would silently
11081    /// consume both spaces and produce the same (still-invalid) input.
11082    /// We instead pick a JSON payload where the number of leading
11083    /// spaces changes the parse result: `{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":" hi"}}]}`
11084    /// with wire `data:  {"choices"...}` — under `strip_prefix(' ')`
11085    /// the accumulated frame starts with a space then `{`, both parse
11086    /// fine and the extracted `content` field is `" hi"`; under
11087    /// `.trim_start()` the frame starts with `{`, also parses fine and
11088    /// yields the same `" hi"`. So parse content doesn't discriminate.
11089    ///
11090    /// Instead observe the raw data buffer that the parser builds:
11091    /// use a plain non-JSON `data:` value and assert the trimmed
11092    /// prefix. Since the parser now runs serde_json on the assembled
11093    /// frame, the only way to expose the trim behaviour is a test on
11094    /// a lower-level helper. We keep this test as a smoke check on a
11095    /// case where the frame *fails* differently: two-space prefix
11096    /// with a leading space kept produces a JSON parse failure the
11097    /// old `trim_start` would not have produced.
11098    #[test]
11099    fn parse_provider_chunk_strips_exactly_one_leading_space() {
11100        // Bare non-JSON `hello` — invalid JSON either way. With
11101        // `strip_prefix(' ')` (spec-correct) the parser accumulates
11102        // ` \thello` (space+tab+hello). With `.trim_start()` (buggy)
11103        // it accumulates `hello`. Both produce `Err(...)` from
11104        // serde_json but the reported column differs — the trimmed
11105        // form reports column 1 (immediate `h`); the correctly
11106        // preserved form reports a later column because of the
11107        // retained tab.
11108        let raw = "data:  \thello\n\n";
11109        let result = parse_provider_chunk(raw);
11110        let error = match result {
11111            Ok(_) => panic!("bare hello must not parse as valid provider frame"),
11112            Err(error) => error,
11113        };
11114        assert!(
11115            error.contains("column 2") || error.contains("column 3"),
11116            "expected error to name a column past the retained leading space+tab; \
11117             got: {error}"
11118        );
11119    }

11202    /// Refusing an unsupported Content-Encoding must retire the durable
11203    /// in-flight response marker and terminally fail the journalled
11204    /// response attempt — otherwise `recover_spooled_sessions`
11205    /// quarantines the session forever over a request the client
11206    /// already saw fail as a clean 502.
11207    #[tokio::test]
11208    async fn unsupported_content_encoding_refusal_retires_marker_and_attempt() {
11209        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
11210        let (state, provider) = test_state(directory.path()).await;
11211        let response = build_router(state.clone())
11212            .oneshot(chat_request_with_payload(
11213                "gzip-encoded",
11214                json!({
11215                    "model": "gzip-encoded",
11216                    "stream": false,
11217                    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]
11218                }),
11219            ))
11220            .await
11221            .unwrap();
11222        assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY);
11223        let body = axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 64 * 1024)
11224            .await
11225            .unwrap();
11226        let error = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&body).unwrap()["error"]["message"]
11227            .as_str()
11228            .unwrap()
11229            .to_owned();
11230        assert!(error.contains("Content-Encoding"), "unexpected error: {error}");
11231        let session = state.sessions.get("gzip-encoded").unwrap();
11232        session.wait_for_worker_jobs().await;
11233        crate::worker::ensure_no_inflight_responses(directory.path(), &state.journal_key)
11234            .await
11235            .expect("refusal must retire the in-flight response marker");
11236        let records = active_records(directory.path(), &state, "gzip-encoded");
11237        assert!(
11238            records
11239                .iter()
11240                .filter_map(|record| record.response_attempt.as_ref())
11241                .any(|attempt| attempt.terminal),
11242            "refusal must journal a terminal response attempt"
11243        );
11244        let event: pv_events::OcsfEvent =
11245            serde_json::from_value(records.last().unwrap().event.clone()).unwrap();
11246        assert_eq!(event.class_name, pv_events::EventClass::StopReason);
11247        assert_eq!(event.status_id, pv_events::StatusId::Failure.id());
11248        assert_eq!(event.payload["reason"], "upstream_unsupported_content_encoding");
11249        provider.abort();
11250    }

11255        let (mut state, provider) = test_state(directory.path()).await;
11256        let config = Arc::get_mut(&mut state.config).unwrap();
11257        config.breaker.min_tokens = 0;
11258        config.breaker.window = 3;
11259        let app = build_router(state.clone());
11260        for _ in 0..4 {
11261            let response = app.clone().oneshot(chat_request("response-loop")).await.unwrap();
11262            assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::OK);
11263            axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 64 * 1024)
11264                .await
11265                .unwrap();
11266            state
11267                .sessions
11268                .get("response-loop")
11269                .unwrap()
11270                .wait_for_worker_jobs()
11271                .await;
11272        }
11273        let blocked = app.oneshot(chat_request("response-loop")).await.unwrap();
11274        // Loop-breaker verdicts are permanent for the current session:
11275        // 403 stops mainstream LLM-SDK auto-retry loops that would
11276        // otherwise burn budget re-hitting the same breaker (see
11277        // pipeline.rs::PipelineError::status).
11278        assert_eq!(blocked.status(), StatusCode::FORBIDDEN);
11279        provider.abort();
11280    }

11381            assert!(parsed["error"]["code"].is_number(), "{parsed}");
11382        }

11384        // capture failure, not a session seal.
11385        assert!(
11386            !state.sessions.get("empty-success").unwrap().capture_failed(),
11387            "a choices-less response must not brick the session"
11388        );

11507    /// Completion-side twin of the prompt over-charge refund: content
11508    /// chunks arriving with `"usage": null` debit the ledger from
11509    /// per-chunk estimates, and an authoritative final usage LOWER than
11510    /// the accumulated estimate previously left the difference debited
11511    /// forever — the session's remaining budget shrank by tokens the
11512    /// provider never billed. The over-charge must be refunded at
11513    /// terminal capture.
11514    #[tokio::test]
11515    async fn completion_estimate_over_charge_is_refunded_after_authoritative_usage() {
11516        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
11517        let payload = json!({
11518            "model": "overcharged-completion",
11519            "stream": true,
11520            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]
11521        });
11522        // The 32-`a` content chunk estimates well above the
11523        // authoritative completion count of 1.
11524        let estimate = pv_core::tokens::approx_tokens(&"a".repeat(32));
11525        assert!(estimate > 1, "test premise: estimate must exceed usage");
11526        let prompt_tokens = pv_core::tokens::approx_tokens(&payload.to_string());
11527        let cap = prompt_tokens + estimate + 8;
11528        let (state, provider) = test_state_with_token_cap(directory.path(), Some(cap)).await;
11529        let response = build_router(state.clone())
11530            .oneshot(chat_request_with_payload("overcharged-completion", payload))
11531            .await
11532            .unwrap();
11533        assert!(axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 64 * 1024)
11534            .await
11535            .is_ok());
11536        let session = state.sessions.get("overcharged-completion").unwrap();
11537        session.wait_for_worker_jobs().await;
11538        // Authoritative usage: prompt 1 + completion 1. Both refunds
11539        // (prompt and completion) must have settled the ledger to a
11540        // spend of exactly 2.
11541        let ledger = pv_state::ActionBudget::new(
11542            state.store.as_ref(),
11543            "overcharged-completion",
11544            &state.config.budget,
11545        );
11546        assert!(
11547            ledger.try_tokens(cap - 2).unwrap().is_allowed(),
11548            "the completion-estimate over-charge must be refunded once authoritative usage arrives"
11549        );
11550        assert!(
11551            !ledger.try_tokens(1).unwrap().is_allowed(),
11552            "refunds must settle to the provider-billed spend, not more"
11553        );
11554        provider.abort();
11555    }

11557    /// No SSE mock ever split a frame across a stream
11558    /// chunk, though `protocol_buffer` exists precisely to reassemble
11559    /// one. Split a frame mid-way through a multi-byte UTF-8 scalar
11560    /// and prove the reassembled message reaches the audit trail
11561    /// intact (the non-SSE equivalent lives at `split-json`).
11562    #[tokio::test]
11563    async fn sse_frame_split_across_chunks_reassembles_before_capture() {
11564        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
11565        let (state, provider) = test_state(directory.path()).await;
11566        let response = build_router(state.clone())
11567            .oneshot(chat_request_with_payload(
11568                "split-sse",
11569                json!({
11570                    "model": "split-sse",
11571                    "stream": true,
11572                    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]
11573                }),
11574            ))
11575            .await
11576            .unwrap();
11577        let body = axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 64 * 1024)
11578            .await
11579            .unwrap();
11580        // The client sees the full reassembled bytes.
11581        assert!(
11582            String::from_utf8_lossy(&body).contains("héllo"),
11583            "client bytes truncated"
11584        );
11585        let session = state.sessions.get("split-sse").unwrap();
11586        session.wait_for_worker_jobs().await;
11587        assert!(
11588            !session.capture_failed(),
11589            "a chunk-split frame must not fail capture"
11590        );
11591        let crate::reconciler::FinalizeOutcome::Atif { path } = state
11592            .finalizer
11593            .close_session(session, StopReason::SessionClosed)
11594            .await
11595            .unwrap()
11596        else {
11597            panic!("expected ATIF")
11598        };
11599        let trajectory: pv_atif::Trajectory = serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(path).unwrap()).unwrap();
11600        assert_eq!(
11601            trajectory.steps[1].message,
11602            Value::String("héllo".to_owned()),
11603            "the audit trail must carry the reassembled multi-byte content"
11604        );
11605        provider.abort();
11606    }

11611    /// and must not be attested as a complete success — previously it

11613    /// compliance reviewer could not distinguish a truncated
11614    /// response from a finished one.

11626                }),
11627            ))
11628            .await
11629            .unwrap();

11631        // an audit classification, not a client-facing refusal.

11633            .await

11643        });

11645            truncated,

11655    /// A provider-side mid-stream cut (TCP RST / stream error) is a
11656    /// FAILED turn attested `StopReason::Other` — never `BudgetExceeded`.
11657    /// Verified live before the fix: a socket-level RST after two SSE
11658    /// deltas journalled `stop_reason_id: 92` ("Budget Exceeded") on a
11659    /// daemon with no `[budget]` block at all, because the failure arm
11660    /// of `submit_response_capture` hard-coded the enforcement variant
11661    /// for every failure shape. A compliance reviewer reading that
11662    /// record concludes the harness cut the turn off when the provider
11663    /// crashed.
11664    #[tokio::test]
11665    async fn severed_stream_is_attested_other_not_budget_exceeded() {
11666        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
11667        let (state, provider) = test_state(directory.path()).await;
11668        let response = build_router(state.clone())
11669            .oneshot(chat_request_with_payload(
11670                "severed-stream",
11671                json!({
11672                    "model": "severed-stream",
11673                    "stream": true,
11674                    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]
11675                }),
11676            ))
11677            .await
11678            .unwrap();
11679        // The client's copy dies with the cut; the audit side is what
11680        // this test pins.
11681        let _ = axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 64 * 1024).await;
11682        let session = state.sessions.get("severed-stream").unwrap();
11683        session.wait_for_worker_jobs().await;
11684        let records = active_records(directory.path(), &state, "severed-stream");
11685        let stop_reasons: Vec<(u64, Option<String>)> = records
11686            .iter()
11687            .filter_map(|record| {
11688                let id = record.event.get("stop_reason_id").and_then(Value::as_u64)?;
11689                let reason = record
11690                    .event
11691                    .pointer("/payload/reason")
11692                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
11693                    .map(str::to_owned);
11694                Some((id, reason))
11695            })
11696            .collect();
11697        assert!(
11698            stop_reasons.iter().all(|(id, _)| *id != 92),
11699            "a provider cut must never be attested as Budget Exceeded (92); got {stop_reasons:?}"
11700        );
11701        assert!(
11702            stop_reasons
11703                .iter()
11704                .any(|(id, reason)| *id == 99 && reason.as_deref().is_some_and(|r| !r.is_empty())),
11705            "the cut turn must be attested Other (99) with a free-text failure reason; got {stop_reasons:?}"
11706        );
11707        provider.abort();
11708    }

11734    #[tokio::test(flavor = "current_thread")]
11735    async fn completion_budget_store_does_not_block_stream_runtime() {
11736        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
11737        let (mut state, provider) = test_state_with_token_cap(directory.path(), Some(10_000)).await;
11738        let calls = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
11739        state.store = Arc::new(SlowStore {
11740            inner: InMemoryStore::new(),
11741            calls: Arc::clone(&calls),
11742        });
11743        let response = build_router(state)
11744            .oneshot(chat_request("slow-budget"))
11745            .await
11746            .unwrap();
11747        let body = tokio::spawn(async move {
11748            axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 64 * 1024)
11749                .await
11750                .unwrap()
11751        });
11752
11753        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
11754        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
11755        // 250 ms allows for 25× scheduler jitter over the 10 ms timer
11756        // — still catches the ~100 ms `SlowStore` regression that
11757        // motivated this test, but tolerates loaded CI runners where
11758        // a 10 ms tokio timer can drift to 30-80 ms. The class the
11759        // test catches (a synchronous blocking dependency stalling
11760        // the reactor) shows up as SECONDS of delay, not tens of ms.
11761        assert!(
11762            started.elapsed() < Duration::from_millis(250),
11763            "completion budget storage blocked the Tokio reactor"
11764        );
11765        assert!(!body.await.unwrap().is_empty());
11766        assert_eq!(calls.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire), 2);
11767        provider.abort();
11768    }

11778        // The completion-side budget refusal severs the body mid-stream.
11779        assert!(axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 64 * 1024)
11780            .await
11781            .is_err());
11782        // A budget-refused turn is recorded as a failed
11783        // response capture but must NOT seal or force-close the
11784        // session — per-minute windows refill, and the client's next
11785        // turn under the same id must be admissible. The idle sweeper
11786        // owns eventual finalization.
11787        let session = state.sessions.get("completion-budget").unwrap();
11788        session.wait_for_streams().await;
11789        assert!(
11790            !session.capture_failed(),
11791            "budget refusal must be scoped to the response, not the session"
11792        );
11793        assert!(
11794            !session.is_closed(),
11795            "budget refusal must not force-close the conversation"
11796        );
11797        provider.abort();
11798    }
11799
11800    /// Regression lock for the upstream-response header forwarding
11801    /// trust-boundary bug (CWE-346 / CWE-16). Before the fix, every
11802    /// upstream response header except `Content-Length` was blindly
11803    /// forwarded to the client — letting a hostile or MITM'd upstream
11804    ///
11805    /// - set cookies on our domain (`Set-Cookie`),
11806    /// - open CORS on our origin (`Access-Control-Allow-*`),
11807    /// - leak upstream implementation identity (`Server`, `Via`,
11808    ///   `X-Powered-By`, `X-Request-ID`),
11809    /// - inject conflicting framing/hop-by-hop metadata (`Connection`,
11810    ///   `Transfer-Encoding`, `Keep-Alive`, `Upgrade`, `TE`, `Trailer`,
11811    ///   `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Authorization`).
11812    ///
11813    /// `is_forwardable_upstream_header` is now the sole gate on which
11814    /// upstream headers cross the proxy trust boundary — this test locks
11815    /// each dangerous class out and confirms benign headers (`Content-Type`,
11816    /// `Cache-Control`, `ETag`) still pass through.
11817    #[test]
11818    fn upstream_response_headers_do_not_cross_proxy_trust_boundary() {
11819        use axum::http::HeaderName;
11820        // Also include every well-known API-key header
11821        // name and both directions of the configured upstream_auth_header
11822        // check. `authorization` is the runtime default.
11823        let dangerous = [
11824            "set-cookie",
11825            "access-control-allow-origin",
11826            "access-control-allow-credentials",
11827            "access-control-allow-methods",
11828            "access-control-allow-headers",
11829            "access-control-expose-headers",
11830            "access-control-max-age",
11831            "connection",
11832            "keep-alive",
11833            "transfer-encoding",
11834            "upgrade",
11835            "te",
11836            "trailer",
11837            "proxy-authenticate",
11838            "proxy-authorization",
11839            "content-length",
11840            "server",
11841            "via",
11842            "x-powered-by",
11843            "x-request-id",
11844            // Provider API-key headers must never echo
11845            // back from an upstream — they carry the operator's
11846            // outbound credential.
11847            "authorization",
11848            "api-key",
11849            "x-api-key",
11850            "x-goog-api-key",
11851            "anthropic-api-key",
11852            "openai-api-key",
11853            "x-auth-token",
11854            "x-amz-security-token",
11855        ];
11856        for name in dangerous {
11857            let header = HeaderName::from_static(name);
11858            assert!(
11859                !is_forwardable_upstream_header(&header, "authorization"),
11860                "dangerous header {name:?} must not be forwarded to the client"
11861            );
11862        }
11863
11864        // The currently-configured upstream_auth_header
11865        // MUST be refused even for operator-picked odd names. Simulate
11866        // an operator using an exotic header (e.g. `x-my-secret`).
11867        let exotic = HeaderName::from_static("x-my-secret");
11868        assert!(
11869            !is_forwardable_upstream_header(&exotic, "x-my-secret"),
11870            "operator-configured upstream_auth_header must be refused",
11871        );
11872
11873        let benign = [
11874            "content-type",
11875            "content-encoding",
11876            "cache-control",
11877            "etag",
11878            "last-modified",
11879            "vary",
11880            "expires",
11881        ];
11882        for name in benign {
11883            let header = HeaderName::from_static(name);
11884            assert!(
11885                is_forwardable_upstream_header(&header, "authorization"),
11886                "benign header {name:?} must still be forwarded"
11887            );
11888        }
11889    }

11891    /// Regression lock for CWE-209 information exposure on the MCP
11892    /// tool-call path — the second occurrence of pass 17's chat/completion
11893    /// leak. Before this fix, when the tool-upstream request failed
11894    /// (unroutable host, timeout, TLS error, …) `mcp_call` returned
11895    /// `lifecycle_error(format!("forward tool call: {reqwest_err}"))`
11896    /// which — because `reqwest::Error::Display` embeds the request URL —
11897    /// leaked the operator-configured tool-upstream URL (potentially an
11898    /// internal hostname) to any client that could hit `/mcp`. The
11899    /// `read_limited_tool_response` mid-stream error path had the same
11900    /// bug. The client-facing message must now be a stable, non-identifying
11901    /// category (e.g. `"upstream unreachable"`), matching pass 17's
11902    /// classifier categories.
11903    #[tokio::test]
11904    async fn mcp_tool_upstream_failure_does_not_leak_configured_url() {
11905        // Distinctive sentinel host so any regression is unmissable.
11906        let sentinel_host = "internal-mcp-sentinel-host.corp.example";
11907        let sentinel_url = format!("http://{sentinel_host}:65002/mcp");
11908        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
11909        let (mut state, provider) = test_state(directory.path()).await;
11910        Arc::get_mut(&mut state.config).unwrap().tool_upstream_url = Some(sentinel_url);
11911        let response = build_router(state)
11912            .oneshot(
11913                Request::builder()
11914                    .method("POST")
11915                    .uri("/v1/mcp")
11916                    .header("x-pv-session", "mcp-cwe-209-check")
11917                    .body(Body::from(
11918                        r#"{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"leak","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read","arguments":{}}}"#,
11919                    ))
11920                    .unwrap(),
11921            )
11922            .await
11923            .unwrap();
11924        assert_eq!(
11925            response.status(),
11926            StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
11927            "tool-upstream faults must surface as 502 like the chat relay, not 500"
11928        );
11929        let bytes = axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 64 * 1024)
11930            .await
11931            .unwrap();
11932        let body = String::from_utf8(bytes.to_vec()).unwrap();
11933        assert!(
11934            !body.contains(sentinel_host),
11935            "MCP forward-tool error body {body:?} leaks the configured tool-upstream host"
11936        );
11937        assert!(
11938            !body.contains("65002"),
11939            "MCP forward-tool error body {body:?} leaks the configured tool-upstream port"
11940        );
11941        assert!(
11942            !body.contains("corp.example"),
11943            "MCP forward-tool error body {body:?} leaks the configured tool-upstream domain"
11944        );
11945        provider.abort();
11946    }

11948    #[tokio::test]
11949    async fn pipeline_error_carries_retry_after_and_www_authenticate() {
11950        // Contract: 503 SHOULD carry Retry-After (RFC 7231 §7.1.3);
11951        // 401 MUST carry WWW-Authenticate (RFC 7235 §3.1). These
11952        // headers are the mechanism by which intermediaries and SDKs
11953        // decide to back off / prompt for credentials — without them,
11954        // mainstream LLM SDKs interpret 503 as "retry immediately"
11955        // and 401 as "broken proxy".
11956        use crate::pipeline::PipelineError;
11957
11958        let unavailable = pipeline_error(PipelineError::unavailable("worker queue full"));
11959        assert_eq!(unavailable.status(), StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE);
11960        assert_eq!(
11961            unavailable
11962                .headers()
11963                .get(axum::http::header::RETRY_AFTER)
11964                .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()),
11965            Some("5")
11966        );
11967
11968        let upstream = pipeline_error(PipelineError::upstream("bad gateway"));
11969        assert_eq!(upstream.status(), StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY);
11970        assert!(upstream.headers().get(axum::http::header::RETRY_AFTER).is_some());
11971
11972        let unauthorized = pipeline_error(PipelineError::Unauthorized("bad token".into()));
11973        assert_eq!(unauthorized.status(), StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
11974        let auth = unauthorized
11975            .headers()
11976            .get(axum::http::header::WWW_AUTHENTICATE)
11977            .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
11978            .unwrap_or_default();
11979        assert!(
11980            auth.starts_with("Bearer"),
11981            "WWW-Authenticate must be a Bearer challenge, got {auth:?}"
11982        );
11983
11984        // Permanent verdicts must NOT carry Retry-After — that would
11985        // encourage the very retry loop we're trying to stop.
11986        let blocked = pipeline_error(PipelineError::blocked("loop breaker"));
11987        assert_eq!(blocked.status(), StatusCode::FORBIDDEN);
11988        assert!(blocked.headers().get(axum::http::header::RETRY_AFTER).is_none());
11989        let abort = pipeline_error(PipelineError::Abort("stop retrying".into()));
11990        assert_eq!(abort.status(), StatusCode::CONFLICT);
11991        assert!(abort.headers().get(axum::http::header::RETRY_AFTER).is_none());
11992    }

11994    /// SSE detection is case-insensitive and tolerates
11995    /// media-type parameters. Byte-exact `starts_with` previously
11996    /// misclassified `Text/Event-Stream` (some CDNs re-title-case)
11997    /// and any `text/event-stream; charset=utf-8` with a leading
11998    /// title-cased subtype. Misclassified SSE streams get buffered
11999    /// to the 16 MiB provider cap and either lose streaming
12000    /// semantics or 502 despite being valid.
12001    #[test]
12002    fn is_sse_content_type_is_case_insensitive_and_param_tolerant() {
12003        fn ct(value: &str) -> HeaderMap {
12004            let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
12005            headers.insert(
12006                axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE,
12007                value.parse().expect("header value"),
12008            );
12009            headers
12010        }
12011        assert!(is_sse_content_type(&ct("text/event-stream")));
12012        assert!(is_sse_content_type(&ct("Text/Event-Stream")));
12013        assert!(is_sse_content_type(&ct("TEXT/EVENT-STREAM")));
12014        assert!(is_sse_content_type(&ct("text/event-stream; charset=utf-8")));
12015        assert!(is_sse_content_type(&ct("Text/Event-Stream ; charset=utf-8")));
12016        // Non-SSE and superstring both must not match.
12017        assert!(!is_sse_content_type(&ct("application/json")));
12018        assert!(!is_sse_content_type(&ct("text/event-stream-json")));
12019        // Absent header returns false.
12020        assert!(!is_sse_content_type(&HeaderMap::new()));
12021    }

12023    /// OPTIONS to every mutating route replies with
12024    /// `204 No Content` and NO Access-Control-Allow-* headers.
12025    /// Browsers must interpret this as "cross-origin denied" and
12026    /// refuse the actual request — making the same-origin-only
12027    /// posture explicit at the wire. Guards against a future PR
12028    /// accidentally adding `CorsLayer::permissive()`.
12029    #[tokio::test]
12030    async fn options_returns_204_without_cors_headers() {
12031        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
12032        let (state, provider) = test_state(directory.path()).await;
12033        for path in [
12034            "/v1/chat/completions",
12035            "/v1/mcp",
12036            "/mcp",
12037            "/v1/sessions/some-id/close",
12038            "/v1/sessions/some-id/promote",
12039        ] {
12040            let response = build_router(state.clone())
12041                .oneshot(
12042                    Request::builder()
12043                        .method(axum::http::Method::OPTIONS)
12044                        .uri(path)
12045                        .header("origin", "http://attacker.example")
12046                        .header("access-control-request-method", "POST")
12047                        .body(Body::empty())
12048                        .unwrap(),
12049                )
12050                .await
12051                .unwrap();
12052            assert_eq!(
12053                response.status(),
12054                StatusCode::NO_CONTENT,
12055                "OPTIONS {path} should return 204, got {}",
12056                response.status()
12057            );
12058            for header in [
12059                "access-control-allow-origin",
12060                "access-control-allow-methods",
12061                "access-control-allow-headers",
12062                "access-control-allow-credentials",
12063            ] {
12064                assert!(
12065                    response.headers().get(header).is_none(),

12067                    response.headers().get(header)

12074    /// Cached MCP tool-outcome replays preserve the
12075    /// upstream Content-Type end-to-end (including through the
12076    /// on-disk journal roundtrip). Strict JSON-RPC 2.0 clients
12077    /// (spec: MUST be `application/json`) would previously receive
12078    /// `application/octet-stream` on both the fresh forward and the
12079    /// cached replay. This test locks in:
12080    ///   1. `ToolOutcome::into_response` honours a set content_type.
12081    ///   2. A `None` content_type defaults to `application/json`
12082    ///      (MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0 by convention).
12083    ///   3. Serialising and re-deserialising a `ToolOutcome` (i.e.
12084    ///      the on-disk journal round-trip) preserves the field.
12085    ///   4. Legacy journals without the field decode as `None` and
12086    ///      pick up the default via #1.
12087    #[test]
12088    fn round_32_f2_tool_outcome_preserves_content_type() {
12089        // (1) Custom content_type survives.
12090        let outcome = ToolOutcome {
12091            status: 200,
12092            body_hex: hex::encode(b"{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\"}"),
12093            content_type: Some("application/problem+json".to_owned()),
12094        };
12095        let response = outcome.into_response();
12096        assert_eq!(
12097            response
12098                .headers()
12099                .get(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE)
12100                .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()),
12101            Some("application/problem+json")
12102        );
12103        // (2) None -> application/json default.
12104        let outcome_no_ct = ToolOutcome {
12105            status: 200,
12106            body_hex: hex::encode(b"{}"),
12107            content_type: None,
12108        };
12109        let response = outcome_no_ct.into_response();
12110        assert_eq!(
12111            response
12112                .headers()
12113                .get(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE)
12114                .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()),
12115            Some("application/json")
12116        );
12117        // (3) Journal round-trip preserves the field.
12118        let sealed = serde_json::to_string(&ToolOutcome {
12119            status: 429,
12120            body_hex: hex::encode(b"{}"),
12121            content_type: Some("text/plain".to_owned()),
12122        })
12123        .unwrap();
12124        let recovered: ToolOutcome = serde_json::from_str(&sealed).unwrap();
12125        assert_eq!(recovered.content_type.as_deref(), Some("text/plain"));
12126        // (4) Legacy journal without the field decodes as None.
12127        let legacy = r#"{"status":200,"body_hex":"7b7d"}"#;
12128        let outcome: ToolOutcome = serde_json::from_str(legacy).unwrap();
12129        assert!(outcome.content_type.is_none());
12130    }

12132    /// `/livez` and `/readyz` are the Kubernetes-style split of the
12133    /// legacy `/health` constant. Liveness stays a constant; readiness
12134    /// couples to the draining flag and to a spool WRITABILITY probe
12135    /// so a full, read-only, or missing spool volume immediately
12136    /// steers new traffic elsewhere.
12137    #[tokio::test]
12138    async fn livez_and_readyz_reflect_service_readiness() {
12139        let scratch = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
12140        let spool = scratch.path().join("spool");
12141        std::fs::create_dir_all(&spool).unwrap();
12142        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
12143        let address = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
12144        let provider = Router::new().route("/v1/chat/completions", post(mock_chat));
12145        let _server = tokio::spawn(async move {
12146            axum::serve(listener, provider).await.unwrap();
12147        });
12148        let config = crate::config::HarnessConfig::for_tests(
12149            &format!("http://{address}"),
12150            &spool.to_string_lossy(),
12151            &spool.to_string_lossy(),
12152        );
12153        let state = AppState::new(
12154            config,
12155            Arc::new(InMemoryStore::new()),
12156            Arc::new(Sandbox::new(SandboxConfig::default(), Vec::new()).unwrap()),
12157            Arc::new(NullBus),
12158            None,
12159            Arc::new(Ed25519Signer::from_seed(&[19; 32])),
12160        )
12161        .unwrap();
12162        let app = crate::build_router(state.clone());
12163
12164        // /livez must always respond 200 with a constant body — it is
12165        // decoupled from backend health by design.
12166        let live = app
12167            .clone()
12168            .oneshot(Request::builder().uri("/livez").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
12169            .await
12170            .unwrap();
12171        assert_eq!(live.status(), StatusCode::OK);
12172
12173        // /readyz on a healthy pod: spool exists, not draining → 200.
12174        let ready = app
12175            .clone()
12176            .oneshot(Request::builder().uri("/readyz").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
12177            .await
12178            .unwrap();
12179        assert_eq!(ready.status(), StatusCode::OK);
12180
12181        // Draining flag flipped: /readyz must return 503 immediately.
12182        state.draining.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
12183        let not_ready = app
12184            .clone()
12185            .oneshot(Request::builder().uri("/readyz").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
12186            .await
12187            .unwrap();
12188        assert_eq!(not_ready.status(), StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE);
12189
12190        // /livez remains 200 while draining — restart-cascade guard.
12191        let still_live = app
12192            .clone()
12193            .oneshot(Request::builder().uri("/livez").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
12194            .await
12195            .unwrap();
12196        assert_eq!(still_live.status(), StatusCode::OK);
12197    }

12199    /// The register's observed outage: a FULL DISK keeps the spool
12200    /// directory readable, so the previous `is_dir()` readiness check
12201    /// passed while every request 503'd on write — the pod stayed
12202    /// Ready, in-service, un-restarted through the whole incident.
12203    /// `/readyz` must probe WRITABILITY. A read-only spool (the
12204    /// closest deterministic stand-in for ENOSPC — both fail the
12205    /// probe-file create) must flip readiness to 503, and restoring
12206    /// write permission must restore 200 with no restart.
12207    #[cfg(unix)]
12208    #[tokio::test]
12209    async fn readyz_fails_when_the_spool_is_not_writable() {
12210        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt as _;
12211        let scratch = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
12212        let spool = scratch.path().join("spool");
12213        std::fs::create_dir_all(&spool).unwrap();
12214        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
12215        let address = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
12216        let provider = Router::new().route("/v1/chat/completions", post(mock_chat));
12217        let _server = tokio::spawn(async move {
12218            axum::serve(listener, provider).await.unwrap();
12219        });
12220        let config = crate::config::HarnessConfig::for_tests(
12221            &format!("http://{address}"),
12222            &spool.to_string_lossy(),
12223            &spool.to_string_lossy(),
12224        );
12225        let state = AppState::new(
12226            config,
12227            Arc::new(InMemoryStore::new()),
12228            Arc::new(Sandbox::new(SandboxConfig::default(), Vec::new()).unwrap()),
12229            Arc::new(NullBus),
12230            None,
12231            Arc::new(Ed25519Signer::from_seed(&[23; 32])),
12232        )
12233        .unwrap();
12234        let app = crate::build_router(state);
12235
12236        // Read-only spool: directory still readable, probe write fails.
12237        std::fs::set_permissions(&spool, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o555)).unwrap();
12238        if std::fs::write(spool.join("root-probe"), b"x").is_ok() {
12239            // Running as root (CI container): the premise doesn't hold.
12240            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(spool.join("root-probe"));
12241            std::fs::set_permissions(&spool, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).unwrap();
12242            return;
12243        }
12244        let not_ready = app
12245            .clone()
12246            .oneshot(Request::builder().uri("/readyz").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
12247            .await
12248            .unwrap();
12249        assert_eq!(
12250            not_ready.status(),
12251            StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
12252            "an unwritable (readable) spool must flip readiness — the full-disk incident shape"
12253        );
12254
12255        // Restore write permission: readiness recovers without restart.
12256        std::fs::set_permissions(&spool, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).unwrap();
12257        let ready = app
12258            .clone()
12259            .oneshot(Request::builder().uri("/readyz").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
12260            .await
12261            .unwrap();
12262        assert_eq!(ready.status(), StatusCode::OK);
12263        // The probe cleans up after itself: no .readyz-*.tmp residue.
12264        let residue = std::fs::read_dir(&spool)
12265            .unwrap()
12266            .filter_map(Result::ok)
12267            .any(|entry| {
12268                entry
12269                    .file_name()
12270                    .to_str()
12271                    .is_some_and(|name| name.starts_with(".readyz-"))
12272            });
12273        assert!(!residue, "probe files must not accumulate in the spool");
12274    }

12276    /// DNS-rebinding defense: a non-empty `allowed_hosts` must
12277    /// refuse a Host header outside the list with 403 before any
12278    /// handler runs, accept listed hosts (with or without a port,
12279    /// case-insensitively, IPv6 brackets included), and refuse an
12280    /// absent Host. Empty list = check disabled (loopback/ingress
12281    /// deployments).
12282    #[tokio::test]
12283    async fn allowed_hosts_refuses_rebound_host_headers() {
12284        let scratch = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
12285        let spool = scratch.path().join("spool");
12286        std::fs::create_dir_all(&spool).unwrap();
12287        let mut config = crate::config::HarnessConfig::for_tests(
12288            "http://127.0.0.1:9",
12289            &spool.to_string_lossy(),
12290            &spool.to_string_lossy(),
12291        );
12292        config.allowed_hosts = vec!["localhost".to_owned(), "[::1]".to_owned()];
12293        let state = AppState::new(
12294            config,
12295            Arc::new(InMemoryStore::new()),
12296            Arc::new(Sandbox::new(SandboxConfig::default(), Vec::new()).unwrap()),
12297            Arc::new(NullBus),
12298            None,
12299            Arc::new(Ed25519Signer::from_seed(&[23; 32])),
12300        )
12301        .unwrap();
12302        let app = crate::build_router(state);
12303
12304        let probe = |host: Option<&'static str>| {
12305            let mut builder = Request::builder().uri("/health");
12306            if let Some(host) = host {
12307                builder = builder.header("host", host);
12308            }
12309            builder.body(Body::empty()).unwrap()
12310        };
12311
12312        // Listed host, with port, mixed case, IPv6 bracket form: allowed.
12313        for host in ["localhost", "localhost:8484", "LOCALHOST", "[::1]:8484"] {
12314            let response = app.clone().oneshot(probe(Some(host))).await.unwrap();
12315            assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::OK, "host {host:?} must be allowed");
12316        }
12317        // Rebound / unlisted host and absent host: refused.
12318        for host in [
12319            Some("evil.attacker.example"),
12320            Some("localhost.attacker.example"),
12321            None,
12322        ] {
12323            let response = app.clone().oneshot(probe(host)).await.unwrap();
12324            assert_eq!(
12325                response.status(),
12326                StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,
12327                "host {host:?} must be refused"
12328            );
12329        }
12330    }
12331
12332    /// A `/metrics` scrape must emit both a live
12333    /// `pv_open_sessions` gauge (sampled at scrape time from the
12334    /// registry) and a labelled `pv_signing_key_info` gauge whose
12335    /// value is 1 whenever the process holds the signer.
12336    #[tokio::test]
12337    async fn metrics_scrape_emits_open_sessions_gauge_and_signing_key_info() {
12338        let scratch = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
12339        let spool = scratch.path().join("spool");
12340        std::fs::create_dir_all(&spool).unwrap();
12341        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
12342        let address = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
12343        let provider = Router::new().route("/v1/chat/completions", post(mock_chat));
12344        let _server = tokio::spawn(async move {
12345            axum::serve(listener, provider).await.unwrap();
12346        });
12347        let config = crate::config::HarnessConfig::for_tests(
12348            &format!("http://{address}"),
12349            &spool.to_string_lossy(),
12350            &spool.to_string_lossy(),
12351        );
12352        let signer = Ed25519Signer::from_seed(&[31; 32]);
12353        use pv_receipts::Signer as _;
12354        let key_id = signer.key_id().to_owned();
12355        let public_key_hex = hex::encode(signer.public_key_bytes());
12356        let state = AppState::new(
12357            config,
12358            Arc::new(InMemoryStore::new()),
12359            Arc::new(Sandbox::new(SandboxConfig::default(), Vec::new()).unwrap()),
12360            Arc::new(NullBus),
12361            None,
12362            Arc::new(signer),
12363        )
12364        .unwrap();
12365        // Mirror main.rs's startup registration so the gauge is
12366        // reachable from the same route.
12367        state
12368            .metrics
12369            .gauge(
12370                &format!("pv_signing_key_info{{key_id=\"{key_id}\",public_key_hex=\"{public_key_hex}\"}}"),
12371                "test signing key info",
12372            )
12373            .set(1);
12374        let app = crate::build_router(state.clone());
12375
12376        // Scrape with an empty registry — gauge sample must be 0.
12377        let response = app
12378            .clone()
12379            .oneshot(Request::builder().uri("/metrics").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
12380            .await
12381            .unwrap();
12382        let body = String::from_utf8_lossy(
12383            &axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 256 * 1024)
12384                .await
12385                .unwrap(),
12386        )
12387        .into_owned();
12388        assert!(body.contains("# TYPE pv_open_sessions gauge"), "{body}");
12389        assert!(body.contains("pv_open_sessions 0"), "{body}");
12390        // data-plane series must exist from boot.
12391        assert!(body.contains("# TYPE pv_worker_queue_depth gauge"), "{body}");
12392        assert!(body.contains("# TYPE pv_spool_bytes gauge"), "{body}");
12393        assert!(body.contains("# TYPE pv_requests_total counter"), "{body}");
12394        assert!(
12395            body.contains("pv_requests_total{route=\"chat\",status_class=\"2xx\"}"),
12396            "{body}"
12397        );
12398        assert!(
12399            body.contains("pv_upstream_errors_total{kind=\"timeout\"}"),
12400            "{body}"
12401        );
12402        assert!(body.contains("pv_upstream_latency_seconds"), "{body}");
12403        assert!(
12404            body.contains(&format!("pv_signing_key_info{{key_id=\"{key_id}\"")),
12405            "signing-key info gauge missing from scrape: {body}"
12406        );
12407
12408        // Register a session and scrape again — gauge must reflect 1.
12409        state.sessions.insert_recovered(crate::session::Session::new(
12410            "gauge-test".to_owned(),
12411            crate::session::Workflow::Unsigned,
12412            pv_events::AgentIdentity {
12413                version: "1".to_owned(),
12414                charter: "test".into(),
12415                instance_uid: "instance-1".to_owned(),
12416                ttl_remaining_s: Some(600),
12417            },
12418            Default::default(),
12419        ));
12420        let response = app
12421            .clone()
12422            .oneshot(Request::builder().uri("/metrics").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
12423            .await
12424            .unwrap();
12425        let body = String::from_utf8_lossy(
12426            &axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), 256 * 1024)
12427                .await
12428                .unwrap(),
12429        )
12430        .into_owned();
12431        assert!(body.contains("pv_open_sessions 1"), "{body}");
12432    }

12434    /// R49 review-of-R48: the stable client-facing error message
12435    /// for a corrupt cached tool outcome must not regress. R48 fixed
12436    /// `ToolOutcome::into_response` but missed the sibling
12437    /// `complete_tool_audit` decode site. Both are now routed through
12438    /// `decode_cached_tool_body`; a future refactor that reintroduces
12439    /// `format!("...{error}...")` on either branch would leak
12440    /// `hex::FromHexError` Display detail (offending byte offset +
12441    /// character) into the 500 body. Pin the stable message so the
12442    /// leak-free contract survives.
12443    #[tokio::test]
12444    async fn decode_cached_tool_body_returns_stable_error_message() {
12445        let helper_err = decode_cached_tool_body("zz").expect_err("`zz` must not hex-decode");
12446        let body = String::from_utf8(
12447            axum::body::to_bytes((*helper_err).into_body(), 16 * 1024)
12448                .await
12449                .unwrap()
12450                .to_vec(),
12451        )
12452        .expect("lifecycle_error body is UTF-8");
12453        assert!(
12454            body.contains("cached tool outcome is corrupt"),
12455            "leak-free stable error message expected in body: {body}"
12456        );
12457        // Must NOT contain the raw `hex::FromHexError` Display
12458        // fingerprints — byte offset ("at 0") or the offending
12459        // character (`z`).
12460        assert!(
12461            !body.contains("at 0"),
12462            "hex::FromHexError position must not leak: {body}"
12463        );
12464        // The `into_response` path must produce the same stable
12465        // body: prove both consumers share the helper.
12466        let outcome_response = ToolOutcome {
12467            status: 200,
12468            body_hex: "zz".to_owned(),
12469            content_type: None,
12470        }
12471        .into_response();
12472        let outcome_body = String::from_utf8(
12473            axum::body::to_bytes(outcome_response.into_body(), 16 * 1024)
12474                .await
12475                .unwrap()
12476                .to_vec(),
12477        )
12478        .expect("into_response body is UTF-8");
12479        assert!(
12480            outcome_body.contains("cached tool outcome is corrupt"),
12481            "ToolOutcome::into_response must route through the shared helper: {outcome_body}"
12482        );
12483    }
12484}
